1667.d: This belt takes its name from its creator, a shoemaker who was less renowned and much older than Bowisse, but quite gifted all the same.

1668.d: The Dodu was a Sadida who loved frightening his enemies. He asked Bowisse to make him a belt that matched the colour of his hair... Like many charmers, the Dodu had a rotten heart.

1669.d: This belt was made for the most popular of all the Craettes who often organised parties and wacky events to keep her countless friends and acquaintances on her side. All this between ironing and washing Captain Chafer's leather underpants.

1670.d: A Wind Kwak can sometimes have a pointed feather different from the others. As a rule, it's magic, but you can nevertheless put it on and then be dressed up as an Indian Chief.

1671.d: This wisp of magic oat straw once belonged to a simple peasant. The poor country fellow was bewitched by a Bwork Magus apprentice, who read his book upside down by mistake.

1672.d: These hairs used to belong to Darit, a young, pretentious wizard who unwisely underestimated his opponent. He forgot to check if  the Prespic had cast a Counter spell before casting 'Ripping Lightning'.

1673.d: This Arachnee Leg is different from the rest - it moves on its own and seems to be well and truly alive, even when amputated from its owner. It could be on the point of starting a family since apparently it is attracted to sewing tools.

1674.d: This great hero was turned into a mushroom thanks to the bumbling magic of the mischievous Soft Oak. Being complete cretins, the Mush-Mush venerate and protect him as one of their gods.

1675.d: This magic Bone allows the Chafer Foot Soldiers to achieve astonishing feats. For instance, while in the middle of a fight, they can take off their briefs, put them on their heads without using their hands, and still avoid being hit by attackers. You will never get never tired of this incredible performance.

1676.d: This piece of Bewitched Wicker will enable you to make a beautiful basket for magic fruits, combining elegance and power... quite the opposite of a bad Liche.

1677.d: This magic potion is the only one that can cast magic into the lattice-work leather panties of Captain Chafer...It speaks volumes about the power of such a potion.

1678.d: This Kokonut was traumatised as a child, and so, over the years, has accumulated an incredible amount of hatred. This hatred has rendered it a very powerful Kokonut indeed.

1679.d: It takes the patience of a saint but this stone can become round and bright like the pompom on a magic hat. Its shape makes it easy to fit almost anywhere.

1680.d: A very powerful incantation has scorched this Minotoror Horn, which makes it a much sought-after magical artefact. Unfortunately, like many things, they only work correctly in pairs...

1681.d: Beneath the slimy exterior, a very precious artefact lies. It will bring you the luck of the devil himself, provided you wear it round your head... You'll have the temper of a devil too with this wet rag clinging to your skull.

1682.d:
This fragment of bark comes from a tree in the enchanted clearing of Liroye Merline. 
This fragment fell down when Brouce Boulgoure the lumberjack broke his Boulgourde against one of the enchanted trees.

1683.d: An artful Sadida carried incredible quantities of peeled potatoes in this sack and then sold them to prisoners. When he died, his bag passed down from artful Sadida to artful Sadida as a family ritual.

1684.d: The Dark Bag of Spuds is identical to the Bright Bag of Spuds apart from the fact that it has been dipped in some Dark Treechnid sap, thus conferring still more powers upon it.

1685.d: Beware! You are now the unhappy owner of the last feather from the rump of the last Cheeken in Amakna. It might be a good idea to give it away to a Tailor friend... or a Cheeken fanatic. There's a lot of them around lately.

1686.d: This small magic potion gives hair a magnificent red colour. Secondarily, it seems to have some magic effects.

1687.d: This small magic potion gives hair a magnificent bluish effect. Oh, and it seems to have few magical powers.

1688.d: This small magic potion gives hair a magnificent bluish effect. Oh, and it seems to have few magical powers.

1689.d: This small magic potion gives a magnificent auburn glow when applied to any kind of hair. Oh, and it seems to have few magical powers as well.

1690.d:
This fur is quite the same as the Boowolf's only a little shorter, less robust and softer.  
Unfortunately, it smells the same.

1691.d:
Rare are the adventurers who have touched these living hairs. 
Something, something, something, I like eating choc eclairs.

1692.d: This small magic potion gives hair a magnificent bluish effect. Oh, and it seems to have few magical powers.

1693.d: The famous tailor, Jules Yanos, was particularly renowned for having exchanged his wife for a magic thimble. What a businessman, hmm? Just great!

1694.d: This piece of Wool comes from the most dangerous Trool of Amakna who, apparently, has been transformed into a bedspread by an unscrupulous tailor, the same tailor who, if you believe what is publicly rumoured, has once exchanged his wife for a magic thimble. I don't see the connection.

1695.d: Some say Captain Chafer tried to steal this cloak to replace his famous leather panties. But it didn't suit him at all - it just wasn't perverse enough.

1696.d: Many years ago, tailors created a simple system for determining the value of a material - the worse it smells, the better it is.

1697.d: Don't expect this bag to make a hero of you. It will keep all your personal items in one place. Better than nothing, I suppose.

1698.d:
This bag has been designed to hold a few collectible resources. 
Only true harvesters can carry it.

1699.d: This bag is ideal for those who never wander far from home but take useless things with them when they do. Like ash planks for example.

1700.d: Designed by Tengra Reufrus, this aerodynamic belt will make you as nimble as a Tofu and as windy as the breeze. Or is it the opposite?

1701.d: This belt has small pockets allowing you to stock more items in your inventory.

1702.d:
This bag has been designed to hold collectible resources. 
Only true harvesters can carry it.

1703.d:
This bag has been designed to hold many collectible resources. 
Only true harvesters can carry it.

1704.d: Legend whispers of a miner who worked continuously for several months in 4 different mines simultaneously, raising a family in the process and running a successful one-man printing press with his feet... The Hammer-Sickle newspaper hard at work again...

1705.d: It's the ideal bag for holding all your bread and potions when you go away for several months... into the labyrinth for example.

1707.d: It's the ideal bag to keep all your bread and potions when you are on an exotic vacation...like in the Moon Island.

1709.d: "Say hello to my little friend"... the last words of a proud female Enutrof who mistook a Boowolf for her trusty poodle.

1710.d: No one knows the origins of this crescent-shaped amulet. Well, almost no one. Who knows what might happen if you put it on...

1711.d:
Take this dog to the park, take him to the toilet, show him to your friends, but whatever you do - and please listen carefully - do not feed him. This pet will remove your arm up to the elbow. 
(THIS PET DOESN'T LIKE ANY RESOURCES)

1712.d: You'll recover between 201 and 400 energy points using this potion.

1713.d: You'll recover between 501 and 1000 energy points using this potion.

1715.d: Christmas Bestseller 634. This is essential reading. It's a classic!

1716.d: Other bestseller of the Winter 634, this book is already a reference.

1717.d: The odds-on outsider for the beginning of 635, this book has gained a cult following in recent months.

1718.d: The powers given to this ring by the Dark Breath of Grougalorasalar are now considerably weakened. This relic was intended for Crocoburio, the only one capable of mastering it without being dominated himself.

1719.d: This pair of boots apparently belonged to Crocoburio. Only a few people can put them on and they are immediately plunged into a clever, Machiavellian frame of mind. Legend has it that this evil spell is due to the numerous skulls the boots have crushed.

1720.d: Grougalorasalar loved collecting the bone fragments of his most fearsome enemies. His affection for Crocoburio inspired the creation of this ultra-powerful belt.

1721.d: Using this potion will cause you to unlearn one level of the Xelor spell 'Clock'.

1722.d: You've been turned into a Treechnid because of the Soft Oak's curse. To remove the bewitchment, you have to defeat an adventurer lost in the forest of Treechnids.

1723.d: This drop increases your energy for a short time.

1724.d: This blessing will increase Strength for your next few fights.

1725.d: This curse will reduce your Strength in your next fight.

1726.d: This tuft of hair proves your victory against Tarche. You're a star!

1727.d: A threatening letter addressed to Lady Marmalade.

1728.d: The fairer sex of the fairest class will fall under the spell of this cuddly little ball of fluff. For this reason alone it's to be avoided.

1729.d: This ring once belonged to Mer, the laziest piece of stuff in Amakna. He worshipped doughnuts and ribs...

1730.d: This salt measure is the ideal quantity to season most family dishes. No meal can be cooked without it.

1731.d: A dose of tasty juice, sometimes known as chef's special sauce, will make a fine, rustic, slightly salty broth.

1732.d: There's nothing more convenient than a bowl to eat your soup properly, even if the fact of eating properly doesn't alter the taste. Unless your fingers are really dirty...

1733.d:
Terrine is like meat... Oooo, that hits the spot. Three cheers for the terrine! Hurrah for the terrine!!! 
Go terrine, it's your birthday. 
Go terrine, it's your birthday. 
(Extract from the butcher anthem, verse 4)

1734.d: Xelors often mistake this fruit for a space hopper. Remember them!

1735.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Bow Meow you've put in the Bow Kennels.

1736.d: This juice of this fruit is perfect for hiding the foul smell of rotting flesh. A must-have if you're serving leftovers to your guests.

1737.d: This Field Bread feels like a stone in your pocket, and in your belly for that matter. But it has at that familiar rustic flavour that any good bread should have.

1738.d: This bread will give you the appetite of a bulimic giant. It'll also fill you very, very quickly. These conflicting properties have killed thousands. Don't be next.

1739.d: This wand is searingly hot to the touch. But the most enigmatic thing about it is its ash smell which would make you think it had survived a forest fire.

1740.d: The Crocobur contains the spirit of Crocoburio. So, the only way of stealing it is to kill Crocoburio. Simple.

1741.d: This phoenix's blood can revive a ghost and give it a few Health Points.

1742.d: This phoenix blood can revive a ghost and give it lots of Health Points.

1744.d: This tuft of hair proves your victory against Torche. Magnificent!

1745.d: One end pointed, a plunger on the other, it's a syringe, no doubt about it... You've been warned.

1746.d: Who would have travelled to Wabbit Island armed with a syringe with the sole aim of extracting some blood from the most genetically modified creature on the island ? You, of course.

1747.d:
Analysis clearly reveal that the blood comes from a Wabbit's hind quarter. After a thorough examination of the sample, the alchemist was able to determine which part of the backside was stung;
            for your information, it was the right cheek.

1748.d: This little Wabbit is domesticated and won't bite you. As for strangers, however...

1749.d: You bought this token from Leonzi Trool. His humble dream is to open the biggest public fair the Cania Plains have ever seen.

1750.d: A cubic fish renowned for its particularly one dimensional thought processes. This piscatorial cretin is exceedingly easy to catch.

1751.d: The breaded fish can now be used as an ingredient.

1752.d: This tasty stick is made from fat-free pieces of cubic fish. Its taste delights children but it has low nutritional value.

1753.d: This very tasty stick is made from decent, fat-free pieces of cubic fish. Its taste delights children and has good nutritional value.

1754.d: This rare species of breaded fish usually lives, as its name indicates, in the icy waters of the far North. Because of its polar diet, its flesh is rich in fibre.

1755.d: This Igloo Fish can now be used as an ingredient.

1756.d: This incredibly tasty stick is made from the best fat-free pieces of cubic fish. Its taste delights children and it has excellent nutritional value.

1757.d: This unusually-shaped crab is much appreciated for the great quantity of flesh it yields. It is also the only crab you can catch with a fishing rod because of its natural instinct to cut thread with its claws... which can't cut a thing!

1758.d: This Surimice Crab can now be used as an ingredient.

1759.d: Although a distant relative of the Crab Stick, this crab has a few brain cells to throw around. This explains its rarity.

1760.d: This Exotic Surimice can now be used as an ingredient.

1761.d: This Kittenfish can now be used as an ingredient.

1762.d: It's the same type of fish as the Kittenfish, just far more dangerous.

1763.d: This tiger fish can now be used as an ingredient.

1764.d: Enjoy it everywhere, but be careful not to eat too much...

1765.d: To be enjoyed slowly, very slowly, with some sauce to bring out the flavour.

1766.d: Made from exotic Surimice Crab meat, this crab stick is simply disgusting... but it's very nutritious.

1767.d: Delicately smoked, this kittenfish makes a marvellous meal. But be careful, its smell will stick to your clothes for several decades.

1768.d: Delicately smoked, this kittenfish makes a marvellous meal. But be careful, its smell will stick to your clothes for several decades.

1769.d: Firmer than smoked kittenfish, and more refined, this smoked tiger fish will delight lovers of fine cuisine.

1770.d: This extract of Blop has a strong smell of coco. How can a monster residue smell like this?

1771.d: A green mouse running across the plains? Whatever you do, don't grab its tail...

1772.d: Say it with Coco Flowers or don't say it at all!

1774.d: Say it with Pippin Flowers or don't say it at all!

1776.d: Say it with Cherry Flowers or don't say it at all!

1778.d: Say it with Indigo Flowers or don't say it at all!

1779.d: You can find this type of fish in glacial lakes and rivers. Fishermen really love it because of its size and its fresh flesh.

1780.d: The Lard Bass can now be used as an ingredient.

1781.d: This Grawn can now be used as an ingredient.

1782.d: A small and fast-moving freshwater fish, the gudgeon is often caught by children and novice fishermen. Don't expect to feed your family with it.

1783.d: This Gudgeon can now be used as an ingredient.

1784.d: The Blue Skate rules the sea bed in which, for some mysterious reason, it digs tiny holes all day long. Every once in a while, it returns to the surface. Sometimes long enough for you to catch it.

1785.d: This Blue Skate can now be used as an ingredient.

1786.d: Transformation of the Grawn. A distinguishing characteristic of this rare species is that it makes nauseating grunting noises when it moves around.

1787.d: This Horror Grawn can now be used as an ingredient.

1788.d: Farle Ingalsse personally discovered this particular species of ray during one of his great adventures. Apparently it has the ability to enchant fish with its deep, southern voice and rhythmic train-like beating of its tail.

1789.d: This Farle's Ray can now be used as an ingredient.

1790.d: This rare species of gudgeon comes from Kiye Island, off Moon Island. Accustomed to warm currents, it migrates once a year to a hotter clime.

1791.d: This Kiye Gudgeon can now be used as an ingredient.

1792.d: A cousin of the Lard Bass, the Siktrin Bass is officially an endangered species. The population was hunted enthusiastically ever since some quack idiot doctor claimed that it improved the singing voice.

1793.d: The Siktrin Bass can now be used as an ingredient.

1794.d: This creature is considered the wisest of all the freshwater fish. It's also surprisingly easy to catch... it's supreme knowledge of all things plunges many of its kind into an mind-numbing depression.

1795.d: This Ediem Carp can now be used as an ingredient.

1796.d: This small carp is sand-coloured, a distinctive feature which in theory should make it invisible to predators. What a pity there's not a grain of sand in the lakes of Amakna...

1797.d: This Small Sandy Carp can now be used as an ingredient.

1798.d: This Kralove can now be used as an ingredient.

1799.d: This Kralove is monogamous. This is surprising when you know its habits.

1800.d: This Unique Kralove can now be used as an ingredient.

1801.d: This fish doesn't look like much but it is the slyest and quickest of its kind. It's worth a try though. Its matchless taste and unique flavour will be ample reward for your efforts.

1802.d: This Perch can now be used as an ingredient.

1803.d: With the hideousness of its father and the savagery of its mother, this fish is the most difficult of all to catch. It's the rarest of its kind, too... Indeed, the mating of a Kittenfish with a Perch was once described by a famous statesman as "Grotesque, unbelievable, bizarre and unprecedented." The phrase GUBU has since been coined to describe such scandalous events.

1804.d: That Kittenperch can now be used as an ingredient.

1805.d: Some fish just don't know when to put it away... Cover up, get off the stage... Catching this bugger couldn't be easier.

1806.d: This Shiny Sardine can now be used as an ingredient.

1807.d: Unlike the Shiny Sardine, the Dark Sardine is extremely difficult to catch.

1808.d: This Dark Sardine can now be used as an ingredient.

1809.d: Served on top of lettuce, this fish will fill your belly for a little while. It's not the tastiest, though.

1810.d: Served on top of lettuce, this fish will fill your belly for a while. It's quite tasty, too.

1811.d: Everybody likes crunchy Grawn Fritters. The problem is that they quickly become addictive.

1812.d: Everybody likes crunchy Grawn Fritters. The problem is that they quickly become addictive.

1813.d: Slices of gudgeon, hard boiled with onions. Quite delightful despite the smell off you for the following few days.

1814.d: Slices of gudgeon, hard boiled with onions. Quite delightful despite the smell off you for the following few days.

1815.d: When cooked too quickly in black Bwork bwutter, this skate wing releases an eye-watering flavour into the chewing mouth of the muncher. This meal is not a memorable one.

1816.d: When cooked in black Bwork bwutter, this skate wing releases a rather bland flavour into the chewing mouth of the muncher. This meal wasn't too bad though, all things considered.

1817.d: Steam-cooked to retain the flavour, this small carp's flavour will sweep you off your feet!

1818.d: Steam-cooked to retain the flavour, this small carp will make you forget all your troubles. Tomorrow's gonna be another day... just enjoy this steamed-carp-flavoured moment!

1819.d: Steam-cooked to retain the flavour, this small carp will make you forget all your troubles. Tomorrow's gonna be another day... just enjoy the steamed-carp-flavoured moment!

1820.d:
This grilled kralove gives off a strong smell, but it's a true delicacy if you manage to overcome your disgust.  
A small piece of advice... find something long and sharp to eat it with.

1821.d: This grilled kralove doesn't smell too bad, and it's a true delicacy if you manage to overcome your indifference.

1822.d: This fish swam a long way, but failed to make it to the spawning grounds. Still, it's ready to be eaten, even if it is a little bland.

1823.d: This fish swam a long way, and made it to the spawning grounds, where it spawned a few young. It's now ready to be eaten, and tastes good.

1824.d: This fish swam a long way, and spawned many young in the rivers of Amakna. It's now ready to be eaten, and tastes delicious.

1825.d: You won't feed the family, or even yourself, with this fried sardine, but it does make an excellent starter.

1826.d: You won't feed the family, or even yourself, with this fried sardine, but it does make an excellent main course.

1827.d: You won't feed the family, or even yourself, with this fried sardine, but it does make an excellent dessert.

1828.d: Served on top of lettuce, this fish will fill your belly for a long time. It's absolutely delicious!

1829.d: Everybody likes Grawn fritters. With a low calorie content, it would stupid to refuse them.

1830.d: Slices of gudgeon, hard boiled with onions. Quite delightful... And the usual horrible odour is masked by a mysterious scent of fresh flowers too.

1831.d: When cooked with care in black Bwork bwutter, this skate wing releases an incredible flavour into the chewing mouth of the muncher. This meal will truly give you wings.

1832.d: If prepared following the exotic and ancestral recipe of the Lenalds, this kind of fish will help rekindle the fire in your belly... provided you can master the recipe, which is very rare indeed.

1833.d: If prepared following the exotic and ancestral recipe of the Lenalds, this kind of fish will help rekindle the fire in your belly... provided you can master the recipe, which is very rare indeed.

1834.d: If prepared following the exotic and ancestral recipe of the Lenalds, this kind of fish will help rekindle the fire in your belly... provided you can master the recipe, which is very rare indeed.

1835.d: Your Daddy caught this pike one day during the war. Now he knew if his captain ever saw the fish it'd be confiscated. Your daddy wanted to bring that fish home to you, so he stuck it up... well, let's say he hid it. Your daddy died soon after, so I pulled it out of his... body and hid it in my own... body. Now, little warrior, I give the fish to you.

1836.d: Your Daddy caught this pike one day during the war. Now he knew if his captain ever saw the fish it'd be confiscated. Your daddy wanted to bring that fish home to you, so he stuck it up... well, let's say he hid it. Your daddy died soon after, so I pulled it out of his... body and hid it in my own... body. Now, little warrior, I give the fish to you.

1837.d: Your Daddy caught this pike one day during the war. Now he knew if his captain ever saw the fish it'd be confiscated. Your daddy wanted to bring that fish home to you, so he stuck it up... well, let's say he hid it. Your daddy died soon after, so I pulled it out of his... body and hid it in my own... body. Now, little warrior, I give the fish to you.

1838.d: This shark wouldn't have the decency to sprinkle you with a few spices before it ate you.

1839.d: This shark wouldn't have the decency to sprinkle you with a few hearty spices before it ate you.

1840.d: This shark wouldn't have the decency to sprinkle you with a few magic spices before it ate you.

1844.d: Trout are easy to catch. Experienced fishermen haul them in by threes.

1845.d: This Trout can now be used as an ingredient.

1846.d: This is one of the oldest trout in the world. If the simple passage of time makes you wiser, this trout must be the wisest of all... To be honest, though, that's not what I've heard.

1847.d: This pike is a freshwater fish of average size. It's a barbecue's best friend.

1848.d: This Pike can now be used as an ingredient.

1849.d: This new species - resulting from the cross-breeding of several types of pike by the scientists Halett and Tupe - is supposed to have magical properties. Created only for experimentation, two specimens escaped during a violent argument between the two experts.

1851.d: This Tupe-Halett Pike can now be used as an ingredient.

1852.d: This Sickle-Hammerhead Shark can now be used as an ingredient.

1853.d: A cousin of the Sickle-Hammerhead Shark, this animal is more ferocious and doesn't have a considerate fish-bone in its body. Catching an Open-Market Shark is the dream of every fisherman - or more precisely, catching one AND staying alive to tell the tale.

1854.d: The Gutted Open-Market Shark can now be used as an ingredient.

1859.d: This grilled kralove smells delicious. A cold Kikim Inn Beer, sunshine glinting off the Asse sea, a plateful of Grilled Kralove ****. Does life get any better than that?

1860.d: This very sturdy fishing rod, specially designed to catch sharks, has a hook resembling a bloody harpoon.

1861.d: This fishing rod has been specially designed for catching perch.

1862.d: The wood that this rod is made from smells of resin, and as a result, so does the hook and the wire. This heady scent must be like that of a female Kralove. Why else would all male Kralove rush towards your tackle?

1863.d: Cho was the most renowned cook at the round table. He always provided fresh food for his customers. This rod allowed him to catch the fish he needed for his famous "Carp at Cho" dish.

1864.d: The thread of this fishing rod is made of pure wool and a ball of wool replaces the bait. Few Kittenfishes can resist playing with it.

1865.d: This fishing rod is especially designed to fit the... "particular" features of the Breaded Fish.

1866.d: This basic rod will allow young fishermen to catch almost anything provided they are patient enough.

1867.d: For professional fishermen only. If you master this hook canon, you'll be able to catch small comets from their orbit.

1868.d: This fishing rod will go to incredible lengths to catch fish for you, but only if you're a master fisherman.

1869.d: This tooth extractor is specially designed for Gobballs but you can also use it to extract one of your own decayed gnashers. The rest will surely fall out not long after, though.

1870.d: This Gobball tooth is so similar to a human one, you'll find it hard to tell them apart.

1871.d: The necklace the Mayor's daughter lost. Unfortunately, it's in bad condition since its sojourn in a Crow's stomach...

1872.d:
Gunpowder. There's a label with a simple reminder printed on it: 
Powder + Flame = Explosion

1873.d: A Plain Crackler's rock block, similar to those used in the building of fortifications of Bonta.

1874.d: Some Scurvion venom which shouldn't fall into foreign hands.

1875.d: Why cut wheat with this scythe when you can cut granite?

1876.d: This inspection form of the Brakmarian act n°243 enables you to detect whether a man is part of it or not...

1877.d: The former owner of this hat probably took a few blows too many to the head, which tends to happen when you rebel against Bonta's authority.

1878.d: This playing card has a particular appearance close to perfection. It is apparently a collector's card.

1879.d: A crate of edged weapons, full of all kinds of blunt instruments.

1880.d: Yum! Kittycare! Your Kaniger will leap over the moon with delight.

1882.d: You have picked up a very appetizing Pulpy substance.

1883.d: The necklace the Mayor's daughter lost, as good as new...

1889.d: Sharpened into quill pens for years, Crow feathers are now used to adorn the rich and famous. No wonder crows are nervous creatures - anyone who knows the value of these feathers will go a long way to get their hands on them.

1890.d: The hair of the Kaniger reflects the sun in a strange way, as if it was absorbing some of the rays.

1891.d: Have you ever dreamt of a magnificent Plissken leather bag? Never? Good on you! It's not that resistant anyway!

1892.d: Panic-stricken, Lord Crow spread its wings to fly off and let this feather fall. Nothing special there and yet...

1893.d: A fantastic trophy, it's a pity it oozes smelly fluid.

1894.d: This type of hair is really disgusting. If you have a closer look at it, you'll discover a great microcosm of different parasites living on it... How lucky you are !

1895.d: You'll recover a few Health Points with this highly alcoholic beer.

1896.d: This Tofu leg is proof that hunters can show, although very infrequently, a tiny sunbeam of sensitivity.

1897.d: Tiny Kwak legs for maximum Kwak-taste.

1898.d: This yellow and putrid heap represents the true nature of the Larva. Now you understand why their skin is so tough.

1899.d: This yellow and putrid heap represents the true nature of the Larva. Now you understand why their skin is so tough.

1900.d: This yellow and putrid heap represents the true nature of the Larva. Now you understand why their skin is so tough.

1901.d: This leg is simply perfect. You just can't help eyeing it up greedily for a while before eating it.

1902.d: This cawwot-flavoured Wabbit leg is ideal for stew.

1903.d: A good muscular leg which will make a delightful meal.

1904.d: A White Dreggon Shell padded with leather and wool, this headgear will protect you against basic attacks and the lightning bolts of a stumbling, drunk Bwork Magus. You'll also look like you just came out of a Dreggon's backside.

1905.d: A big leg which will fill you up!

1907.d: These ears will accentuate your bright smile and get the opposite sex spreading rumours about you...

1908.d: Even Spartapine the Great Reaper doesn't have such a helmet, the precious stones and metals used to make it ensure your noggin will be kept safe and sound inside..

1910.d: This cloak is made from the body parts of an Ouginak, it still has the smell of the creature's humid nose. Personally, its taste reminds me of a horny set of Gobball's udders... Well, someone told me that... damn...

1911.d: The smell off this small leg disappears when cooked.

1912.d: This leg reeks of death... I assure you it was cleared of all involvement in the murder of its owner... Just smells like... Death.

1913.d: This is the leg of a Gobball War Chief. As solid as a Crackler, it could be a very powerful bludgeon, if you can stand the smell...

1914.d: Tender but tough, not too fatty or too dry, this leg improves with age like a good wine.

1915.d: Don't underestimate the value of this slimy and suffocating flesh... It's nutritional value, that is.

1916.d: Similar to Moskito flesh except there is ten times more of it. Fortunately, some people like it.

1917.d: This choice morsel of boar is quite bloody for the moment but it will make a great meal.

1918.d: A bit bigger for a bit more happiness, this skilfully carved lump of Plain Boar will delight all kinds of carnivores.

1919.d: That piece of Dragon Pig is so tender and soft that you could make a perfect cushion with it. But it's still nicer to eat it.

1920.d: This badge is used to identify militiamen who have fallen on battlefields. Apparently some people collect them in Brakmar.

1921.d: A deliciously tough loin of pork from an athletic pig.

1922.d: Rare high-quality meat, it remains hot hours after roasting. It's very convenient for picnics.

1923.d: This dragomeat, on top of remaining hot, has a  naturally smoky taste.

1924.d: Dreggon Dragomeat is a bit hard to chew but is far more nourishing than standard Dragomeat. Some say it has magic properties.

1925.d: This pass gives you a day leave.

1926.d: The meat of the Dragon Pig's dragon parts (nobody knows their exact location, nor does anybody want to try) is a godsend. Which makes sense given that Dragon Pigs can fly.

1927.d: Miliboowolf muzzle, with its small, firm chops, accompanies all salads perfectly.

1928.d: The extraction of this Plain Boar tusk certainly required a great deal of know how.

1929.d: This dainty muzzle is synonymous with a lack of will. Consume without moderation.

1930.d: This tasty meat must be eaten in moderation. There's a reason the Moowolf has such terribly bad breath!

1931.d: It's Amayiro's weapon. You can easily handle it but it seems to be slightly nicked.

2213.d: It's not hard to sleep like a Sadida. A bedside rug, darkness... your head trapped in your rectum. Success guaranteed!

2214.d: You'll have the Iop Attitude until your next fight.

2215.d: You'll have the Xelor Attitude until your next fight.

2216.d: You'll have the Sadida Attitude until your next fight.

2217.d: You took this wig out of an old cupboard, didn't you? It might have been fashionable in your grandmother's day, but not anymore, buddy. It makes you look like a Feca on a Saturday night. Awful.

2218.d: You'll have the Feca Attitude until your next fight.

2219.d: These Eniripsa's wings won't make you fly. So don't try to show this gear off or you're sure to make a complete idiot of yourself.

2220.d: You'll have the Eniripsa Attitude until your next fight.

2221.d: A fake beard which makes you look like an Enutrof and which also gives you the breath of an Enutrof on a Monday morning. You don't need me to tell you that it must be used in extreme moderation.

2222.d: You'll have the Enutrof Attitude until your next fight.

2223.d: A little Tofu blood, a false scar, the eyes of an epileptic pirate, and there you go! You can now go to Sacrier funerals unnoticed! That can be useful, you know.

2224.d: You'll have the Sacrier Attitude until your next fight.

2225.d: A Skully, a cape on your head and the illusion is perfect. If you wear this outfit, you will look like a hideous character coming from the depths of a cemetery... yes, you'll look like a Sram!

2226.d: You'll have the Sram Attitude until your next fight.

2227.d: Whether you like it or not, if you wear these horns and forked tail you'll find yourself invited to numerous secret Osamodas meetings. They're so secret almost nobody ever turns up... That's the one good thing about secret events... You always have a good excuse not to go.

2228.d: You'll have the Osamodas Attitude until your next fight.

2229.d: You will find silky Wabbit ears, a tabby tail and a box of restless fleas. If you find yourself in a popular restaurant and you need a table, just release the little devils, you'll have no problem. Well... the chef will leave too, I suppose. And the staff. Come to think of it, you probably wouldn't want to stay there yourself. I'll get back to you on that one.

2230.d: You'll have the Ecaflip Attitude until your next fight.

2231.d: As you know, a Cra never leaves home without a quiver. No wonder people think you're a Cra when you walk around with yours.

2232.d: You'll have the Cra Attitude until your next fight.

2233.d: Xof the Fox created this belt after he inexplicably decided to gather up all the teeth he could find on a Wabbit battlefield. It has now become a lifelong passion of his.

2234.d: You'll have the Bonta Attitude until your next fight.

2235.d: You have the Brakmar Attitude until your next fight.

2236.d: You won't be able take two steps without being asked for directions when you're wearing this costume.

2237.d: You'll be dreaded by all 'n' sundry with these things on.

2239.d: This powder is only made in small quantities from Eniripsas' wings. Pets all over the world say yes to its amazing healing powers.

2240.d: Ideal at small weddings, perfect for the annual Captain Chafer Panty Party.

2241.d: This Royal Jelly used to strike fear into the hearts of all but the craziest warriors. Be careful not to eat it... it's no plain Mint Jelly.

2242.d: This concentrate of Royal Strawberry Jelly can turn a pacifist Tabi into a bloodthirsty killing-machine. An excellent reason to avoid giving it to your friends as a starter.

2245.d: Once used as a backscratcher (back when a back was a back and a man was a man), it's now used to hang coats. I think that sums up the whole sorry history of the World of Twelve.

2246.d: This crown was either broken by a powerful magic attack or by that last headbutt the Royal Tofu tried to give you.

2247.d: You'd have to be a lop not to realize that this Feather comes from the backside of a Royal Tofu. You'd have to be an Osamodas to want to touch it.

2248.d: This kind of hair can keep you warm since you are all sweaty after holding it for quite some time. Unless you are sweaty because you are afraid of meeting another Ouginak who might see you holding an Ouginak hair and therefore want to avenge his friend.

2249.d: This leaf must supply the Trunknid with strength to fight. But for this, one should know how to use it properly. Indeed, the first thing you'd think about is chopping and adding it to your beans. So delicious!

2250.d: This piece of wood sounds hollow. The green sap coming out of it proves that it is the nose of the Trunknid.

2251.d: Thou shalt not cast the first Megastone!

2252.d: You've just broken the tooth of a Crackler. What a pity it was his only tooth! A denture could easily have covered the monthly cost of the Zaap.

2253.d: This Flower facilitates digestion. Now you can stay as long as you want at the local free buffet.

2254.d: Ambusher leaf has a very unusual taste, somewhere between hazelnut and slightly limp salad. If you dare to try the meals you make, you will soon realise they taste a little like treachery...

2255.d: No recent dangerous activity has been reported. The Militiamen Organization is in turmoil since the murder of one of their people. The culprit is apparently a Bontarian.

2256.d: This rat is now dead meat... one less scum-rodent to crowd out the sewer entrance.

2257.d: This piece of Sewer Wall was found in the stomach of a thingamajig.
2257.n: A piece of the Sewer Wall

2259.d: What's in your hand is the most ancient game in Amakna. The rules are simple: throw a tooth and try to catch it with the same hand while you pick up another Karne Tooth on the ground.

2260.d: Someone, apparently a Brakmarian, slipped this card into your bag. It says that Warriors are interested in your talents as an assassin and they suggest you join the mad Brakmarian adventure.

2261.d: You're possessed by a Sniffling Spirit. Your odour and vitality are its bread and butter.

2262.d: You found a Bontarian who stank of blood. All you know about this fellow is written on this piece of paper.

2263.d: This staff is possessed by a sniffling spirit. This imp-like being haunts items and living things alike with a special smell before going back to the Land of the not-quite-living-but-far-from-dead.

2264.d: Goblins often make fun of people, which can be quite irritating. Slicing up those bobbling, wobbling Goblins should shut them up, however.

2265.d: You've freed a sniffling spirit but he didn't anchor on the targeted person. You have written some information about the person on this piece of paper.

2266.d: This Pig Milk comes from a Piglet. Remember this just in case...

2267.d:
How many farmhands does it take to milk a Dragon Pig? Seven. One to milk it and the other six to carry his coffin. 
BOOOOO! GET OFF THE STAGE!

2268.d: Here is a scalp which could start a new fashion in the Enutrof world: the Toopish. A little bit of anti-lice potion and you'll be ready to participate in the "World's Classiest Enutrof" Contest.

2269.d: This Eye is intact. Scrambled eyes with a pinch of oregano and some salty tears really gets you going in the morning. At the same time having it in your hands will prove to Oto that you've killed a Blue Larva.

2270.d: This bunch of eggs looks like a big bunch of grapes. Don't even think about popping them in your mouth though.

2271.d: Bwork handicraft remains very mysterious. Some adventurers think the purplish colour comes from Goblins. But the origins of the leather are still unknown. Very strange.

2272.d: This larva has just hatched. As its very first image of the world was your face, it considers you as its mother.

2273.d: The main characteristics of this strange Purple Fabric are that it is light and soft to the touch.  The tag says "made in Tie One On".

2274.d: Take an Enutrof. When it's dark in the mines, no one can see him. The dark Miner you took this candle off on the other hand... well, he can't be seen either since you now have his candle.

2275.d: The Lousy Pig nearly disappeared from the food chain. People had to mate Boars with Piglets to fill Cania Plains with Lousy Pigs once more. The Lousy Pig is mad at the entire world ever since.

2277.d: To gain credibility, Ghosts roll themselves up in a Shroud. That's one way of frightening lost adventurers.

2278.d: This fabric once belonged to Mill Burray, hunter of gophers. He spread it out to trap the burrowing creatures and prevent them from tunnelling all over his golf course. The charismatic Captain Chafer took hold of the fabric before disappearing in mysterious circumstances...

2279.d: This tooth once belonged to a Vampire. This can't be any other way. We can see that from the very sharp tip of the tooth.

2280.d:
Never underestimate a Vampire, especially when he is holding a straw;
            he could suck your blood till his thirst is quenched.

2281.d: This tissue looks like it is alive. Vampires often use it to make beautiful costumes for fancy dress balls.

2282.d: Finally, conclusive evidence that even monsters get stressed out.

2283.d: This Kwoan Eye has surprising hypnotic effects. Try to keep a clear head while using it.

2284.d: The entry of the Legendary Golden Larvae Cave is situated a little west of Amakna. The latent powers of your golden larva will allow you to enter the cave. But make sure it doesn't get hurt or else it will run to its daddy's arms.

2285.d: One absolute certainty about this fabric is that it's itchy. You'll understand when I tell you that an Ouginak used to use it as a handkerchief.

2286.d: These bandages are revolutionary: triple thickness, ultra-resistant and violet-scented. Shaped for confidence, shaped for comfort.

2287.d: This leather comes ready-treated. Its origin remains unknown but the colour probably comes from a special dye.

2288.d: Many tourists come to Wabbit Island especially to find a Wabbit's Paw which is supposed to be a lucky charm. It's not true unfortunately, but keep it to yourself otherwise tourism could suffer from it.

2290.d: You want a lampshade? You got it! You don't want a lampshade? You got nothing.

2291.d: You want a lampshade? You got it! You don't want a lampshade? You got nothing.

2292.d: You want a lampshade? You got it! You don't want a lampshade? You got nothing.

2293.d: You want a lampshade? You got it! You don't want a lampshade? You got nothing.

2294.d: At first sight these entrails do not look particularly mouth-watering. However, if you chop them finely with some sun-dried herbs, some wild mint and then braise them in a rusty cauldron, they'll make a satisfying meal for discerning Chafers.

2295.d: With this Fragment of Sword hung above the fireplace, you have at last a good reason to show off. You have defeated the Crocodyl after all, just as the eccentric Mikool J., also known as Crocodyl Dandi, did before you.

2296.d: What purpose could this beautiful, jewel-decorated shield possibly serve? While you search for the answer, you can use it as a tea tray.

2297.d: This Bolt can be used to make a short but sharp weapon. It can also serve as a toothpick. It all depends where your priorities lie.

2299.d: This epaulette has survived many long battles... It's stronger than it looks. It'll make you think twice about hitting Dark Vlad on the shoulder if you're attached to your weapon at the time.

2300.d: This fragment of bone has either come from the remains of a Chafer, or from the leftovers of a Moowolf meal. There's also a large chance that it hasn't got anything to do with either one.

2301.d: Not very resistant, these whiskers will enable you to show off in front of your friends...by imitating Salv and Torh Bali,  Great Brakmarian Painters, for example.

2302.d: Several illustrious Amakna think tanks are solely occupied with finding out what use the crab could possibly make of its little, crabby tongue. They would be shocked if they knew...

2303.d: Once emptied, this crab shell can hold a good many items. The problem is you'll never be able to get rid of the crabby smell. People have lost friends over much less...

2304.d: This fragment of polished stone comes from the left buttock of a Plain Crackler. For squashing Arachnees, there's nothing finer, except for the Crackler itself, perhaps.

2305.d: This fragment of pointed stone comes from the right shoulder blade of a Plain Crackler. Or maybe it's a part of the lower abdomen. Anyway, just be careful where you put it.

2306.d: Heart of stone, don't you see the love I feel for you? But if you go on, I'll leave you all alone, I won't let myself be tired out by you.

2308.d: This badge allows warriors who have fallen in battle to be identified. Apparently some people collect them in Bonta.

2309.d: This red candle is unlike any other.

2315.d: While the tiny, but beautiful, Midgette Bardot ruled the land, a strict ban was imposed on the hunting of Whitish Fangs. Now she's in exile, and it's hunting season all year round! The tailors are crying out for skins... Make sure you slaughter at least one Whitish Fang - before they disappear forever.

2316.d: The Yellow Fang of the Whitish Fang has sent many an adventurer fleeing off in terror, don't underestimate this tooth.

2317.d: When you see what kind of filth and bugs the Whitish Fang has in his ears, you wonder how it hears a thing at all.

2318.d: Some Goblins wear a Bear paw around their neck. Nobody recalls the origin or meaning of this superstition.

2320.d: A message is inscribed on this Ouginak collar: "If lost, please return me to my Brakmarian master on Sidimote Moor, who will reward you with a punch in the face."

2321.d: Did it cross your mind that these Ouginak Chops could slobber for all eternity? Well, the scary part is they probably can - Ouginaks are well-known for their everlasting gluttony.

2322.d: Don't be fooled, these small toothy-pegs are actually real sharp, stinky, used fangs. Sometimes unscrupulous Enutrof dentists replace teeth with them.

2323.d: This is some good quality cord. Heavy though... You'd be amazed how many people put their backs out just picking it up!

2324.d: Unlike the Lolwut Pear, the Lol Wutermelon is made of fail.

2325.d: The famous minstrel Jon Lemon once composed an ode to this fruit: "Happiness is a warm Banana".

2326.d: They say that oranges are not the only fruit...

2327.d: An apple a day keeps apple farmers in business.

2328.d: This golden pearl is a gift from the small larva you have accompanied. Consequently, it has a great sentimental value... and some monetary value too. Its softness and colour make it a perfect gift for every person who has even the slightest feminine side.

2329.d: This juicy Lolwut pear is made of win.

2330.d: This capsule contains extracts of magical citrus fruits. You are advised to shake it before opening, so the pulp doesn't stay stuck to the bottom.

2331.d: This isn't the most nutritious of vegetables and it often requires strong seasoning to make it a bit more tasty. In spite of its bad reputation, however, it's really quite healthy. Well, healthy for everyone except Bworks. No one knows why, however.

2332.d: This boiled sweet appears to be slightly past its best-before-date, or might have been stored in a cupboard next to an open can of Bow Meow food, as it has a rather unusual taste. Eating it might stop you crying, for a few minutes at least.

2333.d: This drop will increase your concentration during fights but it doesn't taste good. (DOUBLE CLICK TO USE IT, bonus 20 for Wisdom and 10 for Prospecting, usable for the 30 next fights).

2336.d: Never more will this skull rattle, but then again...

2337.d: This book appears to be magic. Very strange.

2339.d:
A mid-level warrior should wear anything but rags or flashy clothes. A better option might be the following:
- A Camate
- A Vitality Headband and a Vital Belt
- Kluh's Boots
- A Brakmarian Cloak.

2340.d: You must be a real fetishist to own these... or is someone making fun of you...

2341.d: Mech Riorraw specially designed this bow. It can cross lava rivers and reach the top of Brakmar walls. No more, no less.

2342.d: Domen gave you this ring. If you give it back it means you support the destruction of life itself. Which is perfectly alright, of course, you'll just have to find some new friends.

2343.d: Djaul gave you this bracelet. It shows everyone that you agree with his words.

2344.d: Domen gave you this letter addressed to Oto.

2345.d: This turtle won't show off any longer.

2346.d: Sorry, this is NOT Dragovamp, the famous flying bat outfit. This is the outfit of an inhabitant of the cemetery, some rogue this fellow...

2347.d: This report relates the Brakmar attack on the East wall.

2348.d: You'll have the Rogue Attitude until your next fight.

2349.d: Domen gave you this letter addressed to Oto, but you forgot to give it to him.

2350.d: Is this the tuft of hair you ripped out of that Osamodas' chest that time?

2351.d: You get to eat and drink at the same time with this bread.

2352.d: "I have to talk to you, come and see me when you have a moment to yourself. See you soon, my young friend."

2353.d: "Hi, I'm Larry Poller, we met when Colonel Lyeno was freed. I need your help. Come and see me when you have a moment to yourself. See you soon."

2354.d: Cooked with great loving care, this Turtle Brain can become a delicious meal.

2355.d: This blueish dust is a very powerful magic catalyst.

2356.d: You have a Wonderful Power until your next fight.

2357.d: This wood seems to be completely heat-resistant. Don't try to use it to make a fire as you will die of exposure before the wood ever lights.

2358.d: This wood is the softest you can find. It is solid, malleable and a joy to carve.

2359.d: Ufot Eticili gave you this small brooch.

2360.d: It's the title deed of Ufot Eticili's house.

2361.d: This bow is a creation of the inspired Mulic Bere. Its maximum range is just incredible. The problem is the minimum range can also be as incredible.

2362.d: Paro Cabanne's prediction for the next elections.

2365.d: This ordinary-looking bramble leaf is an essential plant for some strange recipes.

2366.d: This metal and diamond fishing rod is the only pole that can support a kralove's weight. It is also impregnated with the smell of a female kralove in order to give you some chance of luring this monster.

2367.d: Lehunui thought he knew how to make friends. He often invited complete strangers to fancy-dress balls and bought them dinner, champagne and magnificent jewels. His conversation, in contrast, was paltry and extremely monotonous... Most people took the money and ran... stuffing a la carte meals into doggy bags one course after the other to be eaten in better company.

2368.d: Ramoune was a childhood friend of the sunny Nova. When Ramoune decided to put his spotless mind at rest for an eternal nap, he put an end to their friendship.

2369.d: This dazzling belt is the result of a mad bet to restore one of the most dazzling belts ever created in Amakna: it's the Dazzling Belt. Pakape Promethe won the contest.

2370.d: Some incredibly light equipment that finally brings a little delicacy into the cruel world of the Bwork.

2371.d: Jiva recommends this belt for those long, cold waking nights. If stained, hand wash with Rimennelle.

2372.d: Wearing these boots, you'll feel like you're walking on fresh grass. Their particular niche is the bio-conservative Hyuppie demographic.

2373.d: Moon Hair, used to make this pair of boots, is absolutely ideal for keeping your feet warm. These boots are also a heart-warming memory of Moon.

2374.d: Tarsy the hermit quite obviously couldn't stand visitors. Any guests who did dare come along quickly left with nothing but a big, red boot mark on their back.

2375.d: Wearing these boots, you'll hear the noise of the wind on the coast or the cries of a chafer Lancer lost in the inmost depths of the labyrinth. They're disturbingly similar.

2376.d: This axe is the only blade capable of resisting the aggressive power of the Kaerlier tree and therefore, the only one that can cut it down.

2379.d: This wood comes from the legendary Kaerlier. Its properties are quite... surprising.

2380.d: It's a strange cloak made of pieces of Mushd which are very much all of one piece. And you can give the one who is laughing a piece of his mind.

2381.d: This cloak is made with a pennant, which used to be kept on the highest tower of Amakna Castle. This is probably why it smells like fresh, sun-kissed linen waving in a June breeze..

2382.d: Maimpa, an Ecaflip who wasn't afraid of heights... he thought he'd always land on his feet. One day, he landed on a starving Trool and was buried the same day on the very spot where his remains were found... Well, the spot where the biggest pieces were found.

2383.d: Made of bloody tissue, the Kwag'U Cape feels like stiff cardboard... a bit like a big, cape-shaped scab.

2384.d: There's something beastly about these boots. Don't be shocked if a Boowolf starts humping a limb when you put them on... Does your neck count as a limb? Well, it does for a loved-up Boowolf.

2385.d: Ideal for laying on the green grass of your garden or wiping the green mess in your nose, the Grazor can is one of the few inanimate objects that can multitask.

2386.d: This strange cape draws its strength from its rundown look. The dirtier it is, the more useful it is.

2387.d:
This cloak smells very bad - it has to be said. Truth be told, it's made with a dense mixture of monster hairs, which gives off this wonderful medley of odours.
Do not confuse the Hairy Cloak with Hairy Pie, which is something else entirely.

2388.d: A long time ago, an Ecaflip follower called Dodge dropped a valuable treasure map which was carved on stone. He made an amulet of the largest piece, believing he would one day unite the pieces once more. Then he lost the amulet.

2389.d: Dodge brought meaning to his life by smashing, burning, grinding, selling... no, sorry not selling... ehh... throwing away, spitting on... everything he owned. And you should see what he did to his Kamas. My Lord, I know they're only a moulded piece of copper, but still, I pity those poor coins...

2390.d: This Amulet is almost perfect. It considerably increases the wisdom of anyone who wears it. It's useful for making yourself appear wise in front of your friends, or passing yourself off as a model pupil.

2391.d: There's an old saying that goes: "Lucky one day, double lucky the day after." The longer you think about it, the more ridiculous that saying gets.

2392.d: Thanks to the artisans of Amakna who are multitalented, the Modified Dragolyre is almost perfect.

2393.d: The Osamodas Onehaieuf Bek craved the respect of his guild members, so he decided to create a revolutionary Amulet. He found inspiration one morning while making some breakfast for his friends... Okaaaay!

2394.d: This heart-warming, sun kissed little thing lends a feeling of invulnerability to the wearer. It's so light that many wear it for years without realizing they have it on... Yes, there are those among you who do not shower for years at a time.

2395.d: Mad Bacon was a little vile demon with the enraging habit of standing right in front of people and not moving. He was magic-proof, which imposed a certain respect at the time. The Mad bacon went underground recently, he stood in front of the wrong guy for the wrong length of time.

2396.d: The name of this amulet is unpronounceable in the language of the country where it is manufactured, for non-natives, anyway. To make it more appealing to the Amaknean market, its designer used the services of a local translator, a certain Lou Gull, to help him come up with a new name. When the designer saw how much Lou Gull charged for his services, he used a cheaper translator instead. Evidently, you get what you pay for.

2397.d: Law-bibe was an old man who took whatever came to hand to create strange, strange items. One day, he made a locket with scrap off the street. He put it round his neck, and felt a strange sensation... a very strange sensation.

2398.d: The self-made Kaniger Rucky Balboua gave this eye to Melyonen to thank her for introducing his future wife, Adriana, to him. Soon after, they separated. Rucky would scream her name at the top of his voice and burst into tears without the slightest warning.

2399.d:
Barren Sameday, husband to Marman Brigette, was an Ecaflip with extraordinary talents. This Miliboowolf-hair bag containing a lump of bamboo wood was his favourite charm. He'd carve the amount of Kamas he wished to win into the wood with a Kloon Snapper tooth. This gris-gris brought him good and often uncomfortable luck, but above all, incredible wealth.
Maybe he was just good at cards, though.

2400.d: There's something... ehh... how shall I put it... dark about these boots. So don't be surprised if a Vampire falls in love with you when you wear them. I mean I don't know if you've had a hard life up to now, but I would say it would be the worst thing that's ever happened to you... Like, the worst. Worse than... I dunno. Bad, really. Like, awful.

2401.d: This card is linked to Master Kweats. That's all you'll ever know and all you need to know.

2402.d: This sword is only presented to the most accomplished of mercenaries as a kind of conversation piece. That's not to say a single swipe wouldn't take your leg off...

2403.d: In bygone days, it was used for parole, the Peeka Belt has apparently a spare power in relation to the other belts. But nobody has found what it is. You'd better keep a close eye on the thing.

2404.d: This belt once belonged to a Sewer Rat. It suits it perfectly. What I'm not supposed to tell you is that the little rodent had the most horrifying case of love handle you've ever seen.

2409.d: The Fire Kwak Headdress will make a real charmer out of you... Charm is the second best way of sidelining your enemies in the heat of combat... The other is raw, unpackaged, unapproved-by-the-FDA LUST. Let me tell you, though, with the beasts that wander round these parts, you'll feel like a big of cheese in a Bonta rat trap if you take the latter approach.

2410.d: The Treechelmet protects you from hangovers.

2411.d: This magnificent headgear increases strength and intelligence... if you can stand the smell.

2412.d: This cloak won't make you fly but it will itch like hell. Even if you sew a big "S" on it, it won't work... though some people a few years ago on a cliff were absolutely convinced of it. Too bad.

2413.d: With these Treechnid Leaves on, you'll be able to strut about in the forest without being recognized. However, beware of the Treechnids in search of spring buddings.

2414.d: This cape has it all: it's hard-wearing, comfortable, colourful and rare... But it smells dreadful, just awful. Well, as we always say, you can't have it all!

2415.d: The Fire Kwakblade is a magnificent weapon. Even if you don't scare your enemy away, at least, you might make an lasting impression.

2416.d: The user guide explains that this surprising hammer can release astonishingly powerful energy when correctly used. Another Osamodas' user guide translated into Sadida...

2417.d: This staff has kept all the aggressiveness of the Treechnid, but hasn't kept the musty smell which often characterizes old Treechnids.

2418.d: Using this ring, your master may be able to find you if you get lost while delivering a letter.

2419.d: This ring once belonged to the renowned Bouze Lite Yeah, the saviour of the modern age. He never stopped going on about some place he used to drink called the Inn 'Finity and Beyond'.

2420.d: The branch of a Treechnid isn't easy to carve, but with some perseverance you'll get a simple and stylish ring. Simple and stylish like a sleeping Osamodas.

2421.d: With those Fire Kwak spurs on, every Sram for miles around will be on your back.

2422.d: These are the most comfortable boots ever created. The inside seems to be padded with Gobball Wool and you can feel a liquid running through your toes. For all you know, it could be Gobball Saliva... even Blood. Whatever!

2423.d: You'd get the same effects out of this pair of Boots as you would from an evening at the tavern. You must have a drink, or plenty of drinks, to get the optimum effect. And the next day, your legs will feel as heavy as these boots.

2424.d: With all these feathers around your neck, you'll look like Aldo Rado, the great Sacrier adventurer eternally searching for a golden city.

2425.d: A fine piece of Gobball horn, this. The material is known for bringing peace and wisdom to these tranquil beasts, so a Gobball amulet should bring peace and wisdom too. Although since you murdered the poor thing to get it, maybe the opposite will happen. Who knows.

2426.d: This small Arachnee is the proof that you don't have to stuff an animal to turn it into an amulet. It will tickle your neck and might even spin a web in front of your mouth if you yawn too much or talk too much rubbish.

2427.d: This Belt is perfect to strut about like a Fire Kwak during the season of love. Provided, of course, that it's the only thing you're wearing.

2428.d: Easy to wear, this belt is quite light in relation to its size. The wool looks brand new... according to the legend, about a hundred Gobballs had to be cut to pieces to get this smooth and silky look.

2429.d: This belt will increase your self-confidence and give you abs of wood. An anti-Arachnee treatment is nevertheless strongly recommended once a year. It is more or less the same as the hair of a Sadida, but with a lot less anti-parasites.

2430.d: You pity the Blue Jelly, don't you... And you still managed to treat it like this!

2431.d: You've bullied this poor little Lemon Jelly. Be careful because one day you might find yourself as flat as it is now...

2432.d: You've bullied this poor little Strawberry Jelly. Be careful because one day you might find yourself as misshapen as it is now...

2433.d: You've bullied this poor little Mint Jelly. Be careful because one day you might find yourself as squashed as it is now...

2435.d: Thanks to these homemade boots, Kere was the only Eniripsa ever to win the Great Amakna Triathlon. The Ecaflips thought the second coming was at hand when they saw him skimming along on the Asse Sea... For years afterwards he was harassed by Pandawas begging him to turn their water into wine.

2436.d: This pot of Lemon Jelly looks quite strange. According to Elrik Ola, this jelly comes from his place. From the other side of the galaxy, to be more precise. It's a pity it tastes so good!

2437.d: Some say Royal Lemon Jelly is much more tasty than all the others. Maybe because Lemon hides the taste of Jelly.

2438.d: The Royal Gobball headgear will never go out of fashion. Besides being elegant, the bearer gains strength and intelligence.

2440.d: This sword doesn't know whether it's coming or going ... It inflicts all types of elemental damage.

2441.d: This ring increases life, just like the smell of Royal Gobball it gives off increases its charm...

2442.d: They shine, they radiate power, they are fit for a king! Three cheers.

2443.d: This amulet increases strength and intelligence

2444.d: This magnificent belt increases your vitality and conveniently carries all your items. It's so soft that you can even use it to bind your lady-love hand and foot when she refuses to stay home.

2445.d: On top of being classy, this cape, worn by the great Royal Gobball, inspires the wearer with incredible strength.

2446.d: Without any hairs or threads, this cape remains a mystery for the intellectuals of Amakna. At last count there were ten.

2447.d: With this headgear on, the hotties will be queuing up to lick you. It's one of those things Captain Chafer always dreamt of in his own time.

2448.d: There is no doubt that this Brain comes from a Gobball. Well-cooked, it's the favourite dish of young Iops who long to be strong and tall. They also believe it can make them more intelligent, but if that were true, they would stop this idiotic practice immediately.

2449.d: According to hunters, an Army of Starving Ticks can devour a Gobball's woolly jacket in one night. Some mumbling barflies even assure they can get through the magnificent mane of a Sadida.

2451.d: Formerly used as coasters in the finest taverns in the world, the hooves of Gobballs are nowadays made into breakfast bowls by certain stylish Eniripsa alchemists. These are ideal if you like to wake up in the morning to the unmistakable aroma of Gobball dung.

2453.d: In the past, Gobball eyes were made into a delicious soup - so delicious that the recipe had to be destroyed. Numerous people were killed when flocks of Gobballs plummeted over cliffs without the slightest warning.

2454.d: Such a stomach has wonderful elastic properties. Don't worry if there's still a little Clover pulp inside it...  In fact, this stuff works wonders on premature wrinkles.

2455.d: This stuff doubles as bait and weapon. You attract the creatures of the wild with the smell of the stuff, then when it turns all scabby, you use it to knock them over the head.

2460.d: You know how they said that a Gobbly never takes his eye off you?

2462.d: Inevitably, the Gobball War Chief whose brain you removed will speak strangely and make some rash military decisions for a while. In fact, you've probably just signed the death warrant of a whole Tribe of Gobballs.

2463.d: Very few people are skilled enough to extract a Tooth from a Gobball War Chief. Note that this Tooth goes up in value when it's damaged. Don't ask me why...

2464.d: Hide in the forest, watch patiently without making a noise and you may be able to see a Gobball War Chief wagging its tail with joy. But this little gesture only occurs during the mating season.

2465.d: Less gentle than many of its kind, the Gobball War Chief skewers Srams and other reckless species with shocking ease. One can often find pieces of fabric on its horns, just like a small trophy on a proud mother's fireplace.

2466.d: The old expression, "Your breath is killing me" fits the Gobball War Chief particularly well. It's true that one often has the distinct impression he eats diarrhoeic Trools for breakfast, dinner and supper.

2467.d: According to shoemakers, this hoof is one of the most hard-wearing and malleable in the Province. Well it depends what they mean by malleable, doesn't it. Apparently they were going for the rubber boot look here.

2468.d: You will find a few nice surprises inside this stomach. An Enutrof's pinky, an Osamodas' nose...You could almost build your own hero with all the body parts this beast has torn off.

2469.d: There's no need to bite your nails with this ring on your fingers, just lick them instead!

2470.d: These boots are great in summer because they give off a smell of wild strawberries in the heat. Which also masks the smell of perspiration emanating from the hairy toes of an old Sadida.

2471.d: The worst thing about this item is that when you get hungry, you'll be tempted to take a bite of it.

2472.d: This amulet betrays your love of jelly.

2473.d: Classy but not very effective, this cloak will suit young adventurers nonetheless.

2474.d: This hat is not really useful for anything... it does scare the boys away quite nicely though...

2475.d: A small but pleasing ring for beginners which will amuse young children, or Ecaflips.

2476.d: These standard boots are popular with young folk of adventurous spirit.

2477.d: A small belt for budding adventurers.

2478.d: Not too classy or even powerful, but it's better when you've collected the whole set.

2479.d: This hairdo is a sign of maturity for the Lousy Pig. That's why young pubescent Eniripsas can sometimes be seen wandering about the city with the same hairdo. But they wouldn't go into the Rocky Plains like this.

2480.d: "A lousy pig without briefs is a dead lousy pig." Such was the favourite expression of Lady Harre, a disciple of Feca and a dedicated peeping Tom. Her favourite past-time was sneaking up on her friends and putting Lousy Pig Briefs over their heads.

2481.d: This snout, as pink as the buttocks of an Osamodas baby, can certainly be used in a recipe. Or you can maybe make a necklace of snout but you'll have to be brave enough to wear it under the eyes of your neighbours.

2482.d: Once upon a time, a handsome prince found this shoe on the steps of the royal palace. It is said that the shoe's owner had to hurry home to turn the oven off.

2483.d: Some Lousy Pigs have no teeth to begin with. Others wake up one morning gap-toothed, with no memory of how they lost their chompers.

2484.d: Keep this as a memento of the Lousy Pig you just defeated. The problem is that he might hold it against you later on...

2485.d: The MUST-HAVE item, but only in the North-East of Amakna.

2486.d: This Ear will win respect from the people around you. It's a trophy as well as a proof that you can tame Lousy Pigs. But be careful, don't show off in front of other Lousy Pigs because they could take it the wrong way.

2487.d: Ideal for the creation of heavy armour, the Scurvion also has almost unlimited powers of reproduction. Fortunately for the Brakmar armed forces.

2488.d: At first sight, these entrails don't look very appetizing. Fair enough. Scurvion entrails are actually revolting, even when cooked with loving care.

2489.d: This elegant cape will make you irresistible to all the noobs out there.

2490.d: It's quite rare to get a Scurvion leg in such good condition. Use it wisely, to pick the locks on doors for example...

2491.d: Have a look at this intriguing Eye - instead of your reflection you'll see your counterpart, your Dopple. It's completely baffling.

2492.d: This damned Chain comes from an Ouginak, obviously. It was probably used to tie the Ouginak up so that it couldn't escape, before it was broken.

2493.d: This heart will remain faithful to you. As long as you don't sell or exchange it, it will stay in your bag. What a lovely thought!

2494.d: An ultra-powerful blow must have been necessary to crack this Mythical Sword into pieces. The person holding of the weapon can't help roaring with joy! Woohoo!

2495.d: This Eye glows in the dark even once extracted from its owner's face. It's so bright you can read your favourite comic books all night long.

2496.d: Carefully cut, the Kolerat Tail tastes like a sausage. The weird thing is, when you cut out big slices the sausage taste disappears. Another existential culinary enigma in this world.

2497.d: Put it near your ear and you might hear the sea.

2498.d: The Vegamu attracts swarms of Moskitoes that mistake it for one of their friends. They are always disappointed when they see this character.

2499.d: The Kolerat has an incredibly good nose, not as good as the Ouginak, but even so it can smell predators within a radius of 300 meters. Very convenient for avoiding predators.

2500.d: You did good picking it up, it's intact. Dead but intact.

2501.d: God Osamodas can't stand people who hunt wild animals. "They are so cute!" he yells. Well, he has obviously never been torn to pieces by one of these 'cuties'.

2502.d: Whitish Fang Paws are highly prized by Amakna's gourmet chefs. They share their magical properties with whoever puts them on... If you put them on, however, you'll quickly find that luck is not as random as you.

2503.d: You'll be as mischievous as an old Whitish Fang with this rag on your block. If you've always dreamt of wrapping a cloth round your head and walking like a drunken cat, you have no worries. If that is the case, though, I think you have more to worry about than what hat to wear.

2504.d: This tongue certainly explored many dark places before you got your hands on it.

2505.d: To attract a Whitish Fang into the bonds of domesticity, throw him a Croquette - they go crazy for them. He may not tell you, but you'll be friends for life.

2506.d: You can hear the Plissken from a great distance thanks to its bell. And fortunately so, because it isn't easily visible in the luxuriant vegetation of the Cania Plains.

2507.d: You can whip your friends with this Tongue. The followers of Osamodas and the Sacriers will be very pleased.

2508.d: This dreadful venom can wipe out a whole army of furious Gobballs, just pour some of it onto a staff and start a-swipin'!

2509.d: That this tooth once belonged to a Plissken is unmistakable. It's plain to see from its dangerously sharp tip.

2510.d: This stomach is big enough to hold many things. A heaven-sent opportunity for a Iop to sort its Swords out.

2511.d: Despite its high quality,  shoemakers refused to use this leather for many years. Customers thought it was fake because it has no smell! As they say, never judge a boot by its odour.

2512.d: Many Brakmarian poachers collect this hairy trophy. The reasons why are still unknown nowadays.

2513.d: Contrary to its leather, Plain Boar's fabric has a smell that should never be sniffed. It could rouse a Sadida from hibernation.

2514.d: The Hooves of Boars are generally covered with mud or dirt but sometimes with colourful Biblops, which is not that unusual. The Plain Boar hates Biblops as much as you do.

2515.d: At first sight, this snout doesn't look very fresh. But don't be mistaken, it's the most tender and most refined snout that ever did sniff.

2516.d: This Plain Boar Tusk will you remind you how unpleasant this type of boar is. Indeed, the Tusk is as worn as a nibbling Wabbit tooth.

2517.d: This cape used to belong to a famous hero who was famous for confronting the terrible Doctor Wily. This beast wanted to invade and dominate the World of Twelve with his army of summoned creatures. The good Doctor died before his minions had finished eating what he called 'the last supper'.

2518.d: Silvia sewed this bizarre cape from old curtains. Fortunately, you can't really tell since it looks more like a mop that's been boiled in Lousy Pig blood.

2519.d: This helmet is perfect for excelling in the most extreme situations and the most exclusive company.

2520.d: This helmet once belonged to the old Jojo, a renowned hero of times gone by. Though he is world-famous for his epic travels, it is still hard to understand the legendary devotion of his fans.

2521.d: Roll, the boot owner's lovely sister, specialised in astral taxidermy. Long ago, no one knew the difference between astral taxidermy and regular taxidermy. Nowadays, it's easy to see that astral taxidermy is the involves stuffing astral creatures. If you still can't understand where they went wrong, you obviously don't know just how stupid they were.

2522.d: These boots enabled the famous Jojo to perfect his famous roundhouse kick, which was known as "Hot Red Kick". No one knows where this name comes from since his boots were unmistakably white!

2523.d: This belt has been especially designed to protect the hips of our valuable heroes. Totally useless to you then.

2524.d: Rumour has it that this belt was created by Captain Blooe himself. Isn't that incredibly... incredible! You do believe me, don't you?

2525.d: Without its Heart, his song is going to take a turn for the worse. But don't say a word, Lord Crow is very sensitive.

2526.d: This Scythe was originally designed to cut down Iops, but Lord Crow realised that harvesting grain was just as profitable as harvesting blood-thirsty warriors.

2527.d: Lord Crow is just full of surprises! For example, he always carries a Clakoss - the famous royal cheese, in his pocket. He must have really loved this stuff, because its stench would bring a tear to the eye of a Bonta sewer rat. All I can advise is that you leave it in your fridge if you ever happen to get a taste for it.

2528.d: You have to be powerful and fast to take a Nail from a Kaniger - powerful to extract it and fast to avoid getting your ears bitten off.

2529.d: This potion gives a little reality back to an ethereal blade.

2530.d: A bit heavy but really pretty, you'll be the queen of the night with these Caraboots on.

2531.d: Just like you, turtles have very small heads. How convenient! This cap is just the right size for both of you.

2532.d: A practical, well-made cloak. It won't make a champion out of you, but then again, I can't think of anything that would make a champion out of you...

2534.d: Ideal for keeping cool in those hot summers on Moon Island, as well as ideal to cool down the advances of your more eager paramours, this cape will satisfy all the needs of the modern adventurer.

2535.d: This Ice Kwak headdress will keep your head full of fresh and brilliant ideas. And before you say anything, it doesn't work on Iops.

2537.d: Ideal for toning your hips, this belt will allow you to keep cool below the belt too.

2538.d: This potion gives reality back to an ethereal blade.

2539.d: This potion gives a little reality back to an ethereal carving.

2540.d: This potion gives reality back to an ethereal carving.

2541.d: This potion gives a great deal of reality back to an ethereal blade.

2542.d: This potion brings you home whenever you want.

2543.d: This potion gives a large amount of reality back to an ethereal carving.

2544.d: Dreadfully sharp and incredibly classy, this blade will make your Crow friends jealous.

2545.d: With these boots you'll feel incredibly light and peculiarly ridiculous.

2546.d: Thanks to this magnificent helmet, you'll have all the class of the notorious Lord Crow.

2547.d: Long ago, the best Tailors of Amakna united to scavenge the remains of Lord Crow and make the greatest cloak the world has ever seen. It looks incredible draped grandly over your shoulders, but for some reason, it gives you the strong urge to eat cheese.

2549.d: This tin contains a Kaniger cut into pieces. Very convenient to carry, a Kaniger cut up into pieces is really a man's best friend.

2550.d: This fabric is a perfect and beautiful hair replacement. With this on, no one can fail to notice you!

2551.d: The favourite dish of the Ouginak - Kaniger ears with plain sauce. Traditionally, it should be cooked with a lot of wild mint and some Nails for texture.

2552.d: Kaniger Eyes have become a fashion phenomenon - just look at the number of adventurers who wear them around their necks...

2553.d: This, ladies and gentlemen is a reaaal Cannonball. Heavy as a whipped hippy, it tends to make holes in the skull of anyone who gets too close. Not the best idea then.

2554.d: Lousy Pigs Chops have a special taste. Some people cook them with a spicy juice, others eat them raw. As for the Lousy Pig, he will prefer your chops. To each his own... recipe.

2555.d: The Lousy Pig is a weak old beast but he has a hard time coming to terms with the fact. We know this because he stuffs his saddle with feathers so it's more comfy. It's like they say, the proof is in the padding.

2556.d: Blop pollen causes all mild allergies in the world. What is more worrying is that all lethal allergies begin with mild allergies. In short, don't keep this pollen in your pockets if you don't need it.

2557.d: As strange as it may seem, Blop Petals are not edible, neither when cooked nor raw.

2558.d: You did good picking it up, it's intact. Dead but intact.

2559.d: A mane of hair like this one is hard to find. Rich Enutrofs use it as hair replacement.

2560.d: This epaulette is best when admired from afar... and when it's still on the shoulder of the Trool!

2561.d: As if a Trool needed a Bracelet of Strength! This incredible bone-grinding machine wears one bracelet on each wrist.

2562.d: By the look of his briefs, the Trool apparently sits down anywhere and everywhere. There's only one way to find out what age it was... now clear that nose kid...

2563.d: This wedge is a foot for the Trunknid and the foot serves as a wedge. Quite simple!
