6687.d: This tuft of hair belonged to a Cra.

6688.d: This tuft of hair belonged to a Sadida.

6689.d: This tuft of hair belonged to a Sacrier.

6690.d: A pair of damaged scissors, nothing more...

6706.d: These wrappings are as old as their owner who is himself as old as these wrappings. With the passing of time, they have become soaked with Mummy Nova's magic powers... and the smell of her decaying flesh.

6707.d: This stench-soaked cloak is made from pus-impregnated Mummy Nova Bandages. Enough to have the inhabitants of cemeteries for miles around turned on in their graves.

6708.d: This certificate celebrates the date of your last victory over a Dopple.

6712.d: This magnificent cape smells like fruits of the forest. Not enough to drive a Craette mad about you, but enough to drown the stink of a sloppy Sadida.

6713.d: Soaked with the blood of the terrible Lordsoth, these daggers helped him bring down the Chafer King during the famous dagger throwing contest at Troolmusement park. The Chafer King never again revealed his leather briefs and went into exile with the illustrious Captain Chafer in the surroundings of the Pandala cemetery.

6716.d: This pinchy little monkey seems to like you now. It's very docile but it has a huge appetite. It'll only eat things that are native to its own island.

6717.d:
Take this dog to the park, take him to the toilet, show him to your friends, but whatever you do - and please listen carefully - do not feed him. This pet will remove your arm up to the elbow. 
(THIS LEGENDARY PET DOESN'T NEED TO EAT)

6718.d:
The fairer sex of the fairest class will fall under the spell of this cuddly little ball of fluff. For this reason alone it's to be avoided.
(THIS LEGENDARY PET DOESN'T NEED TO EAT)

6719.d: This strange headgear used to belong to the notorious Bearman. Sewn from the remains of the head of a decomposing bear, the headgear will itself turn heads thanks to the unmistakable whiff-trace that follows you wherever you go.

6720.d: This beautiful cloak has been worn for years by the famous Bearman. It won't turn you into a bear, but you will be able to rival the greatest of fighters.

6721.d: These boots are lined with bear fur: even the coldest-blooded creatures will have toasty warm feet.

6722.d: The Bearman has vowed never to take off this wedding ring in memory of his dead wife... the besotted groom summoned a bear to impress his newly-wed love. She went to give it a hug... the summoned bear, raised by a distant father and an abusive mother, thought she was trying to beat him... you can guess the rest... The most tragic thing about this story is that Bearman hadn't made a single payment on the ring. Man, that has to hurt!

6723.d: The Bearman was wearing this necklace around his neck when he faced the hooligans of Bimdhul's lair. Legend has it that the amulet saved him, but on close inspection, you can see why it's just a legend.

6724.d: This little bear hair-covered belt will hide your love handles perfectly. You should wear it always to avoid disappointing your spectators.

6725.d: The Bearman used this staff to tame his summoned Bear and from time to time, to rap his children's knuckles when they didn't do their homework. Here's a man who understood the value of education.

6731.d: With this amulet around your neck, you might fool yourself into thinking people won't smell your breath. No chance!

6732.d: Long ago this small ring was much sought after by Enutrofettes who preferred to use it to decorate their toes. An excellent way of hiding their warts.

6735.d: This tiny root perfectly embodies treachery. Nobody knows why, but everybody knows.

6736.d: This small Ambusher bud contains a sticky and syrupy sap. If you have the misfortune to walk on an old Ambusher hidden in the long grass, you may remain caught until it devours your boots entirely. On the other hand, if you manage to take an intact Ambusher bud, you will be able to hush a moaning Feca by pretending it's chewing gum.

6737.d: The Ambusher doesn't really have real branches like any self-respecting tree. However it has a thin bark that is quite hardy and covered by a vast number of bumps. Very practical for creating tool hilts that do not slip through the fingers, or for beating the behind of the most insolent children. In both situations, you are completely satisfied if you are the one who is holding the hilt.

6738.d: This huge skull is testimony to the appalling dental hygiene of Chief Crocodyl. The funny thing is it still seems to contain some magic power since it is still inhabited by the Chief Crocodyl's soul. Sometimes it even sheds crocodyl tears if you're very nasty to him.

6739.d: Actually getting a complete piece of Crocodyl skin is almost a miracle. Most of the time, poachers only collect a few scales. Ideal to make bags, this old skin will also be appreciated by tailors who make fighting-underwear.

6740.d: This skin, made up of many scales, is superior to any other classical Crocodyl skin. Indeed, the outward side of the Chief Crocodyl skin is stronger and covered with dangerously sharp scales while the inward side is particularly soft. The story goes that some old tailors take one side for the other when they make underwear. It does not say if they get more or less customers as a result...

6742.d: This amulet is made of a mixture of Ambusher leaves and litter from Moon island. It looks more like a garland than a real amulet, but it will help you seduce the wildlife of the island, which almost exclusively consists of abominable creatures. No Ambusher will resist you, they all will fly into your arms to give you a hickey. Only the most unlucky in love will appreciate this piece.

6743.d: Take some Ambusher leaves, pile them up, let them macerate in stale alcohol, pierce them, drink the left-over alcohol, stick the leaves around a piece of bark, fix some pieces of Kokoko leaves with a slimy material, and here is a magnificent Deceitful Wedding Ring. It smells really bad and it will be quite handy for you to justify the smell of your fingers overall if you have a tendency to put them everywhere. Especially where you shouldn't.

6744.d: Once you've tried these boots on, you won't be able to part with them. Not because they are exceptional, but because they are exceptionally sticky. A feature they often share with female Ambushers...

6745.d: Outstanding handicraft made of remains of Ambushers and litter picked up along the Moon beaches, in the middle of the foul foam, this belt, when worn alone, will give you a really surprising look. Enough to disconcert your enemies or surprise your beloved, you'll be able to take advantage of this special moment when, for once, you'll have the upper hand.

6746.d: Oto Mustam, the leader of the Brakmar warriors, wore this small amulet long ago... though only at the organised orgies of Brakmar. They say it doubled as a leash!

6747.d: When the wind blows in its feathers, the Wind Kwak feels as free as an eagle, gliding like a dead leaf carried by a gust of wind. In spite of the clumsy description, it really is quite impressive.

6748.d: Judiciously worn, this ring will make your stubby little fingers look a little longer. Unfortunately for some, it only works on fingers.

6749.d: This ring is so light that it could be blown off by the least gust of wind. But don't expect you'll be taken away with it. At best, you'll be safe, humiliated and on solid ground.

6750.d: Cold and sharp, this blade will revive its users' most primitive instincts.

6751.d: "This ribbed blade is lubricated for increased pain." That's what the handbook says... What is that supposed to mean?

6752.d: Ideal for cutting clouds, this blade will also dissect Moskitoes and split hairs.

6753.d: As perfect as ice-skates on frozen lakes, these boots are very useful for keeping your feet cool, or storing your flask. Recommendations? Don't put them by the fire to dry, you'll never see them again.

6754.d: "Nothing's better for the feet than a pair of Earth Kwakoboots" said Rola Ingalsse, the famous ploughwoman. Soon after she somehow shovelled a giant clod of earth into her own eyes and was blind for ever more.

6755.d: Basic but efficient, these surprisingly light boots are sometimes used as wind socks. Listen carefully though... People who find themselves downwind of this improvised apparatus often die.

6756.d: Ideal for camouflaging yourself as a lump of earth, this cloak will help you attack ploughmen by surprise and steal their treasures. It is for this reason that collectors of ancient pottery covet it so fiercely.

6757.d: Light and refined, this creation is also used as a curtain by the most destitute in the region. Mummy Nova herself used to wear this as an evening dress.

6758.d: The Earth Kwak is not very social and is especially hunted for its feathers, as everybody knows. If you wear this belt around your hips, you'll have the Earth Kwak hunters thinking you're an over the hill Kwak. Sometimes appearances can be truer than reality.

6759.d: "The only way to catch an upset old male Wind Kwak is to dress up as an upset female Wind Kwak. Then, the male will try to understand why the female is upset and will try every possible means to satisfy her. Once the male is satisfied with his performance, you should take advantage of his beatitude to fleece him." This is what one can read in part twelve of book three on Wind Kwak hunting. Besides, it is clearly specified that this belt is an essential element to pass yourself off as a female Wind Kwak. You know what you have to do now.

6760.d: This Earth Kwak headdress is so heavy it'll always keep your feet on the ground. If the ground happens to be soft, well, it'll keep your chin on the ground.

6761.d: To keep your hair streaming in the wind even with a headdress, there's nothing like this lovely Wind Kwak Headdress which will certainly enable you to give free rein to your hair in most circumstances. It is enough to take the most blasé of Chafers aback.

6762.d: "For a punch-up, there's nothing like an Ambusher-up." This is what could be read on the A-Team Travel Agency's advertising leaflet. The agency offered to rebuild this staff for their clients themselves from various resources scattered on Moon Island. Some sort of treasure hunt except there are no maps.

6763.d: As the story goes, the dead Ambushers are very comfortable once they have taken the time to rot under the sun. Indeed, they become much more flexible and softer with time. Many adventurers would like to say the same about their beloved.

6764.d: This headgear isn't giving you the smartest look, is it? But you do  still look less stupid with it on. So just keep it!

6765.d: Warning! As clearly specified on the package you should never give Mimilk to a young Bow Meow - it will ruin the carpets for sure.

6766.d: This apparently simple amulet was made from three magic ears of Corn, covered with the dust of precious stones, and planted in the Snossios plains during the thirteenth harvest of Istrabraq. It gives incredible courage to its bearer, who with its help can reap entire plains and valleys without rest.

6767.d: Shika covered this bracelet of precious stones with a hempen cloth to avoid drawing the Crows' attention while Farle sowed his barley.

6768.d: Take this miserable Bow Meow with you... That'll cheer the little fella up a bit.

6769.d: This magnificent staff has very beautiful teeth on one end, which makes for an excellent fork. Farle used it to make huge haystacks - higher than the biggest Elm growing in the Eltneg forest of old. It is said that Brouce Boulgoure himself felled the tree for this staff, in return for an unbelievable quantity of oat flakes, which Shika Ingalsse himself offered. He used to gulp down fistfuls before spending days on end hacking entire phyla out of existence.

6770.d: This Moumouse was driven out of Grandma's house with a broom.

6771.d: This ring hasn't proved itself yet. It is a unique creation made by a jeweller's apprentice for an important test. It is made from a standard iron ring plunged into a magic Tea solution.

6773.d: This amulet was made in the Tude manner, hence its name. It is one of the earliest and simplest forms of jewellery, and so it is used to train apprentice jewellers. It is true that the thing is not very powerful, but you can't have it all, can you?

6774.d: These hooves have been carved from various rare woods, reinforced with leather pieces of priceless value and padded with magic cereals. Light, stylish and comfortable, these hooves will resist the passage of time. Many misogynistic adventurers would like to say the same about their beloved.

6775.d: This cape, a fashionable patchwork of cloth and leather, has allowed Farle Ingalsse to single-handedly sow entire fields for numberless seasons on end. Once folded up and used as a pouch, its capacity seems to be almost unlimited. Nobody really knows the tailor behind this marvel. All the story tells us is that his business went tail-up when his clients began to confuse his cloaks with floor cloths. What a sad end to a fine career!

6776.d: This belt served Farle Ingalsse as a butcher's apron when slaughtering Gobballs in his makeshift abattoir. A cruel, thankless task which he nevertheless carried out with obvious and undignified pleasure.

6778.d: This straw hat has been made with several plaited magic ears, and padded on the inside with various types of hair and fabrics hand sewn by Farle's wife, Shika Ingalsse. Classier than the Ninnish, and more stylish than the Doddgy, this hat will protect you from the heat as it did Farle through hundreds of long harvests. In this hat, you'll own those fields.

6779.d: Spy Ztiv Oztin's report: taken back with some difficulty from Joe Stonefiddler's very hands.

6780.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6781.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6782.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6783.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6784.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6785.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6786.d: With this basic-looking weapon, you'll feel like you know how to fight.

6787.d: This little form contains the name of a potential candidate for the baker's delivery man job.

6788.d: These cakes are still hot from the oven. You have to deliver them while they're still warm. Do you really think you have time to stare? And wipe that dribble off the crust... Disgusting.

6789.d: This small amulet blooms in spring, dries out in summer, fades in autumn, and goes rotten in winter. An ideal opportunity to change your style with the passing seasons.

6790.d: This form looks like a simple sheet of paper. Get this though - one touch and the paper figures out if the person suits the criteria in the heading! Isn't that nuts?

6791.d: With this little ring on your finger, you'll be able to walk through fields in the countryside. What do you mean you can do that already? Wow!

6792.d: This deflower-shaped staff is made from the remains of wild flowers that were cut down in cruel and bloody battles. All the anger and hatred felt by the poor flowers is concentrated in this tiny tool. This weapon is used by the most treacherous Srams who lure naive females with their 'bunch of deflowers'...

6793.d: This ring has proven its worth, as shown by the little mark made on the inside. It is a unique creation made by a jeweller apprentice for an important test. It is made from a standard iron ring plunged into a magic Tea solution.

6794.d: If you're looking for something to trample those flowers growing in your fields, these boots are just the ticket. Your feet mightn't smell so bad with them on. It's a shame they don't come as shorts too.

6795.d: If you're planning to go to one of those eternally popular BABA theme-nights, this cloak is just what you need.

6796.d: With this petal-peppered belt around your waist, you can slip out of a nasty situation while your enemies roll around the ground laughing. This will take care of the most war-weary Chafer army, and instantly reverse the situation to your advantage.

6797.d: If you have always dreamt of being a florist and having rose-scented breath, it's time for you to put this strange headgear on.

6798.d: It has a light, subtle and intoxicating scent... But Sadidas are the only ones who know the true secrets of these flowers.

6799.d: Sharp as a Bwork blade, the Bwork Chief's blade has the advantage of being much heavier. It is certainly less easy to handle, but you just have to make it fall on your opponent and he'll be in two pieces. Lifting it up again if you miss is another issue, but your enemy will surely have run off by then.

6800.d: This cloak is made of Gobball Wool. It's neither classy nor attractive. Don't bother with it, basically.

6801.d:
A pretty, warm, powerfully smelling lining was sewn beautifully onto an ordinary cape. Around your shoulders, or lain in front of a roaring fire like a Gobball-skin rug, you'll find some use for this cape.
Eventually.

6802.d: These very soft earmuffs will keep your big flappy ears nice and warm.

6804.d: Although basic looking, this flinty amulet is endowed with a very powerful magic that can turn a Bwork into a princess... or the opposite, nobody knows.

6805.d: Even your good friends will think you've married a great Bwork Chief if you sport this little thing on your wrist. It's enough to get you a few free drinks at the local inn... Don't be fooled though, they'll be pity drinks.

6806.d: This fragment of wood comes from a recent building. Must have been red

6807.d: These boots just look like ordinary Bwork boots. And yet, they are Chief Bwork's boots. Hard-wearing, powerful, and smelly, they will be the deciding factor in any evenly-matched battle.

6808.d: This white piece of fabric is very soft... and very dirty.

6809.d: This description is of a little girl with fair hair dressed in a dark colour.

6810.d:
This report... reports that no incident was recorded in the neighbourhood on the day of the burglary. 
A dodgy character was spotted that evening, however.

6811.d: Wear this cloak to look like a battle-weary Bwork warrior. It's perfect for stealing lunch-money off the elderly in the village. All the same, if you're in search of a soul mate, you might want to change your approach... unless you wear it with nothing else on... Hey, that's it... that way, you can keep on scaring the elderly of the village too! Kill two birds with the same stones.

6812.d: These purple leather briefs are all you need, you can wear them on their own and still look distinguished, provided that they fit you. You're better off keeping still in them, though -  even the slightest movement will have you sounding like an old door creaking shut.

6813.d: If you really want to look like a weakling, this helmet is made for you. In your case, it mightn't make too much difference all the same.

6814.d: This pile of wood would make a cosy little bed, ideal for a Piwi.

6815.d: Dragonsly gave you this syringe to take a blood sample from Radlu Minite, the Dark Miner.

6816.d: You finally managed to take a sample of Radlu Minite's blood. Mouth-watering.

6817.d: This amazing amulet was made from a Reptilian Shield, from which all gems were removed. As a result, it's a particularly heavy, but very sturdy, piece of jewellery. Your neck will be protected from vampire-bites, as well as from the aggressive advances of female villagers.

6818.d: This flower, once demonic, is now tame enough to make a nice, romantic present. If all you get in return is a blank look, you can always take it home and make some jam.

6819.d: This bracelet looks strangely like a glove... it's not a glove, it's a bracelet.

6820.d: This herb used to be the main ingredient in any alchemist's traditional remedies. It's hardly used at all nowadays. Clover is now favoured because it doesn't cause serious burns to the lips, which is quite an advantage, let's be honest.

6821.d: Made from the remains of a Chief Crocodyl, this weapon will prove very useful if you are handsome, deft, clever and strong enough to handle it. In your case, I would try to find someone who will trade it for a Twiggy Sword.

6822.d: This syringe contains a potent remedy capable of raising the dead. As a matter of fact, some say the famous undead marauder Hyrkul injected it regularly. We can find no better evidence of its effectiveness.

6823.d: This putrid potion could revive a Sadida on a siesta... Well, not quite... Maybe if the Sadida was an infant and just about to wake up.

6824.d: This healing stone loses its power very quickly. In order to focus the power of the stone and maintain its effectiveness, you have to surround it with a metal that absorbs the appropriate radiation. Standard amulets will do the same trick and they're half the price.

6825.d: These beautiful slippers, made of Chief Crocodyl's skin and scales, come with sharp teeth at their ends. Be careful when you play footsie under the table with your beloved, you might tear off her lovely Tabi woollen stockings.

6826.d: This amulet is a healing stone with added vanishing powers, nicely set in a crafted piece of rare metal. Holding it in your hand makes you feel good, all tiredness disappears and your brain is electrified. By the way, when you wear it, you'll be perfectly visible at night too.

6827.d: Joe has entrusted you with the mission of taking this letter to his good friend, Howard the Ibutno. Just to let you know, he's a lop sooooo...hum...well... you know yourself.

6828.d: This hilt won't transform you into a master of sword handling but it can help you on your way.

6829.d: This sword has just been forged.

6830.d: The first day back to school after the holidays is tough for any child, but for Iops, it's as though they die a little inside every time it happens. This bag makes the whole experience that bit easier to bear.

6831.d: Too stiff to be used as a whip, too flexible to cause any real bodily harm, this gem-covered belt nevertheless serves one obscure purpose... Armed with this, you'll never find your pants around your ankles again. Great or what?

6832.d: This beer deliveryman is as important as a security guard. A lot more aggressive, too.

6833.d: These Kamas seem to come from another dimension. They should be quickly melted down before they go back to where they belong.

6834.d: If you've always dreamt of looking like a Crocodyl - without becoming one - then this headgear's make for you. Don't even think about using this headgear to fool your friends and tell them you've actually killed a Crocodyl. They'll never believe you.

6835.d: The pouch of questionable Kamas was deftly transmuted by Dragonsly. A sword can now be forged with this metal...

6836.d: Though this sword was forged by Two-Fingers, it still seems too fragile for your purposes. Dragonsly the Alchemist should be able to do something about that.

6837.d: Light and fearsome, this sword is meant for you. But the final touch is missing - something from the Ecaflips perhaps...

6838.d: Apparently the moon water had the desired effect. This solid sword can resist anything, but something from the Ecaflips is missing...

6839.d: This weapon, on which Meow Meow put his hallmark, could turn you into a legendary Ecaflip, eventually...

6840.d: This weapon, on which Meow Meow put his hallmark, could turn you into a legendary Ecaflip... maybe...

6841.d: This strange fabric smells of bear. You should know that it attracts females...

6842.d: This strange tooth once belonged to an old Bear. Or to be precise, to a Bear Summon, which is completely different. Imagine that... You are actually holding a summoned tooth in your hands right now. Crazy!

6843.d: This sharp bone broke during a terrible fight against one of the Bearman's Bear Summons. It was too late to put a cast on the poor Bear's paw who was dying and groaning with pain because of your repeated attacks. You chose to let him die slowly, choking him with Gobball slobber, dismembering him and pulling this bone out while he was still conscious. No mercy for the summoned.

6844.d: Sometimes, the Bearman offers a free waxing session to one of his Bear Summonings to pass the time. He then makes quality underwear with the hairs, which are prized by  lonely hunters for their strong sensations and smells.

6845.d: The rough and hairless quality of this skin is the result of a long and intensive waxing session using boiling-hot oil and a branding iron. Don't be surprised if it smells of burnt eyebrow.

6846.d: An ordinary phial at first sight, this container has a tremendous power that only the Xelors know how to control.

6847.d: A rare sort of grain - rather useless to tell the truth. What did you say? Like a Xelor?

6849.d: Enutrofs are the only ones who know how to use this box. The reason for this is most likely the fact that no one likes talking to Enutrofs. Especially about their secrets.

6850.d: The great thing about the delicious Astrub speciality, Pizznosh, is that you can theoretically eat it wherever you feel most comfortable. In practice, most people tend to ram it down their throats behind bushes for fear that someone will ask them for a slice... Some talented souls can even eat a whole pizza while sitting next to you without you noticing a thing. Fear these strange folk... for they are the Pocket-Munchers.

6852.d: The stuffed toy Kry Babby won at the Trool fair...

6853.d: This wood has the distinctive feature of growing as straight as an arrow, which is handy for storage...

6854.d: A slimy piece of flesh snatched from a poor helpless larva.

6855.d: Fruit of the famous bow maker Enileda's gnarled hands, this small bow is not considered representative of the carver's career

6856.d: These scissors have been specially designed to cut the stems of demonic roses without damaging the petals, even when it bites into your calf.

6857.d: A six pack of this classic brew is the only six pack you'll be seeing for a while.

6858.d: This little form contains the name of a failed candidate for the baker's delivery man job. The small red mark at the bottom indicates that the poor sod didn't have enough strength or agility for the job.

6859.d: This pair of scissors is not much to look at... Their former owner glued them to his wrists and went around giving ridiculous haircuts to Gobballs. It was totally unprofitable, nobody paid the slightest bit of attention.

6862.d: This strange parchment explains how the Bearman learnt to summon Bears. Amazing!

6863.d: The helmet of an Astrubian mercenary.

6864.d: The petals of this rose are so dark that its shadow seems to twinkle in comparison.

6865.d: "Meet me at the edge of the forest for the pick-up"

6866.d: This piece of blue cloak belongs to your attackers. You wouldn't think it to look at you, but you can fairly move around on that battlefield

6867.d: In order to remember at what time you have to harvest the Wynd, you wrote it down on this piece of paper... Remember?

6868.d: A Handyman could use this plank to make something delightful - a coffin, for example. Just bear that in mind.

6869.d: Kry Babby doesn't remember where her home is... You'll have to take her.

6870.d: Nomarow Transplent is now under your control. Take him safely to the jailhouse.

6871.d: Frakacia is now under your control. Take her safely to the jailhouse.

6872.d: Nervoes Brakdoun is now in your custody. Take him to the jail.

6873.d: Qil Bil is now under your control. Take him safely to the jailhouse.

6874.d: Brumen Tinctorias is now under your control. Take him safely to the jailhouse.

6875.d: Akornadikt is now under your control. Take him safely to the jailhouse.

6876.d: Ogivol is now under your control. Take him safely to the jailhouse.

6884.d: This key will grant you access to the Bworker Dungeon. Be careful, it will self-destruct after use.

6885.d: Great for playing heads or tails so you can kill your enemy while the coin spins, this pure gold token will make you happy, but maybe unlucky as well...

6886.d: The cloak of an Astrubian mercenary... what were you expecting?

6887.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6888.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6889.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6890.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6891.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6892.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6893.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6894.d: This super-mighty fighting Bow Meow is the embodiment of super-might. Very impressive. Beware, it can only be entrusted to the care of Game Masters... because they're worth it.

6895.d: Less super-mighty than the super-mighty fighting Bow Meow, this small fighting Bow Meow is still very powerful. This pet remains a safe bet for Game Masters but it's not the least bit house trained and tends to roll around in its own detritus. Don't forget to throw some boiling water over it every once in a while so that it retains its splendour.

6897.d: This Piwi feather was taken from the butt of a hapless Piwi.

6898.d: This Piwi feather was taken from the butt of a hapless Piwi.

6899.d: This Piwi feather was taken from the butt of a hapless Piwi.

6900.d: This Piwi feather was taken from the butt of a hapless Piwi.

6902.d: This Piwi feather was taken from the butt of a hapless Piwi.

6903.d: This Piwi feather was taken from the butt of a hapless Piwi.

6904.d: Love can sometimes be more destructive than war, but that's not what Bworker told you.

6905.d: Opening this pack requires a huge amount of serenity on your part... its contents are sensitive.

6906.d: You will be able to join the Mercenaries using this scroll. The one who receives it will have their name added to the Clan register, as a novice.

6907.d: Enables you to set the alignment of the targeted character as Neutral.

6908.d: Hairy but elegant, this belt should remind you of your lady-love.

6909.d: These are the perfect boots for splashing around in the mud or making big dents in an expensive hardwood floor. It's forbidden to wear them on dance floors, beaches and in saunas.

6910.d: This ring used to be fixed on the legs of rutting boars so that breeders could easily recognize them. Today, you are the one wearing the ring. You can take from with what you wish...

6911.d: This ridiculously small ring will help you overcome your Arachnophobia once and for all.

6912.d: Made from the rotting remains of decaying Arachnees, you'll just love this belt. From time to time, it might come back to life and greedily bite you on the hips. Bloody thing!

6913.d: You'll look like a wild Arachnee if you wear this Arachelmet. What will that achieve? Well, you might scare off some flies...

6914.d: Did you know that Weak Arachnees only have four hairy legs? With only four blows of this axe, you could turn one into an Arachneetrunk. Blimey. Imagine everyone in Amakna doing that. It explains why you don't see Weak Arachnees any more, anyway.

6915.d: This is such a light ring that your hands can perform acrobatic feats when it's on. It's also quite useful if you want to humiliate somebody smaller than you by smashing their head with your thumb.

6916.d: Made out of Moskito skin and wings, this bag used to be a big fad in schools. Today, it is old-fashioned and has been replaced by the Small Chief Crocodyl schoolbag. I don't get it - one, a Small Chief Crocodyl bag is much more expensive and two, it's HORRIBLE. Kids these days.

6917.d: This headgear takes its name from the eccentric Enutrof who discovered it while stripping a sick old Moskito for all it had. Extremely useful for inexperienced adventurers, this headgear will help you seduce famished Arachnees.

6918.d: This small amulet is not as effective as the famous Arachnamu. It certainly looks good, though... To be worn on a bare, hairy chest for a great jewel-in-the-roughage look.

6919.d: The Mush Mush has a reputation for being a nasty piece of work. He'll pester and bite you at every opportunity, and he's very moody. I was married to someone like that once... Smelled like mushrooms too...

6920.d: When a Mush Mush gets married, he gives this wedding ring to his bride. Since the bride has no arms, the ring is put delicately on one of its thorns. If you get hold of this ring, you will forever break the sacred bond between the two creatures. At best, the Mush Mush will take you as his bride to make up for it, and just remember, Mush Mushes spend their whole lives where the sun don't shine...

6921.d: Before the prohibition, Musheadgear was smoked or drunk as tea. This headgear really has it all.

6922.d: The only thing more impressive than a livid Mush Mush is a livid Mush Mush in a cloak. Indeed, this particular cloak is the embodiment of a certain kind of ultra-powerful clothing... pretty ugly clothing if you ask me.

6923.d: This amulet used to belong to the great robber "Thisme" who was famous for his limitless cruelty and idiotic death. A central figure of Eniripsa folklore, he was crushed and drowned to death in an olive press having just come out of jail after a 30-year sentence for the theft of a giant walnut.

6924.d: These sharp daggers are very popular among robbers and very unpopular among the elderly for one and the same reason. The daggers cast spells that let them steal Kamas from adversaries. At least that's the story their victims tell.

6925.d: This beautiful belt is essential you if you ever decide to become a highwayman. Don't wear it round town, though, you'll be arrested on sight.

6926.d: With this prespwig on, you'll look like Debbie Crockett, the most celebrated huntress of the modern age, but a tragic victim of premature baldness. That's not to say that this rat-bitten, off-red wig is any better than a balding nut.

6927.d: This reddish small cloak can be also used as a rug or doormat so that you can redecorate the house on the cheap.

6928.d: This ring, both simple and original, will seduce adventurers who long for the good things in life but could never afford them. The kind who would beat the daylights out of helpless animals and strip them of anything resembling an ornament. There's no shortage of them, believe me.

6929.d: The Prespic Belt is the ideal belt for keeping your hips warm. It itches like hell, though... you wanna be hard to wear this one!

6930.d: This helmet directly hewed in stone is worth its weight in gold. It will both protect you from the attacks of a Crackrock and allow you to give head butts worthy of that of Desirock. It's perfect to make your opponents go off their rocker.

6931.d: This stone cloak is a bit too stiff, but you'll be grateful when you're in danger of being spat on by a Crackler.

6933.d: Incredibly heavy but equally effective, these rocky boots will give you a good excuse to drag your feet when you have to defend a Perceptor in a fight you know you can't win.

6934.d: This amulet is as heavy as a bulimic Blop. It has not been designed for weak adventurers. However, once you get used to bearing its heavy weight around your neck, you'll sure cut a dash!

6935.d: Wear it on your waist and you'll gain the respect of your peers. Wear it on your head and you'll be the laughing stock of Astrub

6936.d: With this helmet on, you'll be able to pretend to be a Scaraleaf hunter.

6937.d: Your friends will think that you've joined the elite Scaraleaf hunter clan if you wear this helmet.

6938.d: Your friends will think that you've joined the elite Scaraleaf hunter clan if you wear this helmet.

6939.d: With this helmet on, your friends will think that you've joined the elite Scaraleaf hunter clan.

6940.d: Have you ever dreamt of wearing a cape made of Scaraleaf shells? Well, here's your chance! Once equipped, you should feel as if you were a real Scaraleaf and you might even succeed to slide and skid around. This should be enough to take aback a whole herd of Trools.

6941.d: Who's never dreamt of wearing a cloak made of Scareleaf shells? Once equipped, you'll probably believe yourself to be a true Scaraleaf, and maybe you'll manage to move on by way of slipping and skidding. That's enough to take a crowd of Trools aback.

6942.d: Who's never dreamt of wearing a cloak made of Scareleaf shells? Once equipped, you'll probably believe yourself to be a true Scaraleaf, and maybe you'll manage to move along by way of slipping and skidding. That's enough to take a crowd of Trools aback.

6943.d: Who's never dreamt of wearing a cloak made of Scareleaf shells? Once equipped, you'll probably believe yourself to be a true Scaraleaf, and maybe you'll manage to move along by way of slipping and skidding. That's enough to take a crowd of Trools aback.

6944.d: When you'll wear this ring, you'll spare a thought for all the Scaraleaves you have wiped out. You then maybe ask yourself if it is worth this slaughter... Yeah, of course it is worth it!

6945.d: When you'll wear this ring, you'll spare a thought for all the Scaraleaves you have wiped out. You then maybe ask yourself if it is worth this slaughter... Yeah, of course it is worth it!

6946.d: When you'll wear this ring, you'll spare a thought for all the Scaraleaves you have wiped out. You then maybe ask yourself if it is worth this slaughter... Yeah, of course it is worth it!

6947.d: When you'll wear this ring, you'll spare a thought for all the Scaraleaves you have wiped out. You then maybe ask yourself if it is worth this slaughter... Yeah, of course it is worth it!

6948.d: The Scarabelt was worn as an indicator of a warrior's fist-fighting skills. With a Green Scarabelt, your enemy knew you were a beginner. A red one meant that you were a lusty warrior who ate the uncooked internal organs of your enemies just for fun... And the white one indicated that you were really tough. A blue one meant you didn't spend long enough saving up for one of the others.

6949.d: The Scarabelt was worn as an indicator of a warrior's fist-fighting skills. With a Green Scarabelt, your enemy knew you were a beginner. A red one meant that you were a lusty warrior who ate the uncooked internal organs of your enemies just for fun... And the white one indicated that you were really tough. A blue one meant you didn't spend long enough saving up for one of the others.

6950.d: The Scarabelt was worn as an indicator of a warrior's fist-fighting skills. With a Green Scarabelt, your enemy knew you were a beginner. A red one meant that you were a lusty warrior who ate the uncooked internal organs of your enemies just for fun... And the white one indicated that you were really tough. A blue one meant you didn't spend long enough saving up for one of the others.

6951.d: The Scarabelt was worn as an indicator of a warrior's fist-fighting skills. With a Green Scarabelt, your enemy knew you were a beginner. A red one meant that you were a lusty warrior who ate the uncooked internal organs of your enemies just for fun... And the white one indicated that you were really tough. A blue one meant you didn't spend long enough saving up for one of the others.

6952.d: The smell coming from this Boowolf Headgear will handily mask your terrible breath.

6953.d: These boots are coated with Boowolf hair. They are extremely useful for cleaning dusty wooden floors or fixing up the heads of your enemies as they lie dead on the battle field.

6954.d: This Boowolf fur makes for excellent protection against the cold... and also adventurers with a highly developed sense of smell.

6955.d: Used as a whip, this thong can be a lot more efficient than it looks to motivate your fellow travellers when they've lost the will to live.

6956.d: Beware! This ring will make your finger stink. Although this foul smell may cover a worse smell... This may be the best thing that could happen to your finger... and your hands in general in fact.

6957.d: This sword used to cut the granite blocks for the city walls of Bonta and Brakmar. Nowadays, it's used to crush creatures in battle.

6958.d: Eternally fashionable, this hat will give you a unique look - a long, discreet look up the skirts of the Cra women. Perfect for those warm summer night parties.

6961.d: This ring is as popular with dentists as it is with gangsters. They both use it to  break the teeth of careless people... They both use similar drills too, but let's not dwell on that...

6962.d: We won't spoil the surprise and tell you what's inside! Just have fun my friend and don't party too much!

6963.d: These incredibly big balls are delicious. You'll think there's no end to them, but isn't that a good thing?

6964.d: This rice-based potion enables Brakmarians to return to their hometown instantaneously.

6965.d: This rice-based potion enables Bontarians to return to their hometown instantaneously.

6966.d:
(Double click to learn the spell)
This scroll will teach Srams the class spell 'Jinx'.

6967.d: Use this parchment to promote a Mercenary to Apprentice.

6968.d: With this parchment, an apprentice Mercenary can be promoted to Mercenary.

6969.d: With this parchment, a Mercenary can be promoted to Great Mercenary.

6970.d: With this parchment, a Mercenary can be promoted to Master Mercenary.

6971.d: This hat is quite a good replica of the famous Clint. It will perfectly suit mercenary disciples who are convinced they are master material.

6975.d: This ultra-powerful hat is the Mercenary emblem. It has the power to protect you from both the rain and the sun... a good start at least.

6978.d: From a distance, this creature looks just like a Bow Wow. A simple glance at its head and you can see it's been through terrible trials... which eventually led it to become a vegetarian and to subscribe for life to the Pet Sanctuary Foundation. As such, it will only eat vegetables and plants that grow on Pandala island.

6980.d: This Dofus was laid by a dragon which decided to remain anonymous. Even the wisest adventurers still wonder why.

6981.d: The blade of these daggers is made of ice. Reminds me of an old incident that had the detectives working overtime... A fella called Tum Sellick stabbed his buddy with one of these things over a couple of Kamas... Nice crime... They found the novelty ice-cube maker in his house though... NICKED!

6982.d: These daggers are soaked in the blood of various evil creatures, such as children. They are very special.

6983.d: Only sharpened once every ten years, these daggers retain their lethal edge because of the dark magic that possesses them. They can sometimes be seen walking the streets at the weekend, playing loud music and staring threateningly at passersby.

6984.d: These daggers belonged to a Sadida whose dazzling ascent will be remembered forever in Amaknan history. From a young age, this Sadida dedicated his humble life to Gobbly hunting... the villagers found it hilarious... word spread and soon folk came from all around to watch him hunt those ridiculous balls of wool. His revenge was terrible and long-lived. When the price of Gobbly skins skyrocketed, he became so rich that he paid to have every last villager who mocked him hunted down and murdered. He's storing their skins too, but the stock market isn't going his way.

6986.d: This shield has seen a few battles too many, in this state it is good for nothing. Perhaps Bouwada, in Pandala village, could replace it for you.

6987.d: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 50 souls using this soul stone.
6987.n: Risky Soul Stone for Small Souls

6988.d: The sister of a wild Xelor who was kidnapped by unscrupulous slave drivers used to wear this thing for her nightly shows, the nature of which I will not repeat here.

6989.d: This hat was made a long time ago by apprentice tailors who wanted to protect themselves from the violent fits of rage of Mirko, their boss. This fine business man was often forced to kick his apprentices in the head when they didn't work fast enough. From what I've heard, that was far too good for the lazy bast...

6990.d: This hat is a tribute to the distant cousins of the Moskitoes: the Moths. A lot bigger and a lot kinder than the Moskitoes, the Moths took such good care of their livestock that they soon became extinct from self-inflicted famine. From this tragic story, we have the common insult 'Moth' as in, 'Poor bloody Moth', which describes a fellow who discovers his spouse is devastatingly gluttonous...

6991.d: This strange-looking hat looks like a big dehydrated rotting fruit... A bit like you after a night out at the pub.

6992.d: An improved version of the famous Kanniball mask, the Kannipiwi will make you look like a real Piwi hunter to your friends.

6993.d: Lonard Kohen, the famous minstrel with the voice of a castrated Crackler (which is still incredibly low) was burnt alive in front of the bank of Bonta after causing a moral scandal with his latest, and last, song "Tower of Thong". A full recording was made of his cries of agony, which he had the vision to frame in C#m, modulate to Fb, and resolve in a risqué but manageable G#. Niiice.

6994.d: This hood-cloak hybrid is just amazing. If it was made of leather, Captain Chafer would have loved it.

6995.d: You just can't stay inside this cape, it'll throw you out whether you want to go or not.

6996.d: Stradamus was an old drunken Enutrof who could read the future in pints of beer. Legend has it he was buried standing up in a wall of the Brakmar inn upon his own request, "so that no drunkard can ever spill his beer over my grave". This has been told at least once a week by every drunk in every inn in Brakmar. That's a lot. God I hate that story.

6997.d: The woman who created this ring was convinced the end of the world was near due to plummeting food supplies. She used to spend entire days engraving messages on wooden tables with her motto 'No steak but what we bake'. Time proved her wrong.

6998.d: This small wedding ring will fit an Eniripsa's little fingers perfectly. For Iops, however, it's almost unusable. Their fingers are too fat and they can't get it into their heads that it's not a bracelet.

6999.d: Lahilama was a great spiritual guide who kept his temple right in the heart of the mountains. He was so bored that he spent his days sewing little yellow hats for his disciples. They just had nothing to talk about. They all slowly went mad years of awkward conversation.

7000.d: This ridiculous little piece of bamboo has the strangest magical powers. It used to be worn by young Pandawas, once their puberty came to an end. You might want to wait another couple of years yourself before you slip it around your neck...

7001.d:
"I, I am the kheeng, you, you are the quheen, whee can be heeroes just for one daaaayyyy..." 
Davyd, famous minstrel, was singing his head off on his way back from Moon Island...

7002.d: This amulet of Bamboo resin will spread a nice smell all around you. It comes in handy when you're practising your Wind of Panic.

7003.d: This Talisman was created with stardust and precious stones, encased in Ancestral Treechnid Amber. The mixture can be quite explosive, so it is not recommended you try to make it yourself. Leave it to a Jeweller you don't like.

7004.d: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 100 souls using this soul stone.
7004.n: Risky Soul Stone for Average Souls

7005.d: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 150 souls using this soul stone.
7005.n: Risky Soul Stone for Big Souls

7006.d: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 200 souls using this soul stone.
7006.n: Risky Soul Stone for Huge Souls

7007.d: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 50 souls using this soul stone.
7007.n: Regular Soul Stone for Small Souls

7008.d: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 100 souls using this soul stone.
7008.n: Regular Soul Stone for Average Souls

7009.d: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 150 souls using this soul stone.
7009.n: Regular Soul Stone for Big Souls

7010.d: This soul stone contains the souls of a group of monsters whose only wish is to come back to life to tear your body to pieces. It can only be used in special arenas, located in big cities.

7011.d: This cloak is made of red beard hair... it is quite unique. Animated by extraordinarily powerful magic that renders it all but living, it adores playing practical jokes on the unfortunate bugger who puts it on. It's favourite trick? It unfindably conceals itself when it senses you need it most. If you do ever manage to discipline it, it can be very powerful in fights. As the Wabbits like to say it's a "weal good instwument of wawfawe".

7012.d: This Amulet is, in fact, a candy. It might have been edible if it hadn't been carefully rolled under female Bworker armpits for 36 generations as part of some bizarre ritual.

7013.d: Unlike reed, bamboo can break when bent. Most of the time, it's the teeth of a careless adventurer that will break first. These bloody dentists even have nature on their side... I tell you.

7014.d: You wouldn't think to look at it, but this wood is sacred. Normally, only the finest Pandawas can get their hands on a piece but sometimes, sometimes, lumberjack tourists take a little souvenir of their trip to Pandala island. Bloody tourists.

7015.d: Being completely tasteless, these bamboo shoots are not a popular foodstuff. You should cut them down with a well-rusted scythe and marinate them for a couple years in Greedovore juice before you serve them up to your friends. Another tip from unscrupulous restaurateurs willing to feed you anything at all.

7016.d: Walloh, a young Pandawa once asked his father: "what's the difference between Bamboo and Dark Bamboo daddy?" His dad slapped him in the face for asking such a stupid question. Everyone knows that the difference between Bamboo and Dark Bamboo is the size of their seeds.

7017.d: Walloh, a young Pandawa once asked his father: 'what's the difference between Bamboo and Golden Bamboo daddy?'. His dad smacked him for asking such a stupid question. Everyone knows that the difference between Bamboo and Golden Bamboo is the size of their roots.

7018.d: Either sticky or slimy, rice is a long-time favourite with young, starving Pandawas.

7020.d: Some say it's the oldest known flower. It symbolizes fertility as well as detachment since it can submerge itself in water without getting wet. Some Pandawa Chiefs use this symbol to make their followers understand they have to live their life in the world without falling under its influence...

7022.d: This Staff belonged to Sangroku's grandfather, Sangrokrane, famous for his big head. Legend says this magic staff has the ability to stretch to any length desired... use it to flatten your enemies or stick it down your pants, you're always a winner with this thing...

7023.d: This stone is usually found around Pandala Island. Pandawas are convinced it has special powers. Just like the rumours about Iops and their hidden intelligence, no one has proven this myth.

7024.d: Batches of this weird-looking stone were once used feed the young Crackrocks of Pandala breeders. Believe it or not, the stones are now endangered, so this practice has been discontinued.

7025.d: This stone has been named after a Pandala river in which great quantities of it used to be found. But times have changed and the intensive exploitation of the past now means it is difficult to find.

7026.d: This precious, slightly blue, transparent stone is so bright that it can hide the most ravine-like wrinkles when worn as a necklace. Pandawas even tell tourists: "With this stone, keep your man happy and watch with pity the ravages of time misshape your loved ones." A nice way to kill two birds with one stone!

7027.d: For some dubious reasons, Topaz is still the most popular jewel among jewellers. It attracts quite a lot of Crows in the Cania Plains.

7028.d: This stone has been named after a very famous female Pandawa: Agathe Pahtes. She could be found in places of debauchery such as the Sufokia Pirates' Pub, where she spent her last years dancing, chained up to a big mast in the middle of the pub.

7029.d: Sangroku ate way too many magic beans one time. Forever more, it was a constant struggle to restrain the winds of panic that erupted from his britches without the slightest warning... Those very same winds made him famous the length and breadth of Amakna.

7030.d: Once shaved, Kaniger skin is very soft, a bit like a female Sadida's.

7031.d: Poor Flooey lost his mind after a terrible fight against Many. Fortunately, his amulet didn't suffer. It kept both its mesmerizing properties and its laxative powers. To be taken only when absolutely necessary.

7032.d: This ore probably comes from the depths of the Pandala island mines where Gardan Framine fell head over heels in love with a female Pandawa ghost. Love really doesn't know any boundaries!

7033.d: Irko, the Dark Miner, had great respect for Dolomite. 'The hard and unbreakable rock' he used to call it.

7034.d: Passed down from generation to generation, this misshapen helmet was even worn by Crail himself. Many adventurers think it has mysterious powers. As with many divinities and modern heroes, the magical powers of this helmet have all the potency of a shoe...

7035.d: This alloy was used to forge blades which wouldn't rust when in contact with the blood and drool of its victims

7036.d: A shiny alloy, Brassic is tolerated by bankrupt jewellers who can't afford precious stones. They usually make very competitively priced alloys. Comes in handy when you want to marry for money.

7037.d: This stick used to belong to Granny Candy, one of the three famous Love Priestesses. Sharpened at one end and shiny at the other, this stick is renowned for its versatility and its annoying tendency to turn up just about anywhere. None can resist its power.

7038.d: This crown belonged to the famous King Jellix, renowned for his unbounded romanticism and his seductive power which left its mark on many female Jellies... Some even say he is the father of all the Jellies of the region of Amakna, proof (if needed) of his stamina and legendary fecundity.

7039.d: A famous Sunday fighter, Frank crossed over into martial arts after he failed miserably at his stone-cutter apprenticeship.

7040.d: This bow belonged to Kuri, the famous Love Priestess and left-hand woman of Granny Candy. Never turn your back on a Love Priestess. One arrow from this bow is enough to tear your heart to shreds, or your arse if you have actually turned around.

7041.d: Also called the Duncan Flonuts, The Soil and Bubble or the Pandawa Trots, the MacSheth is a Pandala speciality! Symptoms: an urgent need to get to the throne, violent yanking on the chain of command and a ruthless desire to evacuate all that blocks your passage...

7042.d: Unlike the Pandawa of Amakna, the Pandawa from Pandala won't make you big-headed, but will arouse an inexplicable urge to throw fertilizer around the place!

7043.d: Legend says that this magnificent Dofus came out of the frozen hole of the Water dragon Aguabrial. Legend does not say if he had a cold that day, though it's highly likely.

7044.d: This Dofus looks like no other... Wait a minu...

7045.d: Pandaburg is a tasty drink which could very slowly make you blind, mute and deaf. How convenient! Pandawas aren't the speedy kind.

7046.d: According to the erudite Hel Munster, this genuine nectar delights the goddess Pandawa herself, making her completely euphoric. Any true Pandawa should give his Pandapilers away to the venerated goddess.

7047.d: One of the more sensible Pandawan traditions goes like this: Clink glasses with your neighbour, throw sugar on your hair and burp the following line - "Pandapils, Pandapils, tralalalaHIHOO!".

7055.d: "It's true that Bwaks have short legs, but there'd be no point making them longer". This is the type of conversation you end up having after consuming Pandneken. That's why Pandawas now prefer to keep it for their libations to Pandawa.

7056.d: This unique hat used to belong to a Xelor grandmaster, known the world over for his explosive theories and his incessant meddling with time. His death was as explosive and untimely as his life... Jealous of his neighbour's hat, whose magic powers were said to be even greater than his, he rashly unleashed a Wind of Panic to remove it forever, forgetting about his own. He was blown into a million little pieces when his hat exploded like a giant firecracker.

7057.d: Bring the assistant to the goddess, he will be grateful...

7058.d: This headgear is made of dead dried Kralove leftovers. Be careful, it can come back to life if you use it as a bathing cap.

7059.d: This humongous seed is filled with a heavy but magical oil. Its shell is said to be unbreakable and many craftsmen use it to enchant their weapons. Others stick wiggly eyes on it and put it on the dashboard of their cart...

7060.d: Lenald the Wise gave you this Pandapiler to bring to the Pandawushu Master of the water path.

7061.d: The water from the source juice-sane-ki-oak of the Bow Meow temporarily turned you into a Bow Meow. The slightest shock will make you go back to normal.

7062.d: You must take Poochan to her future husband.

7063.d: This pretty flower only grows in the Imp village, a bit like an Impette, only not as mean.

7064.d: This magnificent orchid is very well-known for the enraging itch that grips anyone who dares to prune it.

7068.d: This flour is perfect for making cement or even bedding for your dog.

7069.d: This shield has seen a few battles too many, in this state it is good for nothing. Perhaps Bouwada, in Pandala village, could replace it for you.

7077.d: This porous but absorbent yellow shield was made from the remains of a creature who used to live in a Pineapple Mask at the bottom of the sea.

7097.d: This Shield is given to disciples who don't know how to correctly use a Shield yet.

7098.d: This hammer is indispensible to blacksmiths.

7102.d: The Ice Knight was famous for being one of the greatest sword smiths in all of Amakna. Only Liche the unmerciful refused to recognize his talent. Offended by this creature's ignorance, the Ice Knight stopped working, refusing to forge so much as a teaspoon until she agreed to publicly recognize his talent. The Ice Knight worked the bars around Amakna for a  couple of hundred years, but the local economy never crumbled as he had expected, nor did Amakna's military influence waver... as he had also expected. When he finally took up his rusty hammer once more, he found he'd completely forgotten his former skill. This ridiculous sword was his last usable creation.

7103.d: This Wand was used to behead all the ninnies in Amakna. Suffice it to say it's seen a lot of action. It's interesting to note how much it resembles a staff or even a walking stick... It might have even been used to satisfy the wicked fantasies of the owner who named it. No one will ever have the last final word on this sordid story.

7104.d: These flee-flops were used to practice various martial arts. Not quite revolutionary and artistically speaking, a failure, they were only good for running away, a bit like yourself...

7105.d: At first sight, this looks like a simple Amulet but it actually holds a mystery that only a dying Pandawa can understand...

7106.d: With this Larva head round your neck, you look like Stive Irween, the famous modern-day larva tamer.

7107.d: You probably never dreamt of putting your feet right inside the guts of a Larva... But here is your chance... Seize it!

7108.d: This plain bag used to be very fashionable a very long time ago. It is the best example of your ancestors' bad taste.

7109.d: You finally have the chance to look like a real larva. You will be able to openly show the world your larvian lifestyle.

7110.d: This terrific Wand is made of larva guts which are firstly dried, then enchanted and finally rehydrated. It's totally shapeless. A bit like you, except you're not even enchanted.

7112.d: The only way to get an egg like this is to force a black dragon to mate with a white dragon. Although some people paint ordinary eggs this colour at home... You may have been tricked.

7113.d: This Dofus is worryingly similar to a wild Dragoturkey egg... For once, appearances might not be misleading.

7114.d: As dark as darkness can be, as solid as a rock, the Dragon which laid such an egg probably didn't forget too quickly.

7115.d: The Ivory Dofus is incomparably white, which isn't surprising given that Dardondakal the White Dragon whitened it with his breath every morning (an old trick passed on to him from his Dragon grandmother).

7116.d: The enchantment in this ring is very strange - once around your finger, the only person you'll be able to talk to will be the jeweller who made it.

7117.d: A particularly talentless group of cosmopolitan minstrels used this type of ring to keep time at their shows after their original drummer left them. They would all put a ring on a toe, and beat in time. Needless to say, it was the percussion that always let them down.

7118.d: This big moth-shaped ring won't make your hands pretty, but isn't that a good thing?

7119.d: The jeweller who created this masterpiece is no relative of the famous Sword Smith, despite appearances. No one ever understood what the designer said about using the ring...

7120.d: Contrary to common misunderstanding, this ring has nothing to do with the beautiful Karin, whose regular live shows at Sufokia Pirates' Inn raised many a visiting spirit from the dead. The namesake of this jewel is a musician who breeds Tofus in his spare time...  so what, you ask. Well, with this ring, it'll sound like there's a dying tofu attached to your finger.

7121.d: This living ring has a terrible curse that makes even the toughest of adventurers seriously ill. They say it was originally designed to heal the person who wore it, but since warriors brought it to the most disreputable locations in the land, its sense of dignity led it to become more and more dangerous and aggressive.

7122.d: This ring is made for tearful novices. It also symbolizes some ancient, unspeakable traditions. It's made for you! Perfect.

7123.d: For experienced adventurers only. It might shock your family and friends to know it's composed of young, innocent creatures.

7124.d: This Dofus has exceptional power: it can make you drool with joy.

7125.d: This Dofus has exceptional power: it can make you drool with joy.

7128.d: Spiteful gossips claim that this ring is the most useful fashion accessory in the world. The wings attached to it can be quite a pain when you need to get a tissue out of your pocket. Now, Iops neither have tissues nor pockets... so, it's just fine.

7129.d: Don't underestimate this chocolaty treat - not only does it taste fantastic, its shape gives it even more flavour as well. Try a chocolate Ouassingue and you'll understand what I mean.

7130.d: The recipe for the Chocolate Dofus is a must if you want to impress your friends.

7131.d: Many other adventurers dreamt of getting their paws on this jewel long before you came along. Indeed, it's said to have many powers, such as the power to turn fierce warriors into good-for-nothing dreamers. It says in my book to never put it near fire. Doesn't say why...

7132.d: This ring owes its name to the last words pronounced by its creator: "O' Ring Ami! You're such a friend!" he said in a painful but bewitching rattle. It is interesting to note that this Bamboo ring was actually made before Bamboo evolved. Another mystery which will not be solved for another ten years or so!

7133.d: As any Wabbit will tell you - if you don't want to see red, avoid the Mixomawose like the plague.

7134.d: Some say Rabies completely changes the affected beings. Warriors become docile, and calm persons become aggressive. However, persons who dribbled will not change.

7135.d: This is a disease transmitted by Moskitoes from tropical regions. Maloria is so called because the disease can be transmitted by Moskito spit as well.

7136.d: This medal used to belong to a famous Pandawa master at an old martial arts school who taught his disciples the principles of defence using their opponents' strength. His school finally closed down because his opponents were no longer strong enough.

7137.d: This Cape was hand-sewn for one single reason: to stop you from sleeping for weeks on end. It is so rigid that it will keep you standing still and upright no matter what happens. Just don't try to tie your shoelaces.

7138.d: Worn by the most important people in the world, this cloak is famous for its legendary softness which means you don't have to put on underwear in the warm season. An elegant way to expose yourself...

7139.d: The shoemaker loved strolling in the fields, looking for improbable love. Instead of finding her soul mate, she died falling into a huge ditch full of filth, close to the Pig Zone. Her body was found seventy years later, when they finally emptied the ditch. Her brother apparently said: "We all have to go sometime", before falling into the ditch himself.

7140.d: Contrary to appearances, Xena was not a warrior, but a shoemaker. Her generous figure and her unlimited passion for housework strongly suggested a brilliant career in the inns of Amakna. But it wasn't to be.

7141.d: This strange hat will protect you from sun beams, especially when its dark. Be careful though, every thirty years it comes to life and tries to suffocate its owner... It doesn't say when the last time... I wouldn't worry about it...

7142.d: This hat was used by some Xelors to hide their hereditary baldness. Enutrofs used it to hide their wives' faces. In fact, the only male syndrome it doesn't treat is prostate cancer...

7143.d: The Solomonk hat was worn by the Chief of a Pandawa tribe. Experts in laxative potions, low-ranking Pandawas were often obliged to test the potions for the alchemists. When banished to the jungle for these trials, this hat doubled as a chamber pot, reducing their load considerably.

7144.d: This wedding hat has gone out of fashion, its lace is no longer considered stylish. If it was recycled into knickers and worn on a hairy head, it might still get a reaction out of a Chafer.

7145.d: Gaddie, a strange creature from an imaginary world, always stood out for its incredible cunning, its total aversion to plants and its ability to fast for days on end in times of war. A creature that complex to understand was obviously impossible to control. It was abandoned in the depths of the Mines of Kruup where its only friend was an old, Gobbly devouring Liche.

7146.d: This headgear looks like any old wig, but it is powerful indeed. It has one prior owner who had the strange and despicable habit of dressing up as other people, and conning the elderly into signing over items of tiny value. Once he convinced a gentle old man that he was his dead wife returned to life, proceeded to 'remarry' him, had six of his children (which even I can't explain) and then, ten years later, just as they were about to renew their vows on a scenic cliffside, he broke the news. It is said he ran off with three party poppers and a half-eaten ball of Stracciatella ice-cream, laughing wildly... still laughing as he tripped and fell over the cliff and laughing to this day if you believe the popular but unlikely sea shanty, 'The crazy fool took my Stracciatella'.

7149.d: Directly extracted from cocoa beans, this square of dark chocolate is very tasty. Be careful not to eat too much of it, it'll give you the spotty skin of a 13 year old, chain-smoking truck-driver.

7150.d: This hat, strangely named, belonged to a poor Ecaflip who became mute after a traumatic event. An artist through and through, he was compelled to follow a Brewer training.  When he turned 14, he drowned in a barrel of beer and tears. Fortunately, beer was not wasted as the priest who was in charge of the funeral fell into an alcoholic coma for many years before he could take his office right where he had stopped it.

7151.d: On the box of this helmet, it said: 'This giant clay protective headgear will turn you into a giant with a head of clay'. Upon further study, you'll realize the helmet is not made of clay, but of lead. Every year, many adventurers die, trapped under the helmet like nipples under a Chinese fire cup...

7152.d: This basin-shaped hat was used by the firemen of Amakna when there were fires on cereal fields. Nowadays it is mainly used by brewers and pub waitresses who are treated like walking barrels.

7153.d: This huge hammer makes a very loud noise when hitting a Iop's skull as it tends to amplify sound. As surprising as it is effective.

7154.d: This light hammer is designed for small beings. Xelors used to find great pleasure in squashing Arachnees with this implement. Its use quickly changed and it became a little toy for young Iop Handymen.

7155.d: For fifty long years, the famous Captain Adock used this terrible Hammer to slay anyone who got in his way - including women and children. In spite of his legendary bad temper and his addiction to alcohol, he won the respect of all warriors - both friend and enemy.

7156.d: This rusty hammer is perfect for all your smashing needs - pulverize maple trees, atomize Moskitoes, this hammer does it all.

7157.d: This hammer was used to sound the bell of the Church of Amakna every Sunday. In these times of war, it's used much more often than that.

7158.d: This hammer was crafted by a famous alchemist during his sentence in the prison of Brakmar. He planned to steal his competitors' secrets and get rich when he got out. This hammer was the first in a collection of devilish instruments.

7159.d: As the Enutrof philosopher Traincartes once said, "I think, therefore I hammer." It sums up the way this greedy bunch sees the world.

7160.d: Many ages ago, this Bow was occupied with a very dark magic, a mysterious force that strikes fear into both its owners and its targets in equal measure.

7161.d: This bow was mainly used to hunt Plain Boars. Indeed, it is so powerful that it can kill several young boars with one single arrow, provided that they stand still in a line. Well it could happen!

7162.d: This Bow belonged to an independent group of Minstrels mainly famous for their war cries which destroyed their enemies' ear drums. They were firstly banished to Pandala, but after driving generations of Pandawa nuts, they were finally brought to the Great Sorlok to be slowly digested for more than 752 years.

7163.d: This bow was used as a dissuasive weapon. The owner of the Runaway Bow claimed that he was using poisoned arrows so any cowards he met would take off instantly.

7164.d: Light and fragile, this bow appeals to adventurers who are more concerned about appearances than substance.

7165.d: This explosive wand was dipped into the lava of an erupting volcano before being sculpted, and then enchanted. It goes without saying that it's very powerful... despite its ridiculous appearance.

7167.d: The craftsman who created this wand had many apprentices. He made them work all day long. He was supposed to teach them the tricks of the trade but as it turned out, he was a terrible teacher. He always started sentences, trailed off, fell asleep, dreamt he was a goat and started licking the blackboard. I'm not suggesting that there's a link between the last two... I'm just reading the... psychiatric... report. OH MAN, this guy was messed up in the head... Blimey!

7168.d: Once sculpted, this wand was soaked in beer for many decades 'to put a few magical powers into it', as the people who made it said. Unfortunately, it started to rot, but it has a few magical properties... it can lure worms to the earth's surface for example. Are you into fishing by any chance?

7169.d: Ideal for lighting a fire, or indeed lighting up a dreary party. With this wand, you just might get the chance to shine once in your life. An opportunity not to be missed.

7170.d: Creizy the pastry chef was nuts... he married Stufh the Lumberjane and choked her to death the very next day with his fat-stuffed pastries. Ever since, the phrase "Creizy Stufh" is used to express an unhappy surprise after a great celebration.

7171.d: The designer of this wand kept forgetting to pick his kids up at school. Conscious of his absent-mindedness, he sculpted a wand that would come to life everyday and remind him to pick his kids up. After a while, he kept thinking the wand was waking him up to remind him to go to the bathroom. His children were taken away from him not long after.

7172.d: This magic wand is still used today to empty septic tanks, clean out ditches and pick noses. Most informed sculptors will tell you that it derives all its magic from all the filthy waste it's been dragged through... in reality, it's the dirty gunge from your snout.

7173.d: This terrific Wand can wrap itself round your opponent's neck and strangle them slowly but surely. An original and distinguished way of killing enemies you don't respect.

7174.d: This cloak is essential if you want to practice Pandawushu...

7175.d: This medical certificate is essential if you want to practice Pandawushuka.

7176.d: Maxx Evanz, master staff carver, is the fellow who created this little wonder. It can darken the sky with raging cloud and draw the blood of your enemies... even if they don't have any. Legend says it took him nine years to carve. Even your enemies will have to complement you on this beautiful piece of stuff.

7177.d: With this Pandawushu Headband around your skull, you'll be able to scare away young Lenalds pretending to be martial arts Masters. Don't forget to bawl a bit of a war cry to be more convincing.

7178.d: If it wasn't for the incessant arguing over whether this thing is a fruit or a root, it would be an excellent weapon.

7179.d: This book contains the best tourist itineraries in the maze of the Damned Forest... a must! That's what it says on the cover, anyway.

7181.d: Red was a young Sadidette. She loved singing, though she had a terrible voice. She always dreamt of travelling to Chili. She was often sent packing but never got anywhere...

7182.d: Mel was quite unlucky. Her husband was a lazy cad, incapable of assuming his status as the head of the family. She was convinced that incessant nagging was the way to go... "You'll get no strawberry jelly if you don't go harvest that barley" or "You'll get no tobacco till you've sheared those Gobballs" and so on. Obviously, this story has nothing to do with this very powerful root... unless it starts to nag you too...

7183.d: This Root has a purity that is the essence of perfection for some wide-eyed craftsmen. I can tell you from experience that this root is the single greatest cause of marital breakdown in the entire region.

7184.d: This terrible root is mainly known for its capacity to provoke climatic disasters at the exact place where it's been used. Avoid using it to kick your enemies around... It is an abuse which could see you and all your friends burnt to a crisp, drowned in a flood, blown to bits, frozen solid, misted to... well the last one wouldn't be so bad, but just don't use it okay!

7185.d: Using this root during a fight is supposed to be very easy. Nevertheless, it can happen that the root somehow comes to life and does whatever it wants... that's generally when the owner yells "This is not the usual Root 'Een, is it?". Well, it is indeed the usual Root 'Een.

7186.d: On this piece of paper, you can read the last date when you gained a few Pandawashuka levels.

7187.d: This bow is reviled the land over for leading its archers into battle at the slightest sign of unusual behaviour. Drinking loudly, shaking hands for longer than is proper, and wearing hats - a few examples of what can make the bow start shooting wildly.

7188.d: These Daggers are often used to cut the ground right out from under your enemies' feet. An original way to surprise them which often comes to a messy end.

7189.d: This strange staff is an improved version of the famous God Rod. Indeed, this staff was designed and made according to the numerous tests done on the God Rod by the Love Priestesses. This model was even used by Kuri herself, which makes it a unique piece.

7190.d: When a precocious Sramette princess couldn't find a single dagger that suited her, she offered a challenge to the dagger smiths of Amakna: the one who forged her a set capable of killing a Tofu in one blow would spend three nights in her bed... Unfortunately, not a single smith took up her challenge. By the time she found a willing craftsman, a retiree of the trade who never should have started in the first place, she'd been advertising her offer among other things on the streets of Madrestam for 17 years... Let's just say that time hadn't been kind to the proud Sramette.

7191.d: Ramougre was an old Sram who became a jewellery master. He used this setter to perfect his creations as well as to murder his clients when he got bored. He was known for his bad temper, sometimes destroying his setter and his most beautiful creations. Today, when people with these daggers get angry, they pay tribute to Ramougre by cutting off some family jewels.

7192.d: Grizmine never succeeded in properly using this Claw - she was always too drunk.

7193.d: No one but Dark Vlad himself can use this sword properly, but if you carry it round town at least people will know you're not one of those pathetic fools who died under its blade.

7194.d: This bow proves that collaboration between technology and magic can lead to excellent results. This bow was quickly forgotten for some strange reason and its creator, Arkanum, had to close down his store.

7195.d: This legendary sword was forged early one morning by a drunken Enutrof army, deep in the mines of Grimoth. It has a very powerful aura as well as a potent hum of beer.

7197.d: This hammer was used to break chocolate blocks into dust for so many years, it eventually gained a delicious flavour. One more reason to give your enemies a taste!

7198.d: Any old Enutrof will tell you that a well-maintained beard is every woman's dream. This razor is so sharp it'll even take care of that thick, curly back hair.

7199.d: This sword belonged to a butcher called Franky Abatz who used it to disembowel his enemies for sausage meat. I used to go to that stall... Believe me, I made sure the dirty mongrel paid for every sausage he ever sold...

7216.d: Those sandals are given to sick Pandawas for those special emergencies... we're talking the dreaded McSheth, which usually comes a knocking when they drink too much down at the Inn.

They're ballasted at the sole so that you can keep your feet firmly on the ground, most of the time. Good for fighting, terrible for running away...

7218.d: Adin was a young Pandawa who loved collecting lamps, but he was far from being a genius.

7219.d: Those sandals were awarded to young Pandits at the end of religious rituals. Nowadays they are mainly used for tap-dancing championships.

7220.d: Between your fat little fingers you're greedily clutching a superb Lottery Ticket. Hold on to it. You might be the lucky winner at the great draw!
