7260.d: This skin is still slightly covered by a down as smooth as that on the armpit of an Eniripsa but.. without the sweaty smell.

7261.d: This amazing magic piece of Bamboo can move. A tribal legend says that every night it wanders round the village and knocks on the doors of people who abandon themselves to nightly pleasures. Pandawas often chain their Magic Bamboo before going to bed to prevent all kind of disappointments.

7262.d: This Bulbiflor Root is not like other roots. It can be chewed for ages and you won't lose your teeth. Be careful though, unlike real sweets, it tastes awful!

7266.d: This flower only grows on the head of the Bulbiflor, so don't try putting on yours... the substrate is not rich enough.

7267.d: These leaves only grow in one place, on the heads of Bulbush, so do not attempt to grow one on your own head, it would fade very quickly.

7268.d: This shoot can grow on the head of the of the Bulbamboo. Don't try putting it on your head, it wouldn't find anything to eat there.

7275.d: Those Kitsou Nae's hairs are as soft as the rump of a female Trool. Something which can remind you of good memories...

7386.d: These humongous testicles are covered with a very soft down which works wonders in resisting magic attacks as well as the self harm Tanukouï San causes himself when summoning a Tanuki Chan. In any case, what you're holding in your hands is something!

7387.d: Find out everything there is to know about the Mercenaries! This work was written by the clan's founder and Grand Master.

7403.d: The Imps once used this small pointy bone as a nasal decoration. An elegant way to enhance a hooked nose, for instance.

7404.d: This bone is still imbued with a magic that can best be described as 'home-made', so do not be surprised if it comes back to life and tries to find the remains of its owner.

7405.d: This bone is the only thing left from the ghost you've just exterminated. Bad luck for you, it doesn't seem to have any magic.

7406.d: This bone hasn't come out of the Pandora's Box... yet, we have every reason to believe it has.

7407.d: Finely carved, this bone can be used as a hand for a giant clock. Just essential.

7408.d: The first time the Soryo Firefoux broke a bone, he tried to take his revenge on the first man that came along. At that very moment, Jon Lemon, minstrel by trade, was walking and singing when he came across the Soryo Firefoux. No one knows what happened next. The only thing that could be noticed afterwards was that his voice had become even more high-pitched.

7410.d: By dint of bearing the immeasurable weight of their humongous testicles, the bones of the Tanukouï San ended up being extremely tough.

7411.d: This bone could have been used to crack cheeky adventurers' skulls open, or to drive Enutrofs into the ground like asparagus. But now it's in your hands, its destiny risks being a little more modest.

7412.d: With this Pack you'll be able to "mark" one single target that you'll be able to hunt down many times.

7414.d: This fluffy ball of hair scratches, bites, and pinches everything that comes close, including the hand that feeds it! It's a terrifying yet irresistibly likeable and fascinating creature. Be careful, not only is this creature quick-tempered but it's also quite picky about its diet. It only eats fresh meat from hunted creatures.

7415.d: This odd little creature only eats fresh fish. But don't worry, its wholesome company more than makes up for the dehydrated-fish breath.

7510.d: This might be part of the key which opens the treasure chest you've always dreamt of. It may also be the key to your grave.
7510.n: Second part of the Dragon Pig Maze Key

7511.d:
If you think this key will attract your dirty pig-friends, you really haven't got it... The only thing it will do is open is the den of the Dragon Pig. 
Be careful, it self-destructs after use.

7512.d: This trophy proves your love for pigs. Scrub yourself down with boiling water before going home in the evening, unless you want to sleep with the Gobballs.

7513.d: Titude, a modest Enutrof Shoemaker, was even smaller than a Xelor. Legend says he created these sandals to be able to kiss his lady-love, a legless Eniripsa, on the lips.

7514.d: Harry was an old wise man who spent his days fishing on the docks of Sufokia. His great moustache made him look like Danous Kwaide, famous actor of a theatre company that used to play at the Amakna Tavern. All this was only a prelude to incredible beer and meat ball orgies.

7515.d: This cape doesn't come from your Galaxy but it seems to match the colour of your Gobbly-wool fishnet stockings all the same.

7516.d: It was an old, unlucky, bitter Enutrof who first discovered this terrible hat, hidden at the bottom of a crevasse in the Bimd'Oule Caverns. Later, the Enutrof exiled himself far away from the lands of Amakna to escape boredom and discover new horizons. Legend tells that he comes back to his native land once a century to make fun of his old friends... but we all know he's just a bit nostalgic.

7517.d: This beer is so acidic it can hardly be drunk. Indeed, the acidity gives the pint the life shelf-life of an overweight Moskito...

7518.d: This surprising creature comes from the afterlife and is not willing to go back there, unless it takes you with it...

7519.d: This little dragon's skin is as pink as a female Bwork's backside, making it a risk-free and cheap way to fantasize in a private corner or to remind yourself of all those happy memories. This dragon isn't just the object of your fantasies though, it's also a very powerful and wise creature. However, you must be careful, as its hunger for other pets is as great as a Chafer's perversion during a full moon.

7520.d: A retired toy soldier, this metal creature suddenly came to life one day. It will follow you everywhere you go, risking its life to save yours. All you have to do in return is feed the little guy. This doesn't mean he'll fight your fights for you, though... he'll never replace those naive Astrubian adventurers!

7521.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

7522.d: Tamed and cleaned, this baby Minimino can be fed and petted without the loss of fingers, hands or elbow bones. You should remain careful though, as sometimes nature can reclaim control of its tamed manners. There is nothing worse than a Minimino being itself. To be safe, feed it only very rarely and beat it regularly with... well anything hard. Just treat him like you would your own child and everything might be fine.

7523.d:
No tomcat can resist this lovely ginger creature... not even the most happily married of them!
(THIS LEGENDARY PET DOES NOT NEED TO EAT).

7524.d: This surprising creature is the result of crossbreeding between a White Bow Meow and a Black Bow Meow. It only eats fish.

The Dragoturkey sacrificed itself for the making of this cape offered to the famous minstrel Pol Akartney on their wedding day. Apparently Jon Lemon even wrote a song about it.

7553.d: If you ever dreamt of looking like a turkey, this is your chance! However, if you want to remain healthy, we advise you not to wear this hat on the streets of Amakna during the Christmas season.

7581.d: This bag looks just like a magic pineapple... maybe it's a magic pineapple that turned into a bag for some reason. It has happened before. Unlike the Cawwot bag, the pineapple bag has not been hollowed out, so you can't put anything in it. And it's very heavy. Contrary to 'popular belief', this bag is not part of the famous Pineapple set. Yes, I lied to you once again. Hahaha. I love this job.

7702.d: This Bow Wow is in a class of its own. The result of generations of breeding, it's a noble-blooded hunting hound. Its extraordinary nose and perky yelping will help you flush out the biggest game in the forest... It will equally help the biggest game flush you out of the forest... Use with care.

7703.d: This dark bird is especially renowned for its love of cemeteries and white-skinned adventurers. It loves to break the bones it finds in graves with its huge beak.

7704.d: This squirrel is a real acorn twister. It'll tickle your monkey nuts one minute and break 'em the next. The crazy thing only eats seed.

7705.d: This magnificent creature is somehow related to the famous Lenalds from Wabbit Island. More reckless and a lot more unruly, it will help you in combat but will prove incredibly deceitful if you don't treat it well. This creature only eats meat.

7706.d: Bilby, short for Bilbiblabaloo, is a little jelly in search of big adventures. Particularly attached to Vald, it has remarkable powers for its size due to its strict diet of flowers.

7707.d: This wild little piggy has an immeasurably large snout, adapted to sniffing out acorns. It seemed to find you quite easily. This devourer of souls feeds off the remains of Lousy Pigs, piglets and boars.

7708.d: This little Piwin is not like the others, one look at its colour and that is clear. However, it seems to share the same inexplicable interest in pecking posteriors. Don't be shocked when I tell you that some people actually enjoy being aggressed by the little creatures. This pet only eats seeds.

7879.d: Domen's Colossal, Immoral, Unusual Annals will send shivers down your spine. Must be read according to prescription. Side effects: cold sweats and bed wetting.

7880.d: This Amulet was worn by adventurers who said they wanted to make tea, not war. Each to their own.

7881.d: This ring will enable you to cause even more pain when doling out those well-deserved spankings to your little darlings.

7882.d: This hammer is great for expressing your pacifism... all over your enemy's face.

7883.d: Stuffed with Gobkool wool, these boots are just fantastic. Light and warm for the cold season and cool for the hot one, they will please even the pickiest of adventurers.

7884.d: If you're the kind of person who always thinks positive, this cape is made for you. It's so thick and comfy that it can be used as an improvised bed when you feel extremely sleepy. Its smoked Kaliptus odour even repels insects and other unwanted creatures.

7885.d: Wrapped around your hips, this belt will give you the appearance of a peace-loving adventurer. This enables you to surprise your enemies with a dagger in their back.

7886.d: Let's be honest, as headwear goes, this cap is about as fashionable as a mullet hairdo. You never know though, look what happened to drainpipe jeans.

7887.d: This headgear once belonged to the famous Koolich, renowned for his clay feet and his legendary good mood.

7888.d: The Koolich uses this bag to keep its Kaliptus leaves fresh or to suffocate Koalaks that are a bit too enterprising.

7889.d: These boots used to belong to the Koolich - even if you can't tell, you can smell! These boots are so comfortable that you'll almost forget how miserable your existence is.

7890.d: This staff is really an emptied bone of one of the Koolich's ancestors. Pierced on both ends, it can be used as a Kaliptus pipe but also as a shepherd's stick. Ahhhh... sticks, eh! What would we do without them?

7891.d: This little Wabbit is in fact a secret son of the notorious Wa Wabbit. Maybe one day it will be its tuwn to weaw his father's cwown. Ha!

7892.d: Willy Peninzias is a nasty creature indeed. He had a very tough childhood. Since then, he soothes his seething anger by eating any and all stuffed animals he comes across.

7893.d: This Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

7894.d: This Peninzias hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

7895.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Mini Wa you've put in the Bow Kennel.

7896.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Willy Peninzias you've  put in the Bow Kennel.

7897.d:
If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.
(WARNING: this gift is very heavy. You might be overweight when you open it. Remember to take your heavy items off, or to ask a friend to help you.)

7898.d:
If you stick your ear to this gift or if you shake it energetically, you might hear strange noises that will reveal the presence of a living creature. Don't waste any more time! Open it! You'll find a wonderful pet inside it as well as a book which will explain to you how to raise it, some resources it can be fed with and the Eniripsa powders you'll need to heal it.
(WARNING: this gift contains very heavy items. You might be overweight when you open it. Remember to take your heavy items off, or to ask a friend to help you.)

7899.d: This book was written by Oshimo Bigglip. It explains how to raise a Mini Wa.
7899.n: How to raise your Mini Wa

7900.d: This book was written by Oshimo Bigglip. It explains how to raise Willy Peninzias.
7900.n: How to raise your Willy Peninzias

7902.d: An old legend extracted from the famous old book titled "Everything You Need To Know About Women" says that this belt once belonged to a golden lady, a lot more interested in wealth than in power. In the non-censored version of this book, we also learn that she was keen on cracking dirty jokes. I guess she wasn't that different from most women...

7903.d: Delicately inserted in nostrils, these leaves will unblock any nose. Some tribal legends even say that this technique works for other orifices.

7904.d: When you burn it, this flower gives off a thick hallucinogenic smoke. When you chew it, it tends to make you impotent. And if you use it to make an infusion, it will have great laxative effects. The best thing to do would be not to touch it at all.

7905.d: This wool looks like Gobball wool but isn't. This wool doesn't smell.

7906.d: According to an old legend, when you grind this horn down, the powder is said to have aphrodisiac powers. The same legend specifies that it can also have surprising side effects. Another reason to try it out!

7907.d: This multicoloured leather is perfect for you to make multicoloured leather underpants. You'll make the most blasé of Chafers jealous.

7908.d: This key of bone will enable you to enter the Koolich dungeon even if you haven't been invited.

7911.d: This little Koalak seems harmless but that's far from the truth. Tortured when he was young, the bullies' favourite game was to hit him in the face with boomerangs. He hates boomerangs. He eats them whole just so he doesn't have to look at them.

7913.d: This mysterious item, forgotten by the world, used to belong to a great magus... People say it gives you the ability to speak to certain animals...

7917.d:
To make up for the recent problems that you've encountered, the Amakna Team offers you this gift-box including:
- 5 Wise Compensation Candies
- 5 Lucky Compensation Candies
- 10 Energy Compensation Candies

7918.d: This key, made of Tofu feathers, can tickle the inside of many locks into hysterics of... opening. It will grant you access to Farle Ingalsse's Tofu House.

7919.d: You can probably exchange this beautiful token for precious gifts at the Trool Fair.

7920.d: This modest wand allows Game Masters to teleport adventurers into areas reserved for tournaments.

7921.d: This crown is almost impossible to hold... No surprise, it belongs to the Royal Tofu! Doesn't seem to suit your small head, though. I think it just might be out of your league. LOSER!!!

7922.d: This stuffed Sacrier Dopple is just perfect for young Sacriers. It's great for mopping up blood and can even be washed at high temperatures.

7923.d: This stuffed Pandawa Dopple smells like alcohol and wet Pandawa hair... Ah, just like mummy.

7924.d: This wonderful key will allow you to get into the Labyrinth of the Minotoror. It won't help you get out again, though.

7925.d: This scented wood can be used to build nice-smelling houses even if their owners stink. It's a pity it isn't supple enough to make underwear.

7926.d: Use this key to meet Lord Crow himself. If you're lucky, he might invite you to share a piece of cheese in his company.

7927.d: This key is almost unbreakable but it is a little worn from opening so many doors. It looks like it's been created from the intimate parts of a Crackler. Just shocking!

7928.d: Use this key to get into the Pet Sanctuary. You'll find all the pets that died from hunger, exhaustion or torture there as well as those who have been devoured, tickled to death, poisoned with Dragomilk, suffocated in a chest, or simply abandoned on the side of the road.

7929.d: This book, written by the famous Igor Ant, Mercenary Chief of Astrub, is bedside reading for those who respect the law as well as for those who flout it.
7929.n: How To Be A Perfect Mercenary In Astrub

7930.d: Some advice and tips to make yourself nice and loyal friends, written by Acidrik Gutsplitter.
7930.n: How To Make Friends And Keep Them

7931.d: Part III of the Fragments of the History of the World, found by the erudite Acidrik Gutsplitter and rewritten by the same.

7932.d: This year, the voluptuous Miss Astrub reveals the charms she used to seduce the jury.

7933.d: These extraordinary dancers liven up the trendiest parties of the region.

7934.d: Wally Elconom wrote this book for adventurers who don't know their compass from their Zaaps.
7934.n: How To Travel Without Ever Losing Your Way

7999.d: Some adventurers say that this cape is as rough as a Crocodyl's skin, and still others say that it's even rougher than a female Bwork's bottom. Be sure to wear it the right way round if you don't want to be pared to a point like a pencil.

8000.d: This small creature is a Bwork. It was locked inside a jar for several decades. As it grew, it took the shape of the jar and will now be a cylindrical dwarf its whole life. Its legendary good humour makes for the perfect companion when you know you're going to die soon or for boisterous social occasions.

8001.d: This bandage is normally wrapped around the Koalak Warrior's arms. This way, he can blow his nose without using any handkerchiefs. When this bandage is old and worn out, you hang it on the ceiling of your house to catch passing Moskitoes.

8002.d: This fabric seems to be impregnated with an ancestral magic that is quite unpredictable and uncontrollable: another thing in common with your beloved.

8003.d: This amulet does not look like any other amulet, simply because no other amulet looks like it.

8004.d: This beautiful ring is worn by the most foolhardy of all Koalaks... the ones who stole it in Astrub.

8005.d: This bow enables you to steal your opponents' life and sometimes, to steal your opponents from life. (Don't spend too long trying to understand, that doesn't mean anything.)

8006.d: These boots are in fact real Koalak feet that were brutally pulled off their owners, then emptied of their content before being padded with Koalak hairs. Both terrifying and attractive, these boots will make you the terror of Astrub.

8007.d: This cloak will protect you from most attacks, but not from being ridiculous.

8008.d: This Kalitpus leaf belt diffuses a delightful smell, that will hide all others. Besides, this belt is perfect for hiding your chubbiness.

8009.d: This headgear is adorned with huge Koalak ears which has the effect of amplifying sounds. Be careful, it can destroy your eardrums if your friends are fond of the Wind of Panic.

8010.d: Enables you to reclaim any piece of equipment installed a paddock.

8011.d: Some great stories about cults that will delight the aspiring mystic.

8012.d: This powder will bring a ghost pet back to life, provided you know how to feed a ghost pet.

8013.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8015.d: As the name indicates, this young Koalak is still enjoying the blood-red sunrise of its life. Maybe it will never stop growing and become taller than you are. The leash will be round the other throat then, my friend...

8016.d: This Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

8050.d: The little immature Koalak who's skin you tore off didn't want you to treat him that way... but hey, you're stronger and crueller than he is.

8052.d: This old and worn skin used to protect the Koalak Master's behind. It still has some nice reddish traces, ample proof of a crazy, restless life.

8053.d: This torn skin was worn out against that of the Koalak Rider's Mount. Obviously, this is a proof of its good quality.

8054.d: This skin's smell should remind you of that of the sheds of the Castle of Amakna. Very handy for scaring sensitive souls away and killing them before they decide to come with you to a dungeon.

8055.d: Mama Koalak has particularly solid bones that don't break under her weight. The same cannot be said for the famous minstrel Jon Lemon who lost the use of both his arms when he got squashed by Mama Koalak's humongous thighs.

8056.d: Once carved and shaped like a dagger, this bone makes a great a boil-piercer.

8057.d: This bone can be used as a shovel to unearth corpses and strip them off, if you like spending your holidays next to cemeteries. Incidentally, it's also the Koalak Gravedigger's shinbone.

8058.d: Thanks to the Koalak Mummy's numerous wrappings, which give good protection against the most powerful magic attacks, this bone has kept all of its splendour.

8059.d: These hairs are covered with Blop pollen, which gives them a delectable taste, but a foul smell.

8060.d: These hairs are covered with Blop pollen, which gives them a delectable taste, but a foul smell.

8061.d: These hairs are covered with Blop pollen, which gives them a delectable taste, but a foul smell.

8062.d: These hairs are covered with Blop pollen, which gives them a delectable taste, but a foul smell.

8063.d: This ridiculous tiny tail is so insignificant it could only have belonged to you. But this is not the case... consider yourself lucky!

8064.d: This weirdly shaped piece of wood travelled for a long time through the air between enemy ranks before breaking. Rumour has it that it will always fly back to its owner, but rarely into their hands...

8065.d: These hairs are urticant enough to change simple Brown Warko kisses into weapons of mass destruction. Very urticant indeed.

8066.d: These hairs are urticant making this beard a war weapon a lot more destructive than the Bwork breath, if we were to compare them. Shocking!

8067.d: Some adventurers say that these boots enable you to walk on traps without activating them. But be careful, this might be a trap in itself...

8068.d: This splendid cape comes with shoulder pads as standard so you'll finally look like a real champion.

8069.d: With this imposing helmet, you'll become big-headed for sure, if you aren't already!

8070.d: With this low-slung belt around your hips, you'll finally be able to hide that pickle-sized bulge in your trousers. Will that stop the girls laughing? I doubt it.

8071.d: This small creature only follows champions... you might get a few days out of it before it realizes you're a hopeless imposter. From that moment on, you'll be wearing the leash.

8072.d: No one knows exactly which dragon created this Dofus, but the rumours suggest it ingested an incredible quantity of Kaliptus leaves before laying the egg and then dying of acute aerophagia.

8073.d: Rigroulak gave you this key in exchange for the Koolich set. This key will enable you to enter Skeunk's Hideout.

8075.d: This weirdly shaped piece of wood travelled for a long time through the air between enemy ranks before breaking. Rumour has it that it will always fly back to its owner, but rarely into their hands...

8076.d: This weirdly shaped piece of wood travelled for a long time through the air between enemy ranks before breaking. Rumour has it that it will always fly back to its owner, but rarely into their hands...

8077.d: This weirdly shaped piece of wood travelled for a long time through the air between enemy ranks before breaking. Rumour has it that it will always fly back to its owner, but rarely into their hands...

8078.d: A Handyman could use this plank to make something delightful - a coffin, for example. Just bear that in mind.

8079.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.
8079.n: Little White Bow Meow Ghost Transformation

8080.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.
8080.n: Little Black Bow Wow Ghost Transformation

8081.d: This huge bag contains an impressive quantity of Hornbeam.

8082.d: This fabric smells like death, whereas you smell as if you were dead. The difference is worth noting.

8083.d: This bone is quite spongy and enables the Fisheralak to float if it falls in while pulling up a big catch.

8084.d: This scar-covered skin became more resistant than a rock but remained extremely supple. It's the perfect for whips and tasteless sandals.

8085.d: These hairs are covered in Kaliptus sap, giving them a shiny glint. Unfortunately, they cannot be used for haute couture as they smell like rotting Dragoturkey.

8086.d: This weird looking headgear used to hide the premature baldness of the Drakoalak. With a little practice, it might soon be able to hide yours.

8087.d:
(Double click to learn the spell) 
This scroll will teach you a spell that will enable you to cause more damage when you use an axe.

8088.d: This wand, made out of useless office stationery, holds incredible magical powers. Legend tells that it can move of its own will, choose its target and protect its master even when death is seemingly inevitable.

8089.d: Iots was a parrot who repeated just about anything you could say. Rumour has it that this wand was carved from its beak.

8090.d: Legend has it that this staff bites people, or was it that people always bit it? Something about biting anyway...

8091.d: This palm cane celebrates a famous festival in the South East. Unfortunately this one isn't made of gold.

8092.d: The Ostwogoth is neither sharp nor smart but when he has his daggers to hand, no one dares face this monster.

8093.d: Carrying these daggers will not necessarily make a hero of you... they could quickly leave you looking like a heroine if you carry them in your pants however.

8094.d: This sword perfectly illustrates the old Iop saying "In a slain enemy is a sword's hilarity".

8095.d: This conversation piece is mass-produced according to an unchanging style. Since it's also quite deadly, it's often used in combat. In this case, art doesn't imitate life, it tears it out at the roots.

8096.d: Its previous owner used to dance with Moowolves. One day he was wolfed down altogether.

8097.d: Even your enemies will be asking to be hit again and again with this weapon.

8098.d: This axe is really special. Its vibrating blade plays beautiful music while you slice the life out of your enemies.

8099.d: Rumour has it this weapon has been dipped into a fountain of pure lightning and then sprinkled with stardust. Other rumours entirely contradict this story.

8100.d: This axe has been pierced in many different places making it whistle pleasantly while you slice your enemies. As the old song goes 'Whistle while you Whack.'

8101.d: This troublesome axe claims it comes from a mysterious land far away... Don't listen to its rambling, though, it has made peace-loving fools out of more than one fine warrior. What a shame.

8102.d: This rock is said to be the heart of the Legendary Crackler. What we do know is that the Legendary Crackler never had a heavy heart. Therefore, this rock is incredibly light making it possible to create suitable items for characters who favour mobility, agility and protection. Just perfect!

8103.d: This bow is made from fossilised hair of a Sadida who slept for so long that Arachnees spun a film of tough webs around it.

8104.d: This bow is a bizarre colour but is perfect to show off at the Zaap of Bonta. You won't pass off as a rooster, but you'll surely attract all the chicks! Sometimes amazing, sometimes disgusting, it might even overcome your enemies without your needing to shoot a single arrow.

8106.d: This Potion will let you unlearn the profession of Handyman.

8108.d: As light as a Tofu feather, this amulet can be worn around your neck or around your forehead if you want to be original.

8109.d: This ridiculously small ring can end up being essential... your enemies might pity you so much they'll finish you off instead of letting you agonize. Let's be positive!

8110.d: Unlike what some adventurers may think, this wand is not used by Tofus - they're way too stupid to know how to use such a weapon - but to fight them. Indeed, this wand is made of Tofu feathers which enable hunters to simulate the Tofu mating dance and catch them. What else will these terrible hunters invent to satisfy their murderous instinct?

8111.d: Light and soft, these slippers are warm in winter and cool in summer. Unfortunately, they can't stand being washed in washing machines.

8112.d: This weird cloak has been cut in half. But why would somebody cut it in half? No one knows... though everybody has his own little idea about it.

8113.d: This belt is the ideal tool for strangling Tofus but hunters also use it to whip any adventurers who stray onto their land in hunting season.

8114.d: This safety helmet became a very fashionable item that every pretty lady adventurer should have. What's wrong in this world?

8116.d: This helmet will hide your teenage acne or your ugly face.

8117.d: More golden than a classical Scaracape and less black than a Black Scaracape, this cape is perfect to hide your outgrowths. The Scarabugly used to use it to hide its awful hump, for example. These days, this cape is mainly used to hide terrible-looking behinds. No need to point out that this cape is very popular.

8118.d: This magic wand is perfect for dusting old furniture or old people.

8119.d: If you love running naked on the paradisiacal Moon Island beaches, you'll surely fall in love with this belt.

8120.d: Worn on a hairy torso, this amulet just looks fantastic! Hair tufts are just the perfect match for this amulet.

8121.d: Scarabuglys are strange creatures. Born hunchbacked and ugly, they inevitably become the laughing stock of the other Scaraleaves. Maybe that's why you feel so close to this creature.

8122.d: These hooked boots make it easy for you to climb the sheerest of cliffs or to plough your fields without a plough.

8123.d: This amulet smells of Wild Sunflower oil and herbs. You can use it as a lure to trap dangerous rummagers... like Gobballs, or your mother-in-law.

8124.d: With its complementary pair of linen Bermuda shorts attached, the Beltudas is simply a must have. This belt is designed for those who need to get their clothes off in a heartbeat and burst into action just as fast. Be careful though. For reasons of hygiene, it is forbidden to wear it in public swimming pools... we don't want a repeat of the Bonta incident... I almost lost my sight that time...

8125.d: If you need protection from the sun while working in the fields, what you really need is a Slob Headgear. If you need protection from the sun while working in the fields and you're poor, the famous Farmer's Sunhat will have to do.

8126.d: These moth-eaten mittens are a real treasure. They're said to be covered with diamond dust which gives them extraordinary resistance. They are also abrasive on one side, perfect for putting the finishing touches to that latest DIY project.

8127.d: This robust but damaged scythe doesn't cut very well, it's seen far too many harvests. However, it's extremely effective if you're looking to yank some veins out of a rival's arm... Nice and blunt...

8128.d: These boots are padded with wheat straw, absorbing perspiration and allowing the portable and low-cost cultivation of toxic mushrooms. Thanks to their soft sole, they've been recommended by all the great Gobbowl players.

8129.d: Behind this stupid name, you'll find an extremely powerful amulet, made with Boowolf fangs and bones which explains why it smells so bad. If it doesn't suit your neck, it will perfectly suit your breath.

8130.d: This terrible axe has beheaded many foolhardy adventurers even if it does not cut very well. Indeed, a dozen attempts can be necessary to finish cutting a resistant neck.

8131.d: This bag is very fashionable among school kids and is ideal for storing animal and vegetable flours. Once opened, unfolded and torn along the seams, you'll be able to use this bag as a skirt, just shave those legs, for Iop's sake.

8132.d: This belt is anything but original... funny, it seems to match your hairdo.

8133.d: This helmet is perfect for those who see the world through opaque black glasses.

8134.d: If you can't afford to buy a Mastralis Croak, but you like to scare Arachnees by wearing black clothes, this is the cape for you!

8135.d: This interesting key will allow you to drag open the door of the Bwork Dungeon... It can't promise you'll get out of there alive though.

8136.d: This beautiful ring can be worn around your big toe. It's perfect to hide your warts and your ingrown nails.

8137.d: These entrails are responsible for the difficult digestions of the Golden Scarabugly. You are entitled to fry them without feeling remorse.

8138.d: Once upside down, this carapace can be used as an ashtray.

8139.d: This wonderful golden key will grant you access to the Scaraleaf Dungeon. And you thought you'd seen it all...

8140.d: The Black Scaraleaf never knew himself why he was given these antennae. Nature can be cruel sometimes.

8141.d: Unlike what some adventurers may think, Black Scaraleaf Wings are not black, but white. Another mystery Mother Nature gave us to discuss at the Inn.

8142.d: This key will grant you access to the Royal Tofu House. You'll get the thrashing of your life there too.

8143.d: This key will let you into the Field Dungeon... It won't let you out again, though.

8144.d: This small flask contains the virile power of the Moowolf in liquid form. Be careful though, it's not edible.

8145.d: Bwork Beer will render a Feca drunk from 12 paces. No one knows if it's made of Bworks or by Bworks, but knowing the Bworks, it's probably a bit of both.

8146.d: If you like to break a few toes when you take your date out to dance, these boots are made for you!

8147.d: This is an improved version of the Crackler Helmet. This rock will efficiently protect you from falling rocks, but not from hair loss.

8148.d: This huge hammer is in fact a Crackler sword, adorned with a rock from the Legendary Crackler. This shocking creation will stun your opponents, just before squashing them.

8149.d: This rock, set with precious stones, is perfect if you want to leave a permanent mark on the forehead of an enemy.

8150.d: This amulet has quite a modest look though it contains many secrets including the one telling what secrets it contains.

8151.d: This little monster will follow you everywhere and devour the remains of his fellow creatures. By turns terrifying and entertaining, it'll brighten up your long, sombre days. Although it could just as easily shorten your long, sombre days considerably.

8152.d: The Legendary Crackler wears this belt around his toes and you around his waist, or ankle maybe...

8153.d: This young Treechnid could no longer stand his family, and like yourself, has decided to rebel. Today, he's coming with you to count how many of his close relatives you can exterminate.

8154.d: This charming little beetle is in fact a thoroughly fearsome creature. Humiliated by his friends when he was younger, he decided to take his revenge. Just tell him if a Scaraleaves is giving you grief and he'll be glad to sort it out for you.

8155.d: This magnificent creature is somehow related to the famous Lenalds of Wabbit Island. More reckless and a lot more unruly, it will help you in combat and, with unspeakable treachery, will also help you defeat members of his own family.

8156.d: This key will grant you access to the terrible Canidae Dungeon. Once inside, you'll most likely be gutted in a relaxing, low-key atmosphere.

8157.d: Just like any magical item, this one is impressive. The petal emits an aura that is as powerful as the incredulity of any onlookers.

8158.d: The Tofurby regularly smears himself with grease to stop his feathers falling off his plumage. A technique as old as the hills, which enables some Enutrofs to keep some of their hair beyond puberty.

8159.d: Put it on your head and this carapace will protect you from bad weather and guano drops.

8160.d: If you want to look like Korgamone the Carpathian Capon, it's very simple - stick these antennae in your nostrils and sing out loud.

8161.d: If you've always dreamt of flying like a fat Piwi, stick these wings to your belt and jump from the Tower of Orders in Brakmar. As well as giving the locals a laugh, you'll make a great meal for Crows.

8162.d:
With this magic Pumpkwin on your head, you'll look even more idiotic than usual. But remember the Al Howin curse... yes, the curse that transforms creatures into misshapen beasts... 
It seems that this headgear is the only thing that can protect you from this terrible curse.

8163.d: Formerly worn by the authorities of the greatest cities, this helmet is now used to intimidate rebels and those who are a bit too curious about the rulers of the universe.

8164.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open it. You'll find a wonderful pet inside, as well as a book explaining how to raise it, some food and some healing Eniripsa powders.

Apparently, the curse can only be warded off by wearing a Pumpkwin on your head. The most surprising thing of all is that this seems to work.

8249.d: This alcohol-soaked feather is extremely inflammable. It's very useful for roasting Drinkers.

8250.d: The Crowfox loves to dress up as a Crow. No one really knows why, but most people have something to say on the subject.

8251.d: Who would have believed that a Peki would accept to give away a bunch of hair just to please you? No one, besides Garlik Jorisk, famous doofus of Amakna, renowned for his dishonesty, and his pathological affection for stuffed Pekis.

8252.d: This greasy feather belongs to a Tamed Crow who spent most of his life locked up and force-fed until he became fat enough to completely fill the space of his cage.

8253.d: This amulet is often mistaken for a lucky-bag gift... It's actually something you win at the shooting range.

8254.d: Offered as a wedding ring, this ring sends two subliminal messages to the wearer: "I love you" and "Go do the dishes". Perfect for those who hate wasting their time repeating the same things over and over again.

8255.d: Many inexperienced adventurers will remember this terribly powerful weapon, used as a defence against sods of earth. If you wet it, it becomes soft and can be rolled about, though it generally takes at least two weaklings like yourself to manage it.

8256.d: With these boots, Eniripsas can walk on water... which is quite useless since they can fly anyway, but it always impresses the crowds. Normal folk can always use these boots to exfoliate their feet while they sit around the house...

8257.d: This belt allowed Vald to take his seasonal bath without putting his life in danger. Indeed, no Iop ever succeeded in learning so much as the doggy paddle.

8258.d: This cape is perfect for camouflaging yourself in the natural environment. Well, it's more like you'll be adding a pleasant touch to the countryside, but hey, who wants to be invisible anyway?

8259.d: Instructions: "Offer this helmet to your husband. Firmly attach it to his head and drag him by his feet around your kitchen. You now have a clean, shining floor. Be careful not to drown him when rinsing the helmet off." This sums up the state of the modern marriage. Bloody feminists.

8260.d: This headband will make Iops more handsome than ever!

8262.d: The Amoolet holds a strange substance that is only found in the guts of a Moowolf. Some say it's the monster's essence, others say it's just the semi-digested remains of a Kirball.

8263.d: Beware! This ring will make your finger stink, although the foul smell may cover a worse odour. Actually, that might be the best thing that could happen to your finger, your hands, and the people around you, to be honest.

8264.d: Ubiquitous boots that are still driven by the voracious appetite of the Moowolf. If your feet smell of Clakoss, these boots will probably bite them.

8265.d: The Moowolf's beautiful, fluffy tail is so long that it trails on the ground. Driven into a jealous rage, some adventurers pulled it off and they now wear it to increase fertility.

8266.d: This coloured belt has a wonderful purple tuft on the front and if you wear it back to front you can pretend to be a Wabbit.

8267.d: While dismembering the Moowolf, hunters discovered that it only has one big horn going right through its skull. That doesn't seem to bother Iops, who wear it proudly anyway.

8268.d: This necklace protected the Minotoror from getting fleas, ticks and even lice. You can be the judge of whether you need it or not.

8269.d: Unlike what some adventurers may think, this ring was never worn by the Minotoror who was unable to fit such a delicate thing around his hoofs.

8270.d: This bracelet fully protects the arm of an Eniripsa, but triples its weight.

8271.d: This ring of leather and ivory makes it easier for you to stimulate your partner.

8272.d: This necklace protects the Minotot's cervical vertebrae from lethal Wabbit punches.

8273.d: This necklace comes with a small loop so the owner of the Dragon Pig can attach a leash to it. It also does wonders for Dragon Pig lice.

8274.d: This very axe actually beheaded one of the most dangerous Minotorors in the province of Amakna. What I can't believe is that you don't seem to care!

8275.d: This sceptre with a Serpentine head made of precious stones at one end enables you to scare away young adventurers and kick their pinky butts.

8276.d: You won't go winning the legendary race of Amakna Bay with these terrible boots of Minotoror Hair and leather. You might manage to break the competitors' toes on the starting line, though.

8277.d: These incredible sandals will enable you to bathe in the most dangerous waters without hurting your feet. However, be careful they're said to scratch the bottom of bathtubs.

8278.d: A good pair of mules at your side and you'll feel stronger, more powerful and deadlier than ever. They're just ordinary mules, though. It must be the vibes they give off...

8279.d: Take a Minotoror. Firmly tie him up. Take a giant plane and peel his back at one go. There! You've got your Minotoror Cloak!

8280.d: This is the perfect cloak to go out or practice your seduction skills at the Captain Chafer's masked ball.

8281.d: This cloak will not turn you into a Piglet but at least you'll be able dress up for one night and seduce a beautiful sow.

8282.d: This supple belt can be used to whip unruly kids' bottoms. Its buckle might even mark their skin but this would only teach them their lesson once and for all.

8283.d: The Minotot used this stiff belt to hold his huge potbelly in, preventing him from toppling over every time he felt a draught.

8284.d: This headgear has been passed down from generation to generation through the Minotot family. This partially explains why it smells like rotting dandruff.

8285.d: With this huge skull on, you'll look like a stiff-bristled Grizball, but with no hair. Your admirers will be speechless.

8286.d: According to the legend, this scale-covered cape will protect you from lightning, beans and femmes fatales, whatever they are.

8287.d: A little angel like you could easily pass for a merciless warrior with such a terrifying and disproportionate helmet on. If that doesn't work, it'll make a great cloak rack.

8288.d: The most perverted minds in Amakna used to say that this belt could be used as a prosthesis. Fortunately the rumour was exposed as a lie - it's just a plain old Dreggon Belt.

8289.d: This ring, directly cut in the shape of a giant Dreggon scale will protect a small part of your phalanx. Maybe the most important part...

8290.d: Made of Dreggon scales, this amulet will efficiently protect your Adam's apple or your tonsils. It will make all the difference on a battlefield.

8291.d: These boots are perfect to kill Gobballs while playing Gobbowl or to make your enemies suffer some more during Spanking sessions.

8292.d: You'll end up without a nose if you use this sword to shave your face. Save it for your back.

8293.d: This axe cuts through skulls like a hot knife through butter.

8294.d: Heavier than an empty Munchor Skull, but less solid than a Cave-dwelling Kirball femur, this hammer is nevertheless quite a fearsome weapon.

8295.d: This bow is so powerful that it can send Dreggon eggs over the great wall of Brakmar. What a wonderful waste of food!

8296.d: This wand seems to be a lot more effective when it's used as a club or as a Moskito swatter!

8297.d: One end of this staff is armed with a long, sharp point. No one knows where it came from, but you can guess where it usually goes.

8298.d: Shika used to help Farle at harvest time by picking up the magic grain his scythe swiped. She used it to make necklaces. Though their roots and stalks have been cut off, these magic ears keep on ripening every year around the same time.

8299.d: This bracelet covered up Shika's arms. This way it protected her from sunburn and Crow pecks... the little creatures were attracted by her stunning beauty and many claim to have gotten lucky with her.

8300.d: This custom made staff helped Shika make the highest haystacks in all of Amakna. Legend has it that they were so big that sailors used them as markers to tell how far they were from land. Now you know why sailors have a fear of harvesting.

8301.d: These clogs were created for Shika so that she wouldn't trample the seedbeds of the Snossios plains. The high-heels make it easier to run in the stubble without hurting her ankles and stop the dew getting in.

8302.d: Flowers from harvest time have been sewn to this cape made of woven magic cereals. It's driven by such a powerful magic that Shika used to use it for protection against lightning on stormy nights!

8303.d: This belt of leather used to protect Shika's thighs when she ran across the wheat fields to bring back to their herd lost Gobballs. Covered with pollen from magic cereals, legend says that it used to shimmer in the moonlight and ensured Farle didn't cut his wife's legs while reaping fields of cereals at night.

8304.d: Covered with a multitude of flowers, this hat made Shika look happy and bright when she left at the crack of dawn to plough the Church Hills.

8305.d: This strange relic is essential for you to meet the Minotoror.

8306.d: This strange relic is essential for you to meet the Minotoror.

8307.d: Crafted from diverse materials, this key will grant you an audience with the terrifying Minotot. If you go the distance, it'll make a great story for the taverns and picnic tables of the land. You'll also have a sore ass, or perhaps the remnants of a sore ass, if you do live to tell the tale... Good luck!

8308.d: This small shiny shell is very useful for creating nice jewellery at a low cost... You'll be able to sell it to an Astrubian for a fortune once you convince them it can make you fly.

8309.d: This feather is covered with magic stone dust which explains why one unit of Quetsnakiatl feather is heavier than three units of Tofu feathers. It's all logical, you know.

8310.d: This jelly pot contains some repulsive-smelling substance with an appalling taste, and yet, you secretly dream to spread it all over your body, don't you. Your perversion is even greater than your gluttony.

8311.d: This hair seems to be covered with short-haired-Tuftie-musk based brylcreem and cave Kirball grease. They almost look appetizing.

8312.d: Worn out by the sand and the sea salt, this skin is as thin as an old sock worn out by... sand and sea salt. Does that mean a healthy Minoskito looks like a fresh sock? Yes it does.

8313.d: This bone is sturdy enough to be used as a girder or to break bricks in packs of ten. It comes in handy if you want to destroy your neighbour's house. Useless for people of sound mind.

8314.d: This roasted skin protects sensitive skins from rays of sunshine. It's a particularly close-fitting skin.

8315.d: This spotted skin is said to be covered with a poison capable of changing anyone into a dried Karaball.

8316.d: This book was written by Oshimo Bigglip. It explains how to raise a Minifoux.

8317.d: This book was written by Oshimo Bigglip. It explains how to raise El Scarador.

8318.d: This book was written by Oshimo Bigglip. It explains how to raise a Treechster.

8319.d: This book was written by Oshimo Bigglip. It explains how to raise a Gobtubby.

8320.d: After getting lost in the Dragon Pig maze, you realised that you had forgotten the key to the Dragon Pig Den. Fortunately, your Porco pals had a spare with them.

8321.d: It's useless insisting! These hairs are not edible.

8322.d: Under its bandages, the Mumminotor hides a very soft down that would make the most coquettish of princesses jealous.

8323.d: This rough, cracked leather will remind you of your beloved's cheeks.

8324.d: The Mumminotor always had sensitive skin, that's why he has to cover himself up with bandages. Spiteful gossips say that it's to hide other shocking things....

8325.d: If you want to protect your pretty face from the ravages of time, we suggest this headgear. It makes a great adult nappy too...

8326.d: Wrapped up around the horns but especially around the private parts of the Mumminotor, this bandage became impregnated with the Mumminotor's magic with the passing years. Smelly and terrifying, this bandage is much sought after by the fetiologists of the world.

8327.d: At first sight, this impressive horn does not seem to be very useful. And even when you take a closer look at it, it doesn't seem very useful - a bit like an army of ticks.

8328.d: Wrapped up in a magic bandage, this horn must be extremely expensive, very precious, awfully smelly and cursed. A bit like a mummy would be.

8330.d: This small headgear enables the Flying Dreggon to attack his enemies without bumping his head. It's been used for a long time on the greater worksite of Amakna. This headgear became quite popular after the invasion of Astrub by Moowolves coming from the Kruup Mountain. There's no logic in this story... so what?

8331.d: With this hat on, you'll be able to dress up and seduce any naive Astrubian you find... Just offer him a hot date for 100 Kamas, and Bob's your uncle, his wallet's empty.

8333.d: This mysterious cape only comes out once a year, but the scammers always use it to get a fast buck from the kiddies.

8334.d: This hat will hide the scars all over your head. That way, no more toddlers will be injured trying to flee in terror from your Santa stall.

8335.d: The Amakna Team sends you its warmest season's greetings. This present will make you happier than you've ever been before... Won't it?

8341.d: These boots smell of pineapple juice marinated with wet socks. The great thing is that when you visit your friends, they will never ask you to take your shoes off.

8342.d: This key, made of pressure-bonded Dreggon shells, will give you access to the terrible Dreggon Sanctuary, reputed for its awkwardly silent inhabitants.

8343.d: You thought you'd seen it all in the Dreggon Sanctuary, but NO! Not by a long shot. In fact, I'm betting this key leads you to your death.

8344.d: It's not as pointy as a Xelor clock-hand but it's a lot more solid. This horn enables the Dragoss to transform a Spanking session into a Cracking one.

8356.d: Smooth and perfumed with young adventurers' blood, this skin makes Dragostesses irresistible. Used to make boots or belts, this skin can be washed in a washing machine at any temperature.

8357.d: The Dragostess has two small horns at the back of her head with which she detects the love waves that float through the air during mating season... which never really ends for the Dreggons.

8358.d: This pair of Dreggon shells protects the Dragostess from love at first sight. Males can also use it, but they'll have to wear it below the belt.

8359.d: Even when this wing is damaged, torn and burnt, the Flying Dreggon can still freely fly above void like a young carefree Moskito.

8360.d: This dark skin is covered with a multitude of small scales that are supposed to improve the aerodynamics of the Flying Dreggon. In fact, they're useless and only make people talk.

8361.d: The Flying Dreggon uses this horn as an aiming device to help him hit his targets when he drinks and flies.

8362.d: Tough enough to resist its own blade, Dreggon Warrior skin is also renowned for being edible... you'll have to boil it for several years first though.

8363.d: The Dreggon Warrior has three different horns: two on the back of his head and a third one on his snout. After a fight, a horn usually ends up in the behind of his victim and the two others stuck up in the nostrils of the foolhardy challenger. But from time to time, the Dreggon Warrior mistakes the behind for the nostrils. This only makes it worse for his victims.

8364.d: This leather strap enables the Dreggon Warrior to attach his shoulder pad or to replace his shoulder strap.

8365.d: Crocabulia broke her horn in a terrible fight while protecting the egg from which Crocoburio hatched some 15 years later.

8366.d: This cape used to belong to a famous Capon, a long-feathered bird that loved to dance in front of the Bonta Zaap where all the gullible poultry and immature chicken hang out.

8367.d: You could use this red skin to make a Little Red Waddling Cape, but your tailor would be very confused. "This recipe has produced nothing!" they would cry, somewhat awkwardly.

8368.d: This huge tooth was pulled out at the very last minute, right before Crocabulia closed her mouth for the very last time.

8369.d: This shell fragment belonging to Terrakubiack the Warrior should help you make a key to access the Dreggon Sanctuary.

8370.d: This shell fragment belonging to Ignilicrobur the Warrior should help you make a key to access the Dreggon Sanctuary.

8371.d: This shell fragment belonging to Aeroktor the Warrior should help you make a key to access the Dreggon Sanctuary.

8372.d: This shell fragment belonging to Aquabralak the Warrior should help you make a key to access the Dreggon Sanctuary.

8373.d: This stone can release a powerful magic wave that will activate and open a magic door, if and only if it is combined with the three other missing stones.

8374.d: This stone can release a powerful magic wave that will activate and open a magic door, if and only if it is combined with the three other missing stones.
