8376.d: This stone can release a powerful magic wave that will activate and open a magic door, if and only if it is combined with the three other missing stones.

8377.d: Handymen use this stone to give their position to clients.

8378.d: This fragment contains some magic transferred by an ancient object. You should be able to get a few magic runes out of it at least.

8379.d: This small rune will make you more hardy.

8380.d: This fabric used to cover up the Peki's hairy behind until you rubbed it up the wrong way.

8381.d: This tail is so magic that it still wiggles even after it's been cut, dried and stuffed! It you're smart enough, you'll find it another use for it than hanging it above your fireplace.

8383.d: Deprived of his soft skin, poor Moon was taken by surprise and could only run away in the jungle screaming with pain. This is a nice bedtime story you'll enjoy telling your kids to make them go to sleep.

8384.d: This fabric seems to be magic and you find it hard to believe. But one day, you'll have to face the truth... You're just too stupid to tell if something's magic or not. Do not follow your Astrubian killer instinct... trust all these descriptions.

8385.d: This Shin Larva skin is even more sticky and slimy than you'd have ever imagined. It reminds you of the last princess you rescued.

8386.d: No one would have ever believed that a Shin Larva would actually have a mouth full of teeth. It's probably because Shin Larvae only have one tooth.

8387.d: More royal than the Royal Tofu feather, more vibrating than the Vibrating Kirball of the Kruup mines, this feather will tickle whoever you want, wherever you want. The instructions say that it should be easy to look after.

8388.d: The Bworkette let you take some of her skin in exchange for your clemency. But she forgot to tell you that she told her big brother Bworker... he might want some of yours in exchange!

8389.d: The Bworkette has very soft skin everywhere but under her arms. Well, the little cookies she makes have to be flavoured somehow, don't they?

8390.d: If you believe the breeders, Farle was the greatest breeder of all. But then again, they were all jealous of Shika. Anyway, what's certain is Farle is the one who created Farle's Pigs. Another certainty is that he wasn't the most handsome creature - the pigs were created in his own image.

8391.d: Dorgan Ation has once more been extremely generous with you in spite of his bad temper. He gave you his skin before leaving and moaning like a Lousy Pig. What a nerve!

8392.d: You used a cheese grater to scrape this skin off a poor Blodz Uker. No doubt he will remember that terrible event for life. Don't count on him to tell you the way next time you get lost in his maze.

8393.d: Though you've searched thoroughly, you couldn't find out where this Dragon Pig hair came from. Search some more. The Dragon Pig's anatomy is full of surprises...

8394.d: This humongous rock looks like a rock from the Legendary Crackler, but it is not. It's a lot more special than that!

8396.d: This small flask contains all the virile power of the Boowolf. Be careful! Its contents are not edible.

8397.d: The Wa Wabbit is usually quite miserly and balks at sharing its hairs. Exceptionally, to reward your courage (or buy your clemency), he has decided to give you one of his body parts. How touching!

8398.d: No one really knows where the Wa Wabbit got this fabric and no one seems to be willing to know either. Disturbing and disquieting, the origin of the fabric remains one of the greatest mysteries of all Amakna.

8399.d: Once again, the Pandora Master tried to show off. Another lesson he won't forget. He'd have been better off in his box.

8400.d:
Whether protecting the nape of his neck or his ample behind, this fabric saved the Pandora Master's life more than once! 
But not this time, however...

8401.d: Worn out by magic attacks, dried out by the wind from Pandala Island, this skin is now of a very poor quality. But you seem to be attached to it as if you were trying to keep a precious memory from this courageous Pandora Master, who tried to kill you many times. It's at times like these that we see the difference between a real monster and a sissy.

8402.d: Though the Koolich is quite a generous thing, he wasn't exactly happy about giving you his big stone. And it's understandable, given what you're going to do with it.

8403.d: This huge braid was made by the Koolich himself, some years ago. With the passing years, it became as stiff as a rock. However, it still holds a foul, slimy liquid that attracts Moskitoes from time to time. The most surprising thing is that this braid used to perfectly suit the Koolich. Like a big Slob, you had the ridiculous idea to steal it.

8404.d: This piece of skin probably comes from Skeunk's heels which can explain its nice yellowish colour. Though this old skin won't enable you to make fashionable clothes, you'll still be able to create "retro" ones that younger generations will love.

8405.d: Skeunk thinks nothing of a full body-shave. Here's the proof.

8406.d: This wool is particularly thin making it possible for the Minotot not to have frizzy hair all over his body. No one knows why he has it. Maybe you should try to make hair grafts out of this wool so that you'll be able to display an abundant growth of brown hair on your chest. See, even your childhood dreams can come true!

8407.d: Almost as rare as Gobball leather, this leather is perfect for creations that require supple seams... leather masks, for example.

8408.d: An enormous number of adventurers have been trampled by this hoof, but then so have many huge turds scattered around the Labyrinth of the Minotoror. You must understand that it's not easy for a charging Minotot to distinguish between the two at first glance.

8409.d: From a distance, this horn looks like a giant, extremely powerful Gobball horn. Surprisingly enough, from up close, it looks like a Minotot Horn.

8410.d: This impressive bone succeeded to bear the excess weight of the Minotot for centuries. Such a feet always deserves to be pointed out.

8411.d: This cursed, bandage-covered amulet might help you overcome the curse of the Labyrinth of the Minotoror, but there's no guarantee... it might just be some tourist-stall junk. Who knows.

8412.d: This ugly, stench-ridden ring is made out of Mumminotor bandages. It makes a great Band Aid when you catch your finger in one of the doors of the Labyrinth of the Minotoror - possibly the least of all your worries, but a comfort nonetheless.

8413.d: The rock at the end of this hammer is rolled in absorbent Mumminotor bandages for those home-based assassinations.

8414.d: These daggers are perfect for cutting the top off a soft-boiled Dreggon egg. They're also very light which enables you to run fast when the Dreggon community realizes what you've done.

8415.d: Padded and decorated with Mumminotor bandages, these boots are comfy and warm. They might even remind you of long-forgotten mother-cuddles.

8416.d: Made from plaited Mumminotor bandages, this cape will give you a slow, sad, undead look. You'll be the envy of the town.

8417.d: This small shovel was once given to a young Enutrof. He liked it so much that he took up digging full time. He dug his own grave when he was twenty eight and healthy... dug himself a whole graveyard, he still didn't die. His body was lost at sea first time he left home. How ironic.

8418.d: The origin of this large Mumminotor bandage is unknown. Its use is even more mysterious, since it actually speeds up decomposition. Great for an April Fool's Day trick. Just make sure you keep a list of all the good friends you give it to so you can tell them to take it off again.

8419.d: Captain Mayhav is said to have used this very shovel to rip open the Great White Kralove known as Dopy Mick.

8420.d: Dreggons like to dig networks of underground passages but they never use these shovels. The Enutrof community studied this enigma but concluded that it was less important to know where they came from than how to hit someone with one.

8421.d: This certificate mentions all the characteristics of the Baby Crowdzilla you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8424.d: This gift is only meant for Breeders - it contains all kinds of breeding machines for your paddock. (Warning! The items contained in this gift are very heavy. You might be overweight when you open it.)

8425.d: This purse is very heavy - it must be worth a fortune. A tradesman will be happy to exchange it for its value in Kamas.

8428.d: This potion allows you to return to your last save point without a trace.

8430.d: Unlike the fake ones you'll find at the Trool fair, this balloon can take off with grace and ease. A beauty to behold, it's handmade with Strawberry Jelly eyelid, according to the traditions of the great magus Betsy Krokerr.

8431.d: This smoke potion creates a whirling smoke screen which hides all your actions with style.

8435.d: Unlike the fake ones you'll find at the Trool fair, this balloon can take off with grace and ease. A beauty to behold, it's handmade with Strawberry Jelly eyelid, according to the traditions of the great magus Betsy Krokerr.

8436.d: This key will grant you to access to the most intimate parts of the Soft Oak's anatomy... I bet you won't even know it when you get to the special place. As disturbing and exciting as the much loved Amaknan sport of naked Judo, this trip will not leave you empty handed, that's for sure...

8437.d: This key, made of marine waste and sea shells, will grant you access to the beach with the whitest sand of all the Asse Sea Coast. (See 'Dedicated Asse-tourist' Vol 1.8: 'An Asse with a view')

8438.d: This key will let you into the Rat dungeon located deep in the sewers of Brakmar. No need for a disguise, you'll go unnoticed even if you're not a Brakmarian.

8439.d: This key will let you into the Rat dungeon located deep in the sewers of Bonta. No need for a disguise, you'll go unnoticed even if you're not a Bontarian.

8441.d: Bill wanted a halo. He screamed so loud and threw such a tantrum that he finally got it. A real little devil.

8442.d: Brouce Boulgoure used this mask to discreetly infiltrate a Grossewer rats' den and cut down an elm by the roots. On the way out, he squashed every single rat in the den with his wooden clogs.

8443.d: This cape can be made with any sort of animal hair provided that it's very dirty. They are plaited together and then cemented with various secretions. The smell is unfortunately not optional.

8444.d: Badly damaged, but extremely sharp, these dagger blades will slice off a limb with disconcerting ease. They'll sink through bones like butter, allowing you to carve your enemies up like spring chickens. What a pity they aren't rusty, poisoned and white-hot too!

8445.d: The rat who used to own this necklace thought he would become the chief of his clan. He was devoured by a rabid Lenald.

8446.d: Be careful when you put on these boots, as there might still be a foot or two of the previous owner inside them.

8447.d: Unlike his white Bontarian cousin, the Black rat is discreet and wears a simple fabric belt. But he also likes to take a lot of weapons with him and it all makes a terrible clinking noise at each of his steps.

8448.d: Turn this ring to the right if you're shaking hands with an enemy and to the left if you're shaking hands with a friend. Make sure you stay away from any situation where you may be forced to clap.

8449.d: A Treechnid bit you and passed on a strange curse.

8450.d: This weapon is the symbol of the White Rat. It will slice both enemies and allies with the same ease.

8451.d: The White Rat of Bonta looks like a real White Rat of Bonta when he wears this hat. Without it, he looks like a real White Rat of Bonta without a hat.

8452.d: This cape is the unmistakable banner of the Bonta white sewer rat network. It is the reward the rat gets after a long and difficult series of examinations and is proudly worn until he pants his final ratty breath... which usually isn't a long time.

8453.d: Plumbers wear this necklace when descending into the intestine-like sewers of our cities. If you wear it as a belt, it will protect your allies from your sewer-like intestines.

8454.d: This Gauntlet used to belong to Julia Dilch, master cook at the Bonta palace. After a while, she never took it off - a Gobball that refused to have its throat cut, a tough fillet of lamb, even the odd head of lettuce, all fell victim to her vicious blows.

8455.d: Though his Black Brakmarian cousin may not agree, the white rat likes to be as discreet as possible.... he padded the metallic links of this belt with tar so it doesn't make any noise... unless the person wearing it trips and falls... which happens a lot given it weighs about a ton.

8456.d: With these boots, your balance will be perfect... they're very popular with drunk drivers, they practically walk along the yellow line for you. Saying the alphabet backwards... that's another story.

8457.d: This hat has nothing to do with a Dora, a Brave's Dark Dora, a Dora Bora or a Doro L. Blak... Absolutely nothing! So don't bother spreading rumours about its designer being slack or uninspired! It's just a very nice looking hat.
8457.n: Lord of the Rats' Ceremonial Hat

8458.d: This colourful cape turns you into an ideal target. Only quick and nimble adventurers can wear it for more than a few minutes.
8458.n: Lord of the Rats' Ceremonial Cape

8459.d: To dissuade greedy thieves, this necklace is secured around the neck of the heir to the Lord of the Rats at his birth. The only way to remove it is to take off his head... This doesn't seem to dissuade the thieves...
8459.n: Lord of the Rats' Ceremonial Necklace

8460.d: This ring was designed at a time when the Lord of the Rats only had one finger left after mutilating all the others. The unfortunate lords that followed had all of theirs.
8460.n: Lord of the Rats' Ceremonial Ring

8461.d: The colours on this belt will have people thinking you're on fire. The optical illusion is so powerful that you shouldn't be surprised when complete strangers throw water all over you. Amazingly enough, this corresponds exactly to the ceremony's ritual.
8461.n: Lord of the Rats' Ceremonial Belt

8462.d: The very first Lord of the Rats died when he stepped in a pool of molten lava. To pay tribute to him, his lords wear these boots. By the way, they are not in the least bit fireproof.
8462.n: Lord of the Rats' Ceremonial Boots

8463.d: The mushrooms pushing up on this helmet spread a nice exhilarating smell that makes you want to take roots. They are also quite tasty but might definitely bury you.

8464.d: In summer, the Ancestral Treechnid likes to sunbathe but as its wood is accustomed to dark forests, it doesn't stand it very well. This cape is made of his bark peelings.

8465.d: Worn around your neck with a low-cut top, this torc will accentuate your beard beautifully. If you don't have one... well... you only have yourself to blame.

8466.d: If you've had a little too much to drink, you might see the Moskito embedded in this ring wink at you. But don't tell your friends, the little beast will deny everything.

8467.d: With these wooden Shin Guards on, your legs will be fully protected. You cannot wear boots at the same time.

8468.d: This belt is supposed to inspire you with ancestral virility. Whether this was ever true or not, the effect has now surely gone without a trace.

8469.d: This piece of wood extracted from the very heart of the Soft Oak is extremely powerful. Indeed, it can even enrage the Soft Oak.

8470.d: This ring is made of Soft Oak faeces. It's wooden alright, but the smell remains the same.

8471.d: On Sundays, the Soft Oak takes a long nap and when he wakes up he likes to have an obedient Trunknid bring him his flip-flops. Fortunately, he doesn't have any feet so they're still brand new.

8472.d: 200 years ago, some fabric got stuck in the Soft Oak's branches. As the tree grew, it impregnated the fabric with its magic. The cloth is now an integral part of this huge piece of wood and though it makes it hard to handle and highly flammable, its power can't be denied.

8473.d: In autumn, the Soft Oak wears its G-string to protect his precious acorns. In summer time, he likes to go commando.

8474.d: No matter how you wear this hat, it will always look like it's on sideways.

8476.d: You picked up this key in the Bonta Rat Dungeon. You'll need it, and its counterpart, to enter Sphincter's Dungeon.

8477.d: You picked up this key in the Brakmar Rat Dungeon. You'll need it, and its counterpart, to enter Sphincter's Dungeon.

8478.d:
This highly illegal potion is feared even by the strongest Pandawa warriors. A single gulp and you'll be obsessed with the idea of licking all footwear in sight. 
Students who are worried about their grades often use a similar potion for their teachers. Their breath smells slightly different though.

8480.d:
This highly illegal potion is feared even by the strongest Pandawa warriors. A single gulp and you'll be obsessed with the idea of licking all footwear in sight. 
Students who are worried about their grades often use a similar potion for their teachers. Their breath smells slightly different though.

8481.d: This hair is dirty and stinky. It roamed the most disgusting sewers of the area. And yet, it's still shiny.

8482.d: This scars all over this skin are actual proof of the Grossewer Rat's difficult childhood. You could at least feel sorry for him.

8483.d: Once washed, this skin can be used as a carpet or a doormat.

8484.d: They were once used to make fake moustaches, but they can also be used for fake armpit hair.

8485.d: Coiled around a soft wooden strip, this fabric can be used as a sponge or as a butt-scratcher. To each their own.

8486.d: This fabric as greasy as a Wabbit Hair that has been dipped into Blop grease efficiently protects you from the cold. Especially if you set it on fire.

8487.d: This fabric seems to be covered in a strange chemical... It definitely has side-effects, but I really don't know what they are.

8488.d: This rat bone can be emptied, pierced and carved. Then it can be used as a musical instrument... or a little place to keep change if you're not into music.

8489.d: This tooth is actually a horrible fang that enabled the White Rat to transmit many diseases to his victims when he bit them. A way among others to make sure his victims would die even if he couldn't finish them off. All means are good when you want to be respected.

8490.d: Sphincter was not kind to bones and would break them in two, three, four and sometimes even five pieces when he had to buck up his sleepy students.

8491.d: The Black Rat was well-known for his bad breath but also for his rough butt skin. The creature evolved this way after generations of slipping off toilet seats. Unfortunately, since he lived right in the sewers, this black rat never needed to go to the toilets.

8492.d: The White Rat loved to mope round the sewers and waited for some nice person to come and comfort him. Then he would abuse the naivety and credulity of his victims to skin them alive, stuff them with cashew nuts and roast them. Poor little cashew nuts.

8493.d: Who would have believed that one day you'd be holding the skin of the famous Sphincter Cell? Well, not Sphincter for sure. His over-confidence led him to his death.

8494.d: This bark got loose from the Ancestral Treechnid without your having to tear it off with your teeth.

8495.d: This shrivelled up bud was completely drained of its sap by a hungry creature. If you plunge it into water, you'll see it resume its original form, swell, and then if you wait a long time, rot.

8496.d: Even if you snatch it from its owner, this root can whip you or twist your ankles. Mean thing!

8497.d: This book contains the secret to a good Filtounga.... The mythic dish created by Mouss Bouff.

8498.d: This meat is as tender as the brain of a Mushd.

8499.d: Most of the time, Koalak meat is quite firm. You can make it a bit more tender if you strike it with a Kaliptus trunk. Just like you'd do with an unruly child.

8500.d: This tasteless meat can be preserved in mud for many years before it rots. Maybe then it'll have a bit of flavour.

8501.d: This Preserved Kaniger Meat may now be kept for many days before use.

8502.d: This Preserved Koalak Meat may now be kept for many days before use.

8503.d: This Preserved Crocodyl Meat may now be kept for many days before cooking.

8504.d: Either hot or cold, this Kaniger steak will satisfy the most voracious of appetites.

8505.d: This piece of meat will fill bottomless stomachs to the brim.

8506.d: This impressive piece of meat is obviously extremely hard to digest. But just as your eyes are always hungrier than your stomach, so your stomach is always bigger than your brain. Fool!

8507.d: The Filtunga is a unique dish. Its perfect mélange of ingredients lends it a heavenly taste. Serve warm with a dash of cream and a sprig of fresh parsley.

8508.d: This dish is for the witch Paindep.

8509.d: The great Bworknroll Magus reveals his sacred Bwork beer recipe, without leaving out a single secret and even giving a few tips on how best to enjoy it.

8511.n: Overpowered Uberleet Dark Crossbow of the Shadows

8513.d: Collecting "pieces" of creatures with the Bworknroll's scalpel will ensure you a good work since it preserves the vitality of the torn off limbs. Use it in fight to collect the parts you want.

8514.d: Always overloaded with fresh globules, a vampire brain sucks in all the red blood cells it can. That's why vampires are so pale. As for Iops, it kind of explains their red feet.

8515.d: If we consider the weight and solidity of a Trool bone, it's easy to understand why it hurts so bad when they smack you during Trool-playing games.

8516.d: This heartless Bworkette, who got rid of her son Krazybwork and threw him in a pit, was cursed by Bworknroll when she refused his love. Locked up in a cellar, she feeds herself with her own heart. Every night, it grows back and starts beating again.

8517.d: This beautiful and fresh Mumussel is a great companion to Bworks when they go plundering away from their wives.

8518.d: From the depths of the Asse Sea, Mumussels collect kelp and roll it under their armpits. Once the material is shaped like French Fries, they reach the beach to brown them in the sun before eating them.

8519.d: This traditional Trool mess sponge cake is made according an old Bwork recipe. Only a Bwork who's defeated a Trool with his bare hands is allowed to eat it. If he survived such a fight, he could eat just about anything!

8520.d: You can use this thick and nutritious grease to cook most types of food in old pots  without ruining the dish. Some Osamodas also use it to slip Tofus into places that the Iop moral code condemns.

8521.d: The red cape is the favourite artefact of megalomaniacs. Once on their frail shoulders, they believe they are Superman or an ultra-powerful magician. Until they meet a Minotoror at least.

8522.d: This surprising item contains a dark, concentrated magic that is said to be highly unstable. No one can foretell the effects it might have, but what's certain is that you shouldn't wait too long before using it... Or throwing it away.

8523.d: This family item is extremely powerful. Usually passed from generation to generation, it hasn't lost any of its powers. There are very few artefacts that contain such power. Some say it has even been in contact with a Dofus...

8524.d: This Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

8525.d: Piwi eggs are a real treat for those who have a sweet tooth! However, they hatch very quickly when they're close to a source of heat. That's why you shouldn't leave it in your pocket or in your mouth for too long! A mini Piwi could come out of its shell when you're just about to swallow. And trust me, having a starving Piwi stuck between your teeth or swimming through your intestines its way is not what you need if you're ticklish.

8526.d: This certificate mentions the characteristics of the Bloody Koalak you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8527.d: These Goblin skin boots were created by Planbworksek to charge the enemy (if possible from behind) extremely quickly. These boots saved many a Bwork comrade in wartime.

8528.d: Thanks to Gordo McRamsay, you'll finally be able to make the perfect pancake dough to feed your little ones and send them quickly off to sleep. What's the secret ingredient of this filling and mildly narcotic recipe? Magical Cure, of course!

8529.d: Nothing's better than this hammer to fix a broken Zaap.

8530.d: This hat keeps your ears warm and absorbs the alcohol on your breath. What else could you ask for?

8531.d: Who would dare wear such a ridiculous cap? No one, if not you.

8532.d: The power of this cape? When you turn your back to someone, your utter indifference will cause them to weep instantly. Only for the very spiteful among you.

8533.d: The Flud is not really a hat. It's more of a parasite that tends to develop on loud or aggressive people's heads. Its disgusting appearance repels all and sundry, compelling its wearer to scream even louder which is useless since these people have nothing to say anyway...

8534.d: This padded cape absorbs all surrounding noise, plunging the wearer into a lifetime of incredibly awkward silences.

8535.d: These getas are so light that they make their owner run and jump all over the place whenever some action starts. Experienced adventurers just hate them... Every Tom Dick and Harry comes and crashes their fights uninvited.

8536.d: This belt must be worn tight... so tight that it forces its wearer to stammer, shake and generally jerk around in the inimitable style of Thrustin Timbertake.

8537.d: This small ring has no use beside making you look extremely flashy. Now people might actually want to talk to you.

8538.d: After several nights of hard work, the most famous jeweller in Astrub, also known for being raised by Bworks, announced to an astounded crowd: "c u l8r @ d gld hs". Even the renowned historian Champo Lhyon didn't manage to decipher the jeweller's message.

8539.d: Even if you don't handle axes very well, you won't hurt yourself with this blunt thing. If you hit hard enough and for long enough, you might be able to knock some trees down.

8540.d: This is a scythe of average quality but don't complain... It reaps and it's bloody well free. What else do you want?

8541.d: Well, this fishing rod used to be in much better shape. Though the string is a bit frayed and the hook dull, you'll have no problem netting a few gudgeons.

8542.d:
You can tell those gloves come from money. You can hardly smell the sweat of the previous owner, it's almost impossible to get your fingers into them, you'd swear they didn't have a hole at all. 
All in all, those gloves just suck.

8543.d: This lemonade, made by the gods, is a mixture of water, bubbles, and animal extracts. It invigorates young souls on their arrival in Incarnam. For everyone else, this sparkling, vaguely yellow trash is just about good enough to use when training for burping contests.

8544.d: This certificate mentions the characteristics of Pingoku that you've just put in the Bow Kennel.

8545.d: This key allows you access to the Incarnam Dungeon where the dreadful Snoowolf lives.

8546.d: Slightly curly, this skin will make a wonderful bedside rug. I'm sure someone around Incarnam will want it. Find out who it is... and get as many Kamas as you can for it!

8547.d: Cirsid hizilnits irik nik gidik fir yik.

8548.d: Cuwsed cawwots awe bad fow youw health.

8557.d: This feather was plucked from the Batofu's armpit and it smells like a marinated ancestral Doobitchoo.

8558.d: If you're planning to communicate with Wabbits, this might be the hat you need. If you want to look good, put it on someone next to you.

8559.d: Mmmmm mm mmmmmm mmmmm, mmm mmm mm mmmmmm mmmmm mmmmmmm mmmmmm mmm mmmm'm mmmmm mmmm mmmmmmm.

8561.d: This cute Pandawa Cub will gladly travel round the world with you and discover its mysteries with its big, round eyes. This tamed pet eats rice, but can also be fed with hazelnuts.

8563.d: Litol must meet his future magic teacher.

8564.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Pandawa Cub you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8565.d: This Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

8566.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8567.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8568.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

8569.d: This cap used to belong to a little Xelorette who got a kick out of disrupting the passage of time. Legend has it that she once stole several days off the inhabitants of Amakna. She had to hand out quite a few candies to make up for that little trick.

8570.d: This hair used to belong to the Bonta sewer rats. Indeed, they were the only ones to have hair tufts which matched the colour of their city wall.

8571.d: This hair used to belong to the Brakmar sewer rats. Indeed, they were the only ones to have hair tufts which matched the colour of their city wall.

8572.d: Using this potion will cause you to unlearn one level of the spell 'Mount Taming'.

8573.d: Using this potion will cause you to unlearn one level of the spell 'Perfidious Boomerang'.

8574.d: Either with or without bacon, this Dofus is delicious.

8575.d: A famous Feca warrior who lived in the jungle of Pandala was often heard to say: "To win the war, you have to become the war".

8576.d: Yse Vewybad gave you this scroll to thank you for your favours.

8588.d: This emblem, given by a rogue, might be the key to enter their den.

8590.d: This contract proves Yse Vewybad's treachery. All you have to do now is to bring it to the right person.
8590.n: Contract between Vil Smisse and Yse Vewybad

8593.d: Uba Tesse gave you this potion. It will turn you into a Wabbit and this should let you pass yourself off as Allisteria's suitor.

8594.d: Uba Tesse gave you this potion. It will turn you into a Wabbit and this should let you pass yourself off as Allisteria's suitor.

8595.d: This egg contains an obese Tofu... a creature that may defeat the Pwince of Wa in the future.

8596.d: This sharp sword gained this elegant crimson colour after gutting thousands of Bworks. Before, it was just purplish.

8597.d: This potion will permit Vil Smisse to force-feed the obese Tofu that you brought him.

8598.d: These blades have holes all over them so that they make a nice little whistling noise when handled quickly. The holes are also extremely useful when it comes to gutting your enemies.

8599.d: These daggers were forged for a manicure-addict Ecaflipette. She didn't like those heavy swords that didn't match her perfectly varnished claws.

8600.d: No wonder you're exhausted, you've been shouting at the top of your voice all this time. Wait 6 minutes or so... Maybe then you won't be so lazy.

8603.d: The Wabbit Prince's servant looks gorgeous, darling, when he slips into his livery.

8604.d: This shiny sword is perfect for trimming flowers and trees, even if the plants fight back.

8605.d: This blade has been lubricated to slip into its sheath more easily. However, it cannot be cleaned after use and must be thrown away, especially if it's covered in blood. Bear in mind that its main use is to protect you.

8606.d: The bride's wedding dress has been carefully wrapped in this gorgeous package. It just needs to be brought to the steward San Lavalss.

8607.d: It's a big staff with nails knocked into it. Do not hope for something else in this staff, it's simple and loosens your enemies' teeth nicely.

8608.d: Rumour has it that a Sadida named Fraye used this staff to protect his wife and son from an enraged flock of Gobballs. What a pity that he also mistook his family for the monsters during the fight.

8609.d: This bow is light, delicate, elegant and smells of cherry tree flowers. But watch out, if you use it properly it can also be lethal.

8610.d: If you hold this bow high and joyfully say "Pampulilu!", you'll look absolutely ridiculous.

8611.d: This wand belongs to a famous Grinegau who makes excellent coffee, but who just can't get the ladies.

8612.d: With the Bidjiz, you'll stay alive probably because your opponents will start dancing when they see the disco ball at the end of this wand.

8613.d: Created like a Smithmagic masterpiece, this shovel digs really bad, except when it's your opponents' heads.

8614.d: This shovel is a great invention. It can dig up a grave and be left on top as a cross, provided only one adventure fellow dies at the time... Or else you'll have to dig the other graves with your hands.

8615.d: This Hammer easily crushes skulls to pulp... which is exactly why it's tinted with a nice red tomato colour.

8616.d: This hammer was created during the reign of King Stephan, a terrible tyrant who terrorised trillions of people.

8618.d: This strange axe is designed to easily behead Bworks. The ease with which it can also behead Astrub's inhabitants clearly indicates that there's a connection between these two populations. But no one has discovered just what it is yet.

8619.d: Thanks to this warrior hat, Iops really cut a fine figure. The only problem is that it hides some of their field of vision and prevents them from hearing their opponents' words. This hat is designed for those who like to strike before they think.

8621.d: This appetizing cawwot looks pwetty owdinawy but it stinks of evil fwom 50 paces. Will you wesist the temptation to devouw it?

8624.d: Unlike the fake ones you'll find at the Trool fair, this balloon can take off with grace and ease. A beauty to behold, it's handmade with Strawberry Jelly eyelid, according to the traditions of the great magus Betsy Krokerr.

8625.d: This green balloon is a delicacy made by force-feeding a Luidegit mushroom a green larva. The eyes of the larva roll out in the process and are sold to Bworks as appetizers. This balloon inspired Betsy Krokerr in some of her most famous recipes.

8626.d: Tis ippitiziknik hizilnik sims ti bik kitik nirmik bik is inik ficik ixtrimilik ivik. Wilik yik risiksitik tik timptitinik ti nibblik itik ik?

8627.d: Colleague and friend of the famous Guy-Guy (close parent of the Soft Oak), Sarr Ys is a minstrel whose enchanting melodies have been engraved in Amakna's collective unconscious. Unfortunately, this brilliant artist had a tragic Quaquack accident after a particularly humid new year's eve celebration.

8628.d: This headgear bestows self confidence and temerity on whoever wears it. Thanks to it you'll always keep going thinking you can actually make exploits. Remember to take it off from time to time or it will take you into inextricable situations!

8629.d: Every time an opponent comes to face this headgear, he turns as silent as the grave. No one dares ask what it is supposed to be. But that's ok, Srams aren't known for their sensitivity.

8630.d: This hat looks like the Sulik and the Paperb' Hat. But since it's very comfy and Xelors never take it off - even when they sleep, it is commonly called Hatter Lily. It gives off a nice pleasant white water lily smell which helps you get to sleep. However, it also provokes snores as unbearable as the Toads' song during the mating season.

8631.d: Thanks to this hat, Eniripsas always know how to deal with emergencies. Indeed, all the first aid tips are discreetly written on the lining. It makes them look as if they just graduated even though no one would normally wear such a ridiculous hat even for a school ceremony!

8632.d: Given its name, you'd think this cap would be a nice orange colour. Well, not at all! Moreover, this fashion accessory is more of a mask than a hat. So why did its creators name it this way? To make curious people talk, of course!

8633.d: The sharpened points coming out of this cap not only enable you to hurt your enemy but also increase your chances of being struck on the head by lightning during a storm. Indeed, Sacriers are a class who love to hurt others as much as themselves. A nice smell of grilled meat: nothing's better to start your day!

8634.d: Thanks to this headgear, you'll really look like a horny beast. People will turn round to admire the huge pair on your head. This roomy hood can also keep food fresh like hay for Gobballs or bread for Tofus.

8635.d: This helmet can make wearers make promises they instantly forget. Is it because it exerts pressure on the part of the brain which deals with memory or language? No one truly knows. What matters is to only take into account the less extravagant words.

8636.d: Robbie Hood was a famous Cra who lived in the woods. This explains the camouflage green colour of the cap. He wanted to take the law into his own hands and spent all his time stealing money from the rich for a good cause: himself!

8637.d: Fecas increase their luck, as well as that of their allies when they wear this hat. If you've hired a Feca who's wearing the Zinda Hood, you're sure to arrive safely and almost without a scratch. The problem is, it smells so foul that it's only useful for protecting widows and orphans.

8638.d: This hood can be used to fend off the bad weather, but it's also great for cooking. It allows you to regulate the strength of a flame with a tip of the head. Now you know why Enutrofs have such muscular necks.

8639.d: The floating cape will give you the aura of a warrior, especially when you turn your back to your enemy. Some think it's reinforced by a metal sheet capable of staving off the slyest attacks.

8640.d: Cut from a soft and strong fabric, this cape gives the Ecaflips the impression that they're always the best, no matter what happens. When they win, they love to wear this piece of clothing and claim their reward: "And now, gimme the cash!"

8641.d: This cape is so light and thin that the slightest wind, wind of any sort, will blow it off... It's anything but discreet especially after a meal of veggies and fermented drinks.

8642.d: The dark colour of this cape makes it easy to match any other cloth, of any colour. Since it's a very wide cape, it can also protect your head and nose.

8643.d: Place the cape lightly on your shoulders to prevent stiff joints, stiff upper lips and other stiffness-related problems.

8644.d: This item is used to hide the Sadidas' weight problem. Because they spend most of their time sleeping instead of practicing sports, the characters of this class tend to become rather stout. If Sadidettes actually have anti-starvation supplies flatteringly placed in the eyes of men, Sadidas usually use this cape to hide theirs.

8645.d: This piece of clothing plays an essential part in the Sacriers' style. They use it to bandage their wounds, to clean off blood, to warm their feet during the cold seasons. We cannot say it enough - this class is terrified of frozen ground!

8646.d: This soft cape is sometimes used by the Osamodettes as a wide-brimmed hat. Male Osamodas only use it as a cape. Thanks to the drawing which decorates this piece of clothing, this character class has inherited the reputation of being frank... they can't laugh up their sleeves since the laugh has actually been sewn onto the cape!

8647.d: Pandawas use this cape as protection against bad weather and as a dance accessory. They put it on the floor, in the middle of a circle of tipsy dancers. Then they start their improvised choreography during which their feet can't leave the cloth.

8648.d: Let me tell you about Hulco, a very strange Cra. He couldn't find his way to his own bathroom because everything he saw looked like a tropical beach at sunset. At least he never had to pay for a sun holiday.

8649.d: This cape's warm and comforting colours take its wearer on an imaginary journey to sunny lands, full of canyons carved by the elements, and cave paintings hidden amongst wind-blasted rocks and weathered cliffs. This is extremely useful way of forgetting the cold, grey, rainy weather that normally blights Amakna. At least it never snows, though - well, only at Kwismas. Funny, that.

8650.d: Enutrofs have the habit of drawing a map on their cape. They live in such a mess that they can barely find the toilets and this is quite a problem, especially when nature calls urgently.

8651.d: This beautiful belt adds to the prestige of the Iops' appearance. Some say that the central cross can become a detachable weapon when their swords aren't within reach. Obviously this is a legend. Only Srams are deceitful enough to have such things.

8652.d: When an Ecaflip is bored, he usually takes his cards from his belt and starts a game of solitaire. In fight, he can also use the cards as projectiles. He draws a card faster than his shadow and once victory is his, there's always time for a little game!

8653.d: The name of this belt comes from the particular noise it makes. The bones decorating the belt bang together, preventing the Srams, even those who are invisible, from going unnoticed. Then, you could easily hear such a dialogue: "Surprising someone wearing the Clinkin Belt? You've got a hope!"

8654.d: The incessant ticking sound of the clock system of this belt prevents Xelors from sleeping when fights last forever. It is strongly advised that you take this belt off before going to bed.

8655.d: Though it won't stop the sobbing, this belt will hold lots of medical supplies. This is especially important for Eniripsas... when they have a sore throat, they can't cast their spells properly. And when they're voiceless ... well, they're as useful as a bear skin jacket in a heat wave.

8656.d: The reason the designers of this fashion accessory put the doll head next to the crotch is still unknown.

8657.d: Warriors of an ancient tribe renowned for their love for blood, the Pados may have been the first worshippers of the goddess Sacrier. Despite its harmless appearance, this belt is a real sophisticated instrument of torture.

8658.d: Osamodas are known to be quite impulsive. They tend to be quite touchy. The numerous buckles on this belt are meant to help them put a cap on their spontaneity. "Before you light up your anger and inject your eyes with blood, touch each and every horn on your fantastic Diezzle Belt!"

8659.d: This belt helps Pandawas stand up straight (or almost) when they're drunk which they are, most of the time. In these moments, they tend to feel like they're stuck to the ground though gravity has no link whatsoever to this sensation. Gravity is way too busy knocking out scientists with apples.

8660.d: This belt enables you to keep up baggy clothes (so as not to scare away sensitive souls) and it also offers a target to apprentice Cras. Indeed, they're taught to shoot right in the centre but never below the belt.

8661.d: Provident, Fecas keep their survival supplies in a small bag, which mainly include Crackrock bread. That's why this food can last for so long. The Sekuritee Belt firmly secures the bag around their waist, because there are still way too many accidents linked to this bag falling, either due to negligence or just plain stupidity.

8662.d: This belt is a very handy fashion accessory used by male Enutrofs. Thanks to the map sewn onto it, they can hide their little accidents when they got lost looking for the toilets.

8663.d: With these boots on, the Iops are always the first to get to the battlefield and start livening the place up. It's common knowledge that this class love to amuse the crowd with their warrior exploits. But they're never taken seriously because of their intelligence, which is inversely proportional to their strength.

8664.d: It is said that Sadidas never feel lonely, since they can summon lots of dolls to keep them company. Thanks to these shoes, you too can say goodbye to loneliness! Not only will you be able to talk to them, but they'll be great for hiding aces when you're playing poker. Once you're wearing them, you'll feel really good, even if you are a little ashamed to actually go out with them on.

8665.d: Impregnated with a revolutionary firming agent, these boots will perfect the curvature of your legs and fight the good fight against your death-like Sram complexion. This cream has spectacular effects on Sramettes but seems to be absolutely useless on Srams. Could it be a hormonal problem?

8666.d: Created by a Xelor artist, these boots should enable him to paint more quickly. And well, it does! However, they tend to distort the vision, meaning the artist was incapable of drawing anything but curvy females.

8667.d: Thanks to these boots, you'll always be protected from the toxins that come from the ground. You can never be suspicious enough of microbes and other germs that hang about. Some fine observers say that these shoes have more of a slipper than a boot look. But well, that's what the Eniripsas call them. Is it because of their small size that they see everything from a different point of view?

8668.d: Thanks to their recognition system, these boots prevent Sadidas from crushing rare plants. However they won't prevent you from stepping in various sort of excrements if you don't watch where you're going.

8669.d: Unlike the other classes, Sacriers love to live with a thorn in their foot and do not wish to have it taken out. The pain they feel reminds them that they're alive and give them the raging energy they need to slaughter their enemies. Besides, the drops of blood they leave behind mean they always find their way back home.

8670.d: Crocodyl Dandy lost many a good opportunity and many a wife through his undying urge to wander round the outback. His fame grew fast and he was even offered a sponsorship deal by the famed shoemakers of Aerdala, but when he saw what they had on offer, he threw them back and shouted "That's not a pair of boots... THIS is a pair of boots."

8671.d: This impressive relic might make you forget all of your worries.

8672.d: This impressive relic might make you forget all of your worries.

8673.d: This impressive relic might make you forget all of your worries.

8674.d: This impressive relic might make you forget all of your worries.

8675.d: This impressive relic might make you forget all of your worries.

8676.d: Vlad fell in love with this wonderful sword. He entered the most terrifying of all Dragokart races to get enough money to buy it. Unfortunately, he didn't know that the sword was cursed...

8677.d: This cute Coney is the favourite pet of the famous Master Nero Jack. Do not be fooled by appearances, he can be really fearsome in battle. This pet only eats Cawwots and other plants.

8678.d: Long ago, Satanass was a figure skater slicing up Holyball on Ice on the rinks of the Second Zone. While recovering from an injury to the coccyx he had a life-changing revelation: his destiny was to be the most talented Dragokart driver of his generation! A little bump can sometimes leave a hefty lump.

8679.d: This Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

8680.d: This slimy, slippery scale allowed its owner to escape capture by strange adventurers who fished with their teeth. Unfortunately, it was no use against the well-placed swipe of a rusty sword.

8681.d: Raul Mops has a real weakness. He loves to smear himself with water, wine and vinegar. What he loves most of all is rolling  peanuts along the road with his nose. Dry roasted, by the way, just in case you ever feel like doing him a favour.

8682.d: Either side of this skin can be used for your DIY projects. The soft side is for cleaning delicate surfaces, and the rough side for scouring all your previously inaccessible body parts.

8683.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

8684.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Ross you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8685.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Bilby you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8686.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

8687.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

8688.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8691.d: You easily defeated the disciple. He agreed and gave you this scroll.

8692.d: This book contains theories from various alchemists about the possibility of Wabbit Twansfowmation. All it does is show how little they've done on the subject.

8693.d: Thanks to this pet, all your classmates will be giving you puppy eyes. Here's a tip: don't count your chickens before they hatch! You'll soon realize that your lover has been hypnotized by Fëanor. It won't even be an advantage: the one you once had eyes for will begin to munch on raw Snapper and rub up against your legs... Not the best. This pet only eats fish.

8694.d: This candied chilli is as explosive as the strainings from the devil's jockstrap. This mind bending mixture of sugar and fire led one Dragoturkey to a string of controversial victories in a the world Dragokart championships before being banned by all major sporting associations. You can use it as a suppository if you need to make a quick exit or as a pill if getting in is your problem.

8695.d: Like Brice said: "It's not the size that counts, it's the sharpness."

8699.d: You'll always have an out-of-bed look if you wear this hat, even if you've spent hours brushing your hair. The hairs on a Tynril's bark curl when the weather is humid, which makes it the surest weather forecaster in the world. This hat fears fire, however, so be extremely careful and keep it away from flames if you don't want to become a human torch.

8700.d: This headgear has been crafted from a broken Emerald Dofus. The egg is not quite empty, so treat yourself to a nice, energising hair mask while you're at it.

8701.d: This sumptuous sword used to belong to a famous thief who was renowned for getting nicked every time he committed a crime.

8704.d: If you shake your two little bells, you might be able to play music.

8706.d: This Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

8707.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Finer you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8708.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Atooin you've put in the Bow Kennels.

8709.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8711.d: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

8712.d: Congratulations! You managed to steal a piece of Goldemort's corpse. You'd make a vulture proud!

8713.d: In some countries, it seems that the Getas Bernacle are thrown at the feet of enemies  to propose a duel... kind of like hitting your opponent with a pair of gloves. The advantage of the Getas Bernacles is that they add the stench factor to the actual blow. Pandawas never were famous for their foot hygiene...

8714.d: Wearing this ring is an honour. It shows that you're a faithful worshipper of the goddess Cra, the only one to reveal how to harden your muscle more quickly to be able fire more effectively.

8715.d: Ecaflips have the gift of the gab. They can talk you into almost any bet you can think of. This ring celebrates their business smarts. It can also be used as a spare dice or to scratch yourself...

8716.d: Osamodettes love this ring which gives an extra feline touch to their walk. Because they're always so close to monsters, they're starting to behave like real animals themselves. But in reality, they're as devoted and caring as lioness mothers.

8717.d: Spiteful gossips claim that this ring is the least useful fashion accessory in the world. The wings attached to it are very awkward when you need to get a tissue out of your pocket. Now, as Iops have neither tissues nor pockets, they don't care. Instead, they prefer shredding their enemies' flesh with the wings during close combat. Thinking about it, you wonder why this isn't the Sacriers' ring instead.

8718.d: Fecas use the mini shields on this ring as memo boards to write love notes and to-do lists. This jewel has been nicknamed the anti-forgetfulness shield. However, it does not protect you from stammering or slips of the tongue.

8719.d: Thanks to this item, Enutrofs can remember their happy times whenever they want. They just need to extract the shovel driven into it. To make the remembrance even more genuine, you'd need to add a specific smell to it... Good luck!

8720.d: The goddess Eniripsa gave this item to her worshippers as a sign of their spiritual union during the class spell initiation session. Incidentally, Eniripsas can also use it as a sponge bracelet to clean off the blood of their allies.

8721.d: This jewel tends to turn Pandawas into insulting devils after two or three beers... just remember the old proverb  "Sticks and stones may break my bones, but a drunken bear-like creature will never hurt me."

8722.d: This jewel with a skull on it was traditionally offered to all Sram kids to reward them for their treachery and blows below the belt. The other classes seem to discredit this practice which tends to overexcite the kids and turn them into little devils.

8723.d: This ring is the only jewel that can tell the time and which is perfectly waterproof. Some believe that if you enlarge it a few hundred times, it'll make a submarine too. A submarine that can tell the time.

8724.d: Contrary to the rumour, Sadidas do not let their hair down... This hair has just been adjusted round a wonderful ring to reinforce its benefits. Never ever cut it! Thanks to the Hai Ring, you'll always be perfect!

8725.d: If you see a character who's not a Sacrier wear the Ring Neinwonwon, take him directly to intensive care. Indeed, this jewel is extremely harmful. In general, people lose their cool when they face the pool of blood caused by this ring.

8726.d: These shoes enable their wearer to dance all night long, despite blisters and corns! They dance to the rhythm of the night and make a little "beep beep" sound when they're next to religious artefacts. You'll be bright as a button the next day too, ready for a bit of slaughter.

8727.d: When Fecas are embarrassed and wish to change the subject, they always mention their Relief Boots. They talk about the way you can pace up and down all sorts of landscapes with them on. When their allies are in trouble on the battlefield, these comfy boots help them recover and ward off the threat.

8728.d: The numerous straps around these shoes can be used as spare bow strings. Young Craettes also use them to cook vegetables. The smell of feet doesn't seem to bother them.

8729.d: Coral only loosens itself from the Coralator when the weather is dry. Coral is a beautiful substance and is often used to make jewellery. Other brutes actually eat it... but only because they mistake it for crab sticks.

8730.d: This strategically-located bone enables the Coralator to sit down with dignity. Now that he's dead, you can use it to establish your own authority upon his fellow creatures.

8731.d: The only difference between the Worn Coral and the Great Coral is their size and what you can do with them. However, a whole lot of worn Corals will never replace a Great Coral.

8732.d: This coral's remarkable blue colour is a result of the Kurasso Craboral's unhealthy diet. It doesn't even manage to eat a single piece of fruit or veg a day, let alone 5!

8733.d: This coral's remarkable green colour is a result of the Mahlibuh Craboral's unhealthy diet. It doesn't even manage to eat a single piece of fruit or veg a day, let alone 5!

8734.d: This coral's remarkable red colour is a result of the Passaoh Craboral's unhealthy diet. It doesn't even manage to eat a single piece of fruit or veg a day, let alone 5!

8735.d: This coral's remarkable yellow colour is a result of the Mojeeto Craboral's unhealthy diet. It doesn't even manage to eat a single piece of fruit or veg a day, let alone 5!

8736.d: The only thing that can differentiate a Crackler's heart from that of a polished Crackler is the delicacy with which the item can break between your toes when you least expect it.

8737.d: From what part of the Crackrock's anatomy does this ball come? And why do they always come in pairs?

8738.d: The Coralator offers you a bone from its backside. It doesn't have much use for it anyway.

8739.d: Even though this bone's called a humerus, it's hard to tell if it actually comes from Sparo's arm. When he died, his skeleton was put in a barrel and smashed up. It sounds painful, even for a bone.

8740.d: If I were you I wouldn't pick this thing up - the mouth it came from is about as clean as the devil's crotch. But well, you're the adventurer, you know your business!

8741.d: This beak is so fragile that Otomai's disciples used it to make training arrows with blunt ends.

8744.d: Just avoid shaking a Craboral on the pincer! You might lose your hand to politeness.

8745.d: The colour of this petal reveals its doubtful origin. Alcohol abuse can even be noticed in Otomai's disciples' creations.

8746.d: The colour of this petal reveals its doubtful origin. Alcohol abuse can even be noticed in Otomai's disciples' creations.

8747.d: The colour of this petal reveals its doubtful origin. Alcohol abuse can even be noticed in Otomai's disciples' creations.

8748.d: The colour of this petal suggests its doubtful origin. Alcohol abuse can even be noticed in the creations of Otomai's disciples.

8749.d: The Palmflower doesn't grow from a seed but a bulb soaked in alcohol. Why? Just because!

8750.d: The Palmflower doesn't grow from a seed but a bulb soaked in alcohol. Why? Just because!

8751.d: The Palmflower doesn't grow from a seed but a bulb soaked in alcohol. Why? Just because!

8752.d: The Palmflower doesn't grow from a seed but a bulb soaked in alcohol. Why? Just because!

8753.d: This mane is an improbable hybrid of hairs and flower petals, which means it's doubly allergenic. So keep away if you're sensitive... a single sneeze could send your brain flying out your nose.

8754.d: This tiny hair tuft will remind you of your holidays thanks to its smell of sand, sunscreen and alcohol. What a pity it stinks so much of gunpowder too!

8755.d: No one knows whether the colour of this tuft is natural or due to some untimely bush fire.

8756.d: Kilibriss down is light and much sought after for the making of mattresses.

8757.d: Do you need an insect repellent? Just put Barbrossa's Shirt on! One side effect is that people will vomit automatically if they come within five feet of you.

8758.d: No one ever found an intact pair of Gourlo's shorts - he was a pyromaniac, and frequently burnt his clothes right off his body.

8759.d: This box is shaped like Flib... unless it's the opposite! In any case, it's still a cursed little chest.

8760.d: This scarf is an essential accessory for both the summer and winter seasons. It will give you an original look, though a bit kitsch. Its flashy colour will certainly excite male Gobballs, but is that really what you want?

8761.d: To compensate for the cannon he couldn't transplant as an arm, Gourlo never goes out without his weapon. He can't shoot very quickly since he must wait for the powder to dry each time.

8762.d: Thanks to this fragment, you'll learn the Cracklers' good manners: hand crushing to say hi.

8763.d: Marylork the painter prefers his brushes to be made from thick, luxuriant Mufafah Moustache, rather than the slightly wispy Kittenfish Moustache, which is liable to blow away in the slightest of breezes.

8764.d: To prove that he's the Boss, the eyebrows of the Greater Bherb are always frowning, even beyond death.

8765.d: Thanks to its length, this staff will enable you to reach the most difficult places to access and to scratch yourself all over.

8766.d: One of Otomai's greatest riddles was inspired by this resource: what's the heaviest? One hundred pods of Kido feathers or one hundred pods of Pyrute?

8767.d: The Pikoko never was famous for its grace in flight. Once you've seen its wings, well, you'll understand why.

8768.d: If you stick this ear to yours, you'll be able to hear the plain boar gallop instead of the  roar of the sea.

8769.d: There's no milk in this Pikoko Nut but you'll find some brain juice with a few floating neurones.

8770.d: This bark is curiously curved. It looks like it went through a rasp.

8771.d: This bark is curiously curved. It looks like it went through a rasp.

8772.d: This bark is curiously curved. It looks like it went through a rasp.

8773.d: This bark is curiously curved. It looks like it went through a rasp.

8774.d: This bark is curiously curved. It looks like it went through a rasp.

8775.d: This bark is curiously curved. It looks like it went through a rasp.

8776.d: There's no milk inside this Pikoko Nut, just brain juice. If you're lucky, you might find a few neurons floating on the surface.

8777.d: Should a Sacrier be lucky enough to remove several of these sexual organs from the four Tynrils after a long, arduous fight, the rest of his teammates would be well within their rights to refer to them as "The Sac's Pistils". Whether they should or not is another matter altogether.

8778.d: The stamen is the male organ of a plant. Yep! Despite appearances, it seems that Floramor is a male...

8779.d: A little biology lesson: the flowers are the plants' sexual organs and the pistil is part of the flower while the carpel is part of the pistil... I'll let you decide what does what.

8780.d: This part of the Gwass' body is always green, no matter what. Is it due to some excess of chlorophyll or to something else?

8781.d: Don't bother trying to use the Barkritter Calyx to drink anything. It might resemble a cup, but it's about as solid as a sieve.

8782.d: The Warguerite bract refers to an area that decency prevents me from uttering.

8783.d: The Dark Pikoko is not as nuts once he's got his tonsils removed. Well, this is no surprise since the surgery usually kills him.

8784.d: You won't defeat the Dark Treeckler by shooting an arrow in his Achilles' heel. But you can always try...

8785.d: With a lot of patience, time, water and fertilizer, you might manage to grow a Treeckler in your garden so that you can practice fighting against him. It would be easier to just catch a boat to Otomai Island..

8786.d: This thick and harsh hair can be used as a mop if not to hide your baldness. But you'll have to wash it many, many times before.

8787.d: No, it's not disgusting! It's nature!

8788.d: This rump will enable you to create items that will cover up your own backside.

8789.d: Despite appearances, Kimbo does wear socks, but he just doesn't wear them on his feet. He prefers rolling them and then placing them in strategic places.

8790.d: Nature having been only modestly generous to the Moopet, the creature has to resort to artifice to pass for a living thing. At times, he uses it to make his bed pass for a bed too.

8791.d: This fabric has a strange texture but will quickly dress any modest monster.

8792.d: There's no milk in this Pikoko Nut but you'll find some brain juice with a few floating neurones.

8793.d: Round and shiny, this shell has been polished with slobber for several centuries.

8795.d: To hide his premature baldness, Kimbo puts on this stupid wig. Fortunately for him, the coconut covers most of it.

8796.d: Captain Chafer heard the name of this object, and for ever more, the Treeckler was known as "Knob Head".

8797.d: A stump unlike any other stump, and yet, it spins.

8798.d: One by one, year after year, the number of feathers on the Bherb's tail increases. You can tell its age by the bushiness of its brush.

8799.d: Even if he often shaves it off, his hair always grows back thick and smelly. So the smell is not due to sweat.

8800.d: Made of a soft and resistant material, this fabric is perfectly adapted to the Zoths' figure and hides what needs to be hidden.

8801.d: This fabric has more holes than Swiss cheese, but it is still capable of absorbing a maximum amount of waste to regurgitate at the least opportune moment.

8802.d: Just like all the other bones of the Zoth Warrior, this shinbone has been broken many times. It healed perfectly and became even stronger. If it could talk it would say: "What doesn't kill you, makes you stronger."

8803.d: Since the Zoth Disciple always attacks with his knees, the kneecaps became extremely large and tough. I know tortoises who'd trade their shells for one of these things.

8804.d: The Zoth Master's fly is outstanding. It's been specially designed not to cut you.

8805.d: The Zoth girl does not use this handkerchief to wipe away her tears but to clean off her enemies' blood.

8806.d: This embroidered tab is more of a childhood memory than a military insignia.

8807.d: Unless you're flaming drunk, there's no way you'll confuse Ouassingue juice with any drinkable liquid you can name. The nauseating stench will dissuade the blind from knocking back a mouthful.

8808.d: This fabric has more holes than Swiss cheese, but it is still capable of absorbing a maximum amount of waste to regurgitate at the least opportune moment. BANG! And the dirt is back.

8809.d: Taking after their ancestor, Mopy King Dagobert, all Mopy Kings wear their shorts inside out. What's confusing is that it doesn't turn their stomachs inside out as well.

8810.d: Made from rotting vegetables, this peat has incredible powers of absorption. Mama Bworks save them for Auntie Floe's monthly visits.

8811.d: The Miremop spends a lot of his time taking mud baths in the hopes of slimming down. He has never lost an ounce, but at least his double chin evens out his figure.

8812.d: Slimy and dense, the Kralove ink can be used either to write romantic letters or to paint your room a depressing black depending on how your love-life's going.

8813.d: Given the size of this sucker, there's no doubt about its grip. And when you remove it, the slurping noise is deafening.

8814.d: This purse is heavy - it must be worth a fair bit. A tradesman will be happy to exchange it for its value in Kamas.

8815.d: This purse is quite heavy - it must be worth something. A tradesman will be happy to exchange it for its value in Kamas.

8816.d: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. For once, the gods might not have been pulling your leg.

8817.d: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. For once, the gods might not have been pulling your leg.

8818.d: Made from Mopy King Fabric, this cape is riddled with micro-holes that allow sweat to escape more easily during periods of intense exercise, during aggressive melees in steamy swamps, for example. Even though this cape lets the humidity out, it keeps the heat in. This way you're always dry, no matter the situation. What a pity the stench of mould is so hard to shift, though.

8819.d: Even though this cape is not as powerful as the fancier Mopy King version, it still has the same sweat evacuation system. You'll be able to face any situation wearing it, as long as you're able to fight while holding your breath, that is. The stench is truly unbearable!

8820.d: Thanks to this mask, you'll face all sorts of dangers without fear! But it's normal since it blocks the view.

8821.d: From a distance, this hat looks like a lampshade with two holes for the eyes. It looks the same up close actually.

8822.d: This mask won't help you avoid or heal hangovers, but at least it gives you some chance of hiding the effects.

8823.d: This mask won't help you avoid or heal hangovers, but at least it gives you some chance of hiding the effects. The dark touch simply indicates that you're in a bad mood... and that you should not be annoyed and you're ready to throw a flurry of blows to anyone who does not respect that!

8824.d: You'll look like a Snailmet if you wear this hat. Of course it will protect your head from blows, but does that make up for the slobber all over your head?

8825.d: Bigger, heavier and more powerful, this mace makes a louder noise when smashing the enemies. But curiously, it's lighter and has a better grip to it. The Coralator we used to make it wasn't great for no reason!

8826.d: Despite her small size, the Zoth Girl carries a huge hammer. It's a way to reinforce her muscle structure. No need to add weights round her wrists and ankles to increase her strength. Dragging the hammer is quite enough!

8827.d: The Zoth Warrior is used to carrying two axes because he can't reach his enemy's left side with his right hand. It's hard to tell whether it is due to a lack of self-confidence or if he was just born clumsy!

8828.d: The Cheeken is an awkward winged creature which has as much energy as if it had the avian flu and is as intelligent as  a Tofu. No need to say that it was not especially proned to survive. However, some people seem to just love its weird hair looking like a plaited mop. Human nature is an infinite mystery!

8829.d: This hat is large enough to hide Barbrossa's ridiculously hairless head and beard. But it won't cover big-headed skulls.

8832.d: This Snailmet slobber won't break a Pikoko's bones, but it'll certainly keep one glued to the ground.

8833.d: This hammer took its nice colour from the pieces of Coralator used to make it. Unlike what people think, it was not originally used to crush Iops and other enemies, it a door knocker for the hard of hearing.

8834.d: This branch was apparently used to scrape some otherwise inaccessible body part. But don't worry, the dark colour is authentic, it's got nothing to do with the various sorts of deposits contained in the inaccessible cavities of the Treeckler.

8835.d: This branch was apparently used to scrape some otherwise inaccessible body part. This might explain the stick's stickiness.

8836.d: Rotaflors use their stem to clean their ears. However, staff carvers prefer to use them as a weapon. Proof, if needed, that there's no accounting for tastes.

8837.d: This staff completely binds the Zoth Master, making him fearless and therefore formidable. When it comes to eating though, it makes an awful mess.

8838.d: Just like weeds, Tynrils can breed infinitely thanks to this simple piece of rhizome. After making this discovery some greedy staffmakers make a staff from Tynril and tried to breed it. It was a miserable failure.

8839.d: This is reputed to be the only mask that allows you to eat while you wear it.

8840.d: When Jav Kanniballs feel a little blue, they dye their hair this colour. Is it due to frustrated love or something else? Hard to know for sure, but It would be great if they could just wear the mask and stop telling everyone how sad they were.

8841.d: Many moons ago, the Kannibal's were travelling actors respected for their comedies and tragedies, as represented by two masks - one laughing, the other cruel. When their chief lost the happy mask, the Kannibals descended into savagery.

8842.d: Kanniball archers can't concentrate and aim right unless they are very angry. They painted their masks red so they'd be fuming all the time.

8843.d: When he puts on this hat, Crocodyl Dandy thinks he's at the forefront of fashion. Fashion must be pretty dull if that's the case. However, it'd be best if you didn't let him know how ridiculous he looks, after all, he is particularly touchy...

8844.d: This hood, a royal headdress, shares the same virtues as the Mopy King Sovereign Cape. Its micro-vents allow sweat to drain away more easily, so you'll always have a cool head. Unfortunately, it also has the same defects as the cape: its foul stench is so strong, you could almost cut it with a knife.

8845.d: Though it is less efficient than the royal hood, this one allows for a good draining of the sweat. Maybe too good, actually. As a result, whether you wear it or not, it doesn't make any difference.

8846.d: The Zoth girl's hat makes her see double. Strange. This is the reason she lisps.

8847.d: This helmet has the same advantages as other Zoth hats - it'll protect you from the sun no matter how hot it is, from blows dealt on the head, and it prevents the wearer from being aware of the danger by restricting his visual field. Anyway, this is the perfect warrior headgear.

8848.d: The Zoth Master hat has the great advantage of almost completely restricting your field of vision... This way, you have to hit out wildly, so you've some chance of hitting something.

8849.d: This stick is a firm favourite with the trunk-women. But it'll seduce any old kind of girl. Probably.

8850.d: If you're superstitious and always need to knock on wood, use the Floramor Root! On the other hand, you should try to be careful not to saw the branch you're sitting on and especially not to get your fingers in the way!

8851.d: Even though your eyes are wet with joy, you are still able to read that the treasure is hidden somewhere along the road of enslaved waters.

8854.d: You say that a kraken, with the foulest breath you've ever seen, follows you wherever you go? Well, deal with it: it's only a tiny inconvenience that comes with the hat!

8855.d: This shield is protecting you for now, but don't be fooled, it won't last.

8856.d: When the Bherb has got butterflies, he wears his Bherbal belt and healthily eliminates them.

8858.d: These boots create a disgusting suction noise with each step, which will remind you of a rutting Trool's love chant if you've ever heard it. A painful memory that you could easily live without.

8859.d: This seal indicates that its owner is the undisputed sovereign of the Bottomless Peat Bog of Otomai Island. It's hard to imagine a more pastoral kingdom...

8860.d: This ring was pulled off the still-warm finger of a freshly slaughtered Coralator. His mother was expecting him for dinner, until she saw him being transformed into a tombstone. Coralators are not as stone-hearted as people might imagine.

8861.d: Only Kimbos, with their weird feet, feel comfortable in these sandals. However, they're not the only ones who can benefit from their powers. But be careful not to wear them the wrong way!

8862.d: Parkinn Pan truly believed that he could fly thanks to this belt trimmed with Pikoko wings, but didn't know that very few Pikokos can fly. That's why every time he jumped off the Tree Keeholo he systematically crashed on the ground. His nickname "Cake" comes from "falling as flat as a pancake".

8863.d: This amulet is just a piece of wood with a strip of torn fabric. But Zoths are absolutely convinced that it has powers. Old fools!

8864.d: This bow string is made of Snailmet slobber, not too dry with a unique elasticity. However, its slimy and gooey texture reminds you of ... well, nothing really, but it's quite unpleasant.

8865.d: Carved in a Snailmet carapace, this ring can resist anything or anyone.

8866.d: Weaved from Zoth fabrics, this cape has extraordinary power of unknown origin.

8867.d: With this cape on, you'll be craving for some vinaigrette.

8868.d:
The Cheeken Beak on this weapon is absolutely useless, and can be more of a handicap than anything else. 
Fortunately, it is quite powerful.

8869.d: These boots are so heavy that they should actually be categorised as weapons. Indeed, they make the slightest kick lethal.

8870.d: Carved in a Dark Treeckler, this belt isn't pliable enough to let you move around easily, but at least, it'll protects you.

8871.d: Carved from a Light Treeckler, this belt won't afford you great protection, but at least it is soft enough to let you move around freely.

8872.d: This jewel is not precious but is the perfect size to balance the moorgale in a nice belgroot flavoured with a hint of Glaviooze.

8873.d: Finally a good excuse to smell of the sea!

8874.d: This jewel sometimes tries to steal some of your food when you're eating, so don't let it hang down too low.

8876.d: This strange cape seems to be made of black ink, but oddly enough, it behaves just like fabric - it doesn't run. As for stains, well, that's another matter. Your backside will never be clean again.

8877.d: Once round your finger, you won't be able to take it off, ever. Its suckers are way too powerful.

8878.d: This hammer is not handy, not particularly good looking, not very ergonomic, not powerful, too light, too fragile, unbalanced, too shiny and smelly. But at least it's got pretty colours.

8879.d: Unfortunately, this ring is only polished on the outside. You put your finger through a hole full of sharp rock fragments. It is recommended for Sacriers.

8880.d: It's the Mufafah moustaches that cause the wearer of this necklace to bellow so loudly. Why? They hang down and tickle the nipples constantly.

8881.d: Solo was a nice good-for-nothing, and he admitted as much himself. That didn't stop him from being hanged on the village square for stealing a thong belonging to the chief's wife. Solo wasn't a bright guy, no, but he was a nice guy all the same..

8883.d: This potion enables you to get back to your guild house.

8885.d: This Tabby Bow Meow hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

8886.d: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8887.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Tabby Bow Meow you've put in the Bow Kennels.
8887.n: Bow Kennel Certificate: Tabby Bow Meow

8888.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Mischievous Squirrel you've put into the Bow Kennels.

8889.d: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Leopardo you've put in the Bow Kennels.

Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.
