8913.d: This potion has been made from extracts of bulbs that soaked in Kloug mash. The most audacious alchemists use rice flour instead of Kloug mash, which can no longer be found. Even though it might seem impossible, you'll get used to its taste.

8914.d: This card contains all the necessary information to find the handyman described herein.

8915.d: This empty card should be filled with all the necessary information to find a Handyman.

8916.d: This amber is different from any other. If you close your eyes, shake it and dance the manic tango of Captain Chafer, you might feel it vibrate and glow as if a mysterious spirit inhabited it. To be honest though, you'll look like an idiot. A shiny, vibrating idiot.

8917.d: This strange key will let you enter the Grotto Hesque in one piece.

8918.d: In theory, this helmet should keep your wig on your head if you decide to go ride a Scaraleaf. Simply priceless!

8919.d: These improved wooden wings have been padded and made lighter thanks to feathers and high-quality fabric. Since the frame is still in wood, it will be hard not to crash!

8922.d: This purse contains a considerable amount of Kamas. Choose carefully who you bribe.

8923.d: A bag of potatoes? What are you doing with a bag of potatoes? Idiot.

8924.d: Once upon a time, a man named Rahm got lost in the jungle. Have you heard of Viet Rham?

8925.d: This strange bow was carved by a Sadidette during a very productive sleep-stroll. Just looking at it makes you feel sleepy - that goes for the archer as well as the target.

8926.d: These daggers are perfect for pushing pineapples and shaking trees, or pushing pineapples and grinding coffee, if that's what takes your fancy. Just remember: to the left, to the right, jump up and down and to the knees.

8927.d: Long ago there lived a mad Sram called Gaga... this guy, he robbed from the poor and gave to the rich.

8928.d: Porkeez is a better drinker than he is a fighter, and let me tell you he doesn't get any better as time passes by. All the same I wouldn't go around looking like a cork when he's got his daggers out.

8929.d: This should not be mistaken for the famous staff of similar name. The blades on this implement spill far more blood.

8930.d: Many a proud adventurer refused this weapon because of its colour. Many the same died by its blade.

8931.d: This sword used to belong to an old power hungry Enutrof. Just like his ego, it's made of solid gold.

8932.d: Smile! Say cheese! Perfect! Sliced in half!

8933.d: Ourag'han was an old Pandawa with skin so soft he was known as Slippiderm. His odour on the other hand gave rise to another name altogether. He christened his trusty axe likewise.

8934.d: Driven into a horticidal rage when a mischievous squirrel stole a grain of his rice during a summer holiday on Pandawa Island, Brouce Boulgour used this axe to flatten each and every bamboo shoot the squirrel hopped onto. The Pandawas in the village had to feed him half their stock of bamboo wine to keep him from razing the entire forest. Trust old Broucey.

8935.d: Even as a young Iopette, Mel dreamt of slaying dragons. With a spade for a sword and a rock for a dragon, she honed her skills in the back yard. The mere mention of a shovel now has the poor rock in convulsions.

8936.d: This is a wild shovel which tries to bite its owner each time it's picked up. It makes the most unusual sounds when it's happy and can only be pacified with the soothing sound of chimes.

8937.d: A cunning Enutrof became a pirate after noticing that there were more treasures to be found on fresh corpses than in rotten graves. This blood-red shovel was his symbol and filled the sailors of the Asse Sea with terror.

This candy increases wisdom by 20 points for 5 fights.

8989.d: If you spin around at the speed of sound while wearing this helmet, you'll take off. As for landing, well, you'll have to sort it out.

8990.d: This magical stone can fill the darkest corner with a shimmering glow - no need to waste your precious urine to mark your territory. Not to be used in moderation if you have a conquering spirit. Warning! You can place a prism only if you clearly display your rank (with the player versus player mode activated), and if you are in an area with no other prisms. The area where you want to place a conquest prism must be adjoining at least a 5-minute old ally area.

8991.d: This cold, slimy ring never stops sucking on your finger from the minute you slip it on. If you can see past its flaws, however, its great powers are yours to wield.

8992.d: This blade cuts wheat as well as enemies, but it also makes your allies extremely jealous. That's the destiny of powerful people.

8993.d: This sword holds an immense power of which the many victims fill chapters in the history books. On the other hand, wielding this weapon has proven mortally dangerous. Is there someone who can tame its vicious force?

8994.d: This humid rag was long hidden underwater where particles of coral covered its surface thread by thread. It's a pity it's as hard as stone - it would have made a nice hanky.

8995.d: Used in the past as a blister bandage by Gourlo the Terrible, this fabric is still impregnated with a dizzying stench. The funny thing is, one sniff and you'll be overcome with an irresistible hunger.

8996.d: This skin is softer than a Kilibris' bottom. Fat lot of good it will do you.

8997.d: This skin probably covered a sensitive area of the Tynril. Poor lad.

8998.d: Let me tell you a little story... for many long years, the Kimbo sucked on this precious stone to soften it up. Then he shoved it up his nostril. Hmm, sometimes mother nature suckles her runts.

9001.d: This shield will remind your opponents you grew up in the Sidimote moors. That alone could be enough to scare them away.

9002.d: This shield is covered with peepers to allow you to give one of those devastating multi-evil-eyes. Unstoppable.

9003.d: The Innkeeper at the Feubuk Brewery in Bonta was bored to death one day when he suddenly got the idea of equipping his bouncers with neon advertising shields.

9004.d: To stave off wicked or tough hits, this shield from Akwadala should do.

9005.d: When your allies run out of breath, or when you want to clear the air after an unexpected wind of panic, this shield can save your life. The only thing you need to do is to shake it energetically in all directions, like you'd do with a hungry baby.

9006.d: Originally, this shield was used as a stool by the Sadidas when they needed to rest. If you tuck in your feet, it will protect you from a wide range of attacks. Nothing will protect you from the cruel laughter of your opponents though.

9007.d: This surprising creation is covered in the Leather Briefs of the Lancer Chafer, which have been boiled, cleaned and stretched so that they hug the arm as perfectly as they did the full, generous curves of Lancer Chafer's... I think that's quite enough of that actually.

9008.d: This magnificent shield contains a few drops from the Asse Sea. Not only does it bring good luck but it can also be used as a flask.

9009.d: Hidden behind this shield, some naïve adventurers could mistake you for a Treechnid and run off screaming. Most will attack all the more eagerly, thinking they can get some amber out of you.

9010.d: Perfect if you want to fit in on Pandala, or to stand out anywhere else! The biggest advantage of this shield is that it's entirely covered with hypoallergenic Pandawa hair, so now you don't need to pack your underwear and your armour in separate suitcases when you take your vacation.

9011.d: This special shield will protect you from the Fire element and will also give your opponents plenty of time... Time to make their last wishes that is!

9012.d: This special shield will protect you from the Air element and will also give your opponents plenty of time... Time to make their last wishes that is!

9013.d: This special shield will protect you from the Earth element and will also give your opponents plenty of time... Time to make their last wishes that is!

9014.d: This special shield will protect you from the Water element and will also give your opponents plenty of time... Time to make their last wishes that is!

9015.d: This shield used to protect Lumberjacks from falling trees. Its function quickly changed and now it is more often used to it to protect warriors from enemies who tend to land on them without warning!

9016.d: Greenish and smelly, this shield remains a first choice for protection when it comes to fighting the creatures of green and smelly Mount Stinkky.

9017.d: If your dearest dream is to become a real imp, this is the shield you need. Passed down from generation to generation, it will enable you to rob all the young Astrubian adventurers you like without getting hurt.

9018.d: A renowned adventurer spent his whole life looking for all four quarters of this shield. Some say that when the shield is complete, it has the exact opposite effect as that of breaking a mirror.

9019.d: Not all Wabbits are nice little creatures. In fact, all Wabbits are vile creatures. Some get their kicks smashing up cawwots with this huge shield and taking baths in the juice.

9020.d: This shield of skin will fit you like a glove. Don't forget to treat its warts and furuncles from time to time to prevent them from getting worn.

9021.d: A young adventurer once dreamt of joining the Bonta militia to protect the oppressed. Considered morally unfit for service, he was contacted by an Amakna Alchemist who took advantage of his good nature, using him as a guinea-pig for his potions. You'll be glad to know that this is one story that ends... well, the middle bit is happy. He became so strong that he was known forever more as Captain Amakna and had this reputedly indestructible shield forged for him. The end... well, you don't wanna know the end.

9022.d: This huge shield saved the famous adventurer Kloome from an awful death: squashed under the weight of a Crackler who was in love with him. The legend doesn't say if he survived the side effects of his subsequent romance with the stony beast.

9023.d: As strange as it might sound, some say this shield of wood and hair enables the lightest adventurers to become airborne for a brief moment... a final attempt to shock their enemies before falling flat on their faces.

9024.d: LeChouque used this shield to protect himself from the friendly cannonballs his friends regularly tossed him. Some crazy stories tell that some of those balls were alive.

9025.d: Although it's all but useless, its stench alone will spread your fame far and wide. This shield accompanies many young adventurers on their first quests - maybe that's why so few make it to thirty...

9026.d: This shield is a tribute to Bowisse's Cloak which itself was a tribute to a famous relic composed of three triangular shapes. God all this history is putting me to sleep.

9027.d: This stone shield is in fact made from a Crackler's head, smashed by the foot of a Minotoror. A perfect combination of big head and smelly feet.

9028.d: To stave off wicked or tough hits, this shield from Terrdala should do.

9029.d: To stave off wicked or tough hits, this shield from the village of Feudala should do.

9030.d: To stave off wicked or tough hits, this Shield from the village of Aerdala should do.

9031.d: In his time, Gore Master was very strong and had all he needed - money, women, and more. He didn't quite deserve all of it since he got his strength from his nice ring. Until the day he carelessly crossed the street. And BAM! No more Gore Master. Since then, unscrupulous people pass it on to other unscrupulous people.

9035.d: This potion enables you to go back to your guild paddock.

9036.d: This potion enables you teleport to the Zoth Village, if you happen to own it.

9037.d: This potion enables you to unveil all the invisible characters surrounding you.

9038.d: This potion will make you so angry that you'll automatically attack enemies that get too close.

9039.d: This potion lets you teleport yourself to the closest ally prism.

9040.d: This potion will make you so angry that you'll automatically attack enemies that get too close.

9044.d: This potion will allow you to take on the appearance of your choosing. Watch out, your mum might call the police if she finds you in your bed tomorrow morning.

9060.d:
Part of a letter someone has torn up. Upon it, you read: '... as we arranged, I'll make sure the investigation into this merchant goes nowhere. Come and pay me the amount we agreed where we usually meet... where the women are pretty...' 
The letter is signed X.

9061.d: Exoram has to be escorted out of the goblin camp and up to the Sram temple.

9062.d: This document contains lots of interesting information about a guy named Xephires. What's most amazing is the amount of time he spends in the Drunken Pandawa Inn.

9063.d: This incredible list was given to you by Milone the Jeweller. It tells you of the objects necessary to create a sumptuous jewel.

9064.d: Is it really any different to ordinary slobber? It certainly doesn't look like it.

9065.d: This hastily written letter explains to Milone that the jewel is in danger... so why are you still reading this? Get going!!!

9066.d:
This was found on one of the burglars you beat at Milone's house:
Milone the jeweller has just created a very valuable jewel. Steal it by whatever means necessary. Fortunately, Milone gave them a copy, but it's no thanks to you.
On the back of the message, though, there is a guide to their hideout. A friendly visit? Why yes! Still, you probably shouldn't go alone.

9067.d: This letter from Oto Mustam explains to Xephires the plan in detail.

9068.d: You and Milone the Jeweller joined forces to create this jewel. It'll sell for a fortune... if you ever manage to find anyone who wants it, that is.

9069.d: Oto describes the conditions for corrupting Xephires.

9070.d: This sword really is unusual. You've never seen such a thing in Bonta.

9071.d: Innkeeper Feubuk received the Ecaflips who mentioned Loudac's name.

9072.d: Innkeeper Pinchaut heard some guards talking about their problems with a gang of Ecaflips.

9073.d: You found this emblem on the Ecaflip Plain Bandits around Cania.

9074.d: This jewel will be just perfect for luring the bandit chief into your trap.

9075.d: This letter was transmitted to you through Marge the Jeweller. Bring the jewel to Ekysoy Kubnan in the Woodenglass Inn. It'll be quicker for us and more profitable for you.

9076.d: This jewel looks just like the one Amayiro sent you to get.

9077.d: This Feca skull will make a perfect bookend.

9078.d: A Tofu here, a Magus Bwork there... This Osamodas disciple just lost his head!

9079.d: This trophy was already old before it became a trophy.

9080.d: This trophy was already morbid before became a trophy.

9081.d: This skull is often mistaken for that of the famous mummy Tuthan Kamha. But don't be fooled, these bandages are not made with melted Kamas, but with some papier-mâché.

9082.d: That's enough of heads or tails. How about a game of knucklebones instead!

9083.d: Don't be cruel ... this isn't a sparrow's skull!

9084.d: This trophy is as empty now as it was when it was supposed to be living...

9085.d: This cute Cra skull seems to be coming out of a recent archaeological dig.

9086.d: What? There's actually a skull underneath this huge bunch of hair?!

9087.d: This Sacrier can't show off anymore with his thousands of health points.

9088.d: One could have thought that after being hung over such a long period of time, the Pandawa would have appreciated to be placed in a coffin!

9089.d: You found this insignia during the (very easy) skirmish with Bontarian forces.

9090.d: You found this insignia during the skirmish with Brakmarian forces.

9094.d: This stuff looks more like mint jelly than poison. Bworks aren't known for making jelly, though... and neither are Brakmarian spies, which is even more worrying.

9096.d: The tactician agreed to follow you to your leader.

9097.d: You found this badge on a particularly frightening militiaman who vanquished several warriors from Brakmar. His equipment seemed very strange.

9098.d: This hammer will prove to Oto that you've vanquished the mercenary smith of Bonta.

9099.d: Signed by Amayiro, this letter is a request for official help.

9100.d: Lenglad won't want people gossiping about him for a very long time.

9101.d: In this toolbox are all the tools that Nara the blacksmith forgot.

9103.d: This letter, dated to a week ago, explains in detail the plan to attack Bonta. You'll need to be careful though, because a note at the end says the plan is still to be confirmed and may be changed in the coming days by officer Kapp Tenn. As a result, you'll have to find out what's happening with the plan at the moment.

9104.d: You found this insignia on a Brakmarian patrol you attacked at the Cemetery of the Tortured.

9105.d: Someone slipped this letter into your bag while Amayiro was giving you your mission: Retrieve the documents, but bring them back to me rather than Amayiro. You will be rewarded. Danathor.

9106.d: These documents contains lots of information on Bonta's defence system. But who are you going to give them to?

9107.d:
Break into the Tower of Brakmar at midnight and collect up all the documents that you find on the second floor. Come back to Bonta via the East road.
No, that's not what YOU have to do, they're the instructions for the spy you have to save.

9108.d: These documents contains lots of secret information on the Fogornleg Horn.

9109.d: This tattered old bandana is in a right state. It's covered in phlegm, like it's been used as a handkerchief by generations of Wabbits. It belongs to Elturt, that much is obvious, as despite the stink of cawwots, you can still smell rotten herring. It must contain very powerful magic if it still smells that bad after so many years.

9110.d: You tried blowing in it, but nothing much happened.

9112.d:
Break into the Tower of Bonta at midnight, cut the throats of anyone that tries to stop you, and collect all the documents you find on the first floor. Then return to Brakmar by road.
No, that's not what YOU have to do, those were the instructions for the spy that you have to find.

9113.d: These are the documents that the injured spy recovered from the Tower of Bonta.

9114.d: The secret documents that the injured spy found in the tower of Bonta. They were slightly crumpled during your fight against the Bontarian forces.

9115.d: This salad was prepared in the primordial cauldron, which has given it special qualities. To find out what they are, you'll have to taste it. Sadly, it's destined for Elturt's consumption. Life can be so cruel sometimes.

9116.d: A weapon, a helmet, a shield: this crate contains rudimentary but effective equipment for warriors.

9117.d: It was only a matter of time before they started making hammers from the head of this thick-skulled dummy.

9122.d: Once it wraps its Bloppish way round your finger, it's impossible to get rid of this ring.

9123.d: Once it wraps its Bloppish way round your finger, it's impossible to get rid of this ring.

9124.d: Once it wraps its Bloppish way round your finger, it's impossible to get rid of this ring.

9125.d: Once it wraps its Bloppish way round your finger, it's impossible to get rid of this ring.

9126.d: Kroula had a plan. He was going to put this ring on his big toe, get Blops to lick his feet and collect litres of Royal Blop juice. Well, the ring didn't fit.

9127.d: Kroula had a plan. He was going to put this ring on his big toe, get Blops to lick his feet and collect litres of Royal Blop juice. Well, the ring didn't fit.

9128.d: Kroula had a plan. He was going to put this ring on his big toe, get Blops to lick his feet and collect litres of Royal Blop juice. Well, the ring didn't fit.

9129.d: Kroula had a plan. He was going to put this ring on his big toe, get Blops to lick his feet and collect litres of Royal Blop juice. Well, the ring didn't fit.

9130.d: This rough copy of the Big Ougaa is worn around the neck... a hungry stare and a well-kept beard are essential.

9131.d: A young Craette named Colette once lost her head in Eltneg Wood. The poor girl stepped in the way of Brouce Boulgoure's hatchet which he threw thinking she was a giant fern. Lucky she didn't live, she would have died if she'd found out she looked like a giant fern.

9132.d: Are your fingers too young to get into the good clubs? Are they nervous around the girls? Well, stick this ring on, it'll add a few years to their age and do wonders for their self-confidence.

9133.d: Dangle your fingers in front of any enemies who are allergic to mushrooms. Makes for a quick fight.

9134.d: This bow is made from sharp, thin and very flexible slats that are more often used to make beds than deadly weapons. Now they're used to bring on a more permanent sort of sleep. Quite a coincidence.

9135.d: This trumpet-shaped fungal wand was used long ago to call the wandering minstrel, Jon Lemon to the scene of battle. When he began singing, everyone who hadn't blocked their ears died on the spot. When the insufferable song and dance man began getting too popular, the gods blocked the trumpet and transformed it into a relatively harmless wand.

9136.d: The three points of this staff can attract the particles of Plasmogrine present in the quadramental breeze. To do this, you must carefully lick the points of the stick, align them with the hands of an inverted Xelor clock, count to sixty (try six if you're a Iop) and squeeze your buttocks together. You'll have a fifty fifty chance of making a thunder bolt... and changing your enemies into grizzly Kirballs.

9137.d: These knives were used to scrape the feet of kings and queens, relieving them of the worms and fungi that cling to anyone with a bit of power.

9138.d: The triple blades of this axe had been used for many years for cutting hams and cheeses three times faster than usual. If you see a warrior carrying one about, though, run away very fast... you've most likely just seen a cannibal.

9139.d: These toeless boots are perfect for teaching a good lesson to those who dare speak of the forbidden things.

9140.d: Contrary to popular misconception, the holes in these shoes are not there to let your feet breathe, but to let the spawn of your foot fungus escape and infect the feet of other footloose adventurers.

9141.d: If there wasn't so much mould on this rag, it would make a great tablecloth. Not to worry, you can always dry the dishes with it when your guests aren't watching.

9142.d: One more glass for the road? Ah, well, roads are long and nights are short, so this cape is usually used to keep the barflies warm as they finish their endless rounds of night caps. It'll kill them in the end, you know.

9143.d: As its name suggests, this string assassinates any flies that get too close to your sweet spots. Just one piece of advice - never, ever pull it off a loved one with your teeth.

9144.d: The best way to solve crotch fungus is to lure it elsewhere. As there's no longer room between your toes to accommodate any more fungi, you can use this belt, a truly impressive residence for any fungus worthy of the name.

9145.d: Take an Elm, strip the bark off, soak it for a few months in a muddy puddle, cover it with fungal infections, stick it under your bed for a week while you sleep on the floor, basting it regularly with Blop fat. All you need to know to make an Elm belt that stinks. Are you happy now?

9146.d:
The tag on this belt says 'Sorry, but if you're looking for a way to get Ougaa's power, this belt is not for you.' 
Well that's just great, isn't it.

9147.d: Take a Dora, cover it in Gobball spit and Iop sweat, let it stew for a couple of weeks and you'll get an idea of the intoxicating effects of the Mush Ombrero. Try to stay away from heavy machinery while you wear it. In fact, stay away from anything that's heavy.

9148.d: Instead of cutting down on impure Blop juice, Shika Ingalsse pressed on with her harvest through her inebriated state. One day, as she was stumbling and falling through the golden fields, Shika landed on this ring. Whoever said that impure Blop juice should be taken in moderation?

9149.d: When Lorkos set off on his trip to the Labyrinth of the Minotoror, the first thing he did was put on his Amublop. No one ever found out why.

9150.d: When Lorkos set off on his trip to the Labyrinth of the Minotoror, the first thing he did was put on his Amublop. No one ever found out why.

9151.d: When Lorkos set off on his trip to the Labyrinth of the Minotoror, the first thing he did was put on his Amublop. No one ever found out why.

9152.d: When Lorkos set off on his trip to the Labyrinth of the Minotoror, the first thing he did was put on his Amublop. No one ever found out why.

9153.d: This Amublop costs a lot more to make than an ordinary Amublop, but look on the bright side... it will sell for a lot more too, especially if you offload it on an Astrubian.

9154.d: This Amublop costs a lot more to make than an ordinary Amublop, but look on the bright side... it will sell for a lot more too, especially if you offload it on an Astrubian.

9157.d: They have to put heaps of artificial colorants and flavourings into this amulet to stop it coming out white when it's crafted. A word of advice, it might look great and smell delicious, but don't try to eat it.

9158.d: Does it make your mouth feel funny when you say the name of this object? Well, let me tell you, if you find yourself face to face with a highway robber who asks you for your 'Boot.. Bloops... Bloo...', you'll be glad to have just enough time to scurry off while he figures out how to pronounce the word. So stop your complaining.

9162.d: Say the word Bloopts ten times fast while spinning round in circles. Now you know what it feels like to be a Iop.

9166.d: Some people let the grass grow under their feet. With these boots, you'll have enough foliage for four weddings and a funeral.

9167.d: Behind the silly name is a belt. A belt that we don't know much about. Its original design and its magical ability to conceal the worst love-handles known to science ensure this is always a favourite with image-conscious middle-aged men.

9168.d: Behind the silly name is a belt. A belt that we don't know much about. Its original design and its magical ability to conceal the worst love-handles known to science ensure this is always a favourite with image-conscious middle-aged men.

9170.d: Behind the silly name is a belt. A belt that we don't know much about. Its original design and its magical ability to conceal the worst love-handles known to science ensure this is always a favourite with image-conscious middle-aged men.

9171.d: The tiniest bluesman in the world is playing the blues for this belt on the tiniest guitar in the world. It lost its buckle. If belts could cry, this one would never stop sobbing.

9172.d: The tiniest bluesman in the world is playing the blues for this belt on the tiniest guitar in the world. It lost its buckle. If belts could cry, this one would never stop sobbing.

9174.d: The tiniest bluesman in the world is playing the blues for this belt on the tiniest guitar in the world. It lost its buckle. If belts could cry, this one would never stop sobbing.

9175.d: If you tighten this belt fully, you can shut down your digestive system completely. Why you would want to do this is another question entirely.

9176.d: Jon Lemon created his last and greatest song as he was being slaughtered by the Bworker and this very blade. Goes a little something like - 'I heard the news today oh boy, Ten thousand holes all over meeeee...' Thank the gods that the Bworker had the good sense to jot down the words and music of the ditty.

9177.d: The three points of this bracelet represent the three major weaknesses of the Bworker: Thirst for vengeance, thirst for victory and, well, thirst for liquids.

9178.d: This ring is covered in little bits of nose rubble from the Bworker's shnoz. The dirty creature uses the sharp points to achieve that perfect pick.

9179.d: When a certain Captain Chafer met the Bworker for the first time, he took the liberty of saying 'Wow, is that your backside or is it your face?' Nobody has seen the good Captain, or his famous moulded underwear, since. This amulet was created in his memory.

9180.d: The story goes that the Bworker sewed this cape from Rushu's butt skin. The story would be entirely believable if the Bworker actually knew how to sew.

9181.d: This helmet holds its fair share of secrets. It was once a kind, gentle, pure creature, but after many years of violent adventures with the Bworker, it slowly became bitter and twisted. Then, it died. The legend says a mischievous Ecaflip found the dead hat and dyed it grey using a Payntshup Potion and some Kralove ink. He fooled the inhabitants of Imp Village by claiming it had fantastic powers but he was rumbled when it rained and the dye washed out.

9182.d: A long, long time ago, Danous Kwaide wanted to be clever and beat the Bworker in a baiting contest: "Your boots are covered with earrings because you're too stupid to realise that you're not supposed to put boots in your ears", he teased. The Bworker replied by crushing Danous' skull with his axe. Do you blame him? Do you even understand what Danous was going on about? No, neither do I.

9183.d: This belt is used in the feast of the Dofus eggs which celebrates the gift of the six eggs, as recorded in the Biibl, an ancient text written by a Bontarian Joiner. Most people just paint ordinary eggs to look like Dofus and give them to one another, but some go a bit further, wearing this painful belt for the forty days and nights which precede the feast.

9184.d: In spite of appearances, this helmet won't help your hearing. It'll help you see farther, though. Just watch out for any strong winds or you'll be taken away like a little feather.

9185.d: This headgear won't really make you any more fearsome, and definitely not more powerful... And if you think for a moment that some naïve souls will mistake you for Goultard, well you're crazy. Your enemies will see you coming from miles away, that's all.

9186.d: Beyond his love for porcelain vases, there's little we know about Flash Gorgone. One legend says he was always in such a hurry that he could out run a Tofu... He learnt his lesson when he rushed out of bed one morning and tied his belt round his ankles. His porcelain collection still remembers that like it was yesterday.

9187.d: Master Black Jack, the Eniripsa, was a dedicated follower of fashion. So much so, that he was even able to give stitches to real people after a while! A friend to tailors, they say that his inspiration for this headgear was a cruel tailor who once exterminated a tribe of Ouginaks called the Macians. What a lovely story.

9188.d: This sombrero is the last trace left behind by a dark, heroic Xelor who is said to have disappeared suddenly. The last time he was sighted, he was serenading his beloved. What is more, they say his fiancée's brothers were in the know about the whole thing. Still others say he was whisked away into a parallel dimension just like that. The mystery shows no signs of solving itself.

9189.d: If you keep trying to butt the horns off your enemies, you're the one whose head will start to resemble a sieve! XVII's horns have the same effect - they make you forget everything. Except dinner time, maybe.

9190.d: This headgear is just perfect for Cras who don't mind looking average. Careful though, you will look very silly, stupid even. Usually this headgear is given to retired combatants who've lost a good portion of their brain-cells.

9191.d: This blade was stolen from a sword smith's shop window where it had laid for many years. Let's hope it sees more use in your hands than it did in the shop, because I think we both know that nobody will pay money for it.

9192.d: The bigger your love handles are the better with this attractive and delicious belt.

9193.d: This amulet will remind you of the happy days, the picnic days, the days before you turned into... this.

9194.d: Lice used to eat your head. Not anymore, this new range of confectionary headgear will divert the nasty creatures. Now they'll graze on your hat instead, like a herd of tiny, white cows.

9195.d: Roll it up in fruity jam, cover it in jelly and resist the temptation to scoff it. This treat is best enjoyed as a suppository.

9196.d: Made from enormous coffee beans, this cape smells like a Pikoko's armpit. It really gets the blood flowing before a battle... and it's cheap, too.

9197.d: Pop in two sugars, give it a quick stir and quench your thirst with this revitalizing hat.

9198.d: If you find yourself stuck with a tasteless beer or coffee, stick this ring in there for a while.

9199.d: Look what you've done. Just look. Trying to smash coffee cups with your boots... what were you thinking?

9200.d:
(Double click to learn the spell) 
This Scroll teaches you the spell 'Summoning of Chaferfu'.

9201.d: This Scwoll weveals how to teach youwself, in 101 simple lessons, the basics of the famous but not particulawly secwet Wa Wabbit technique.

9202.d: Even in death, the Gore Master kept crafting items that were out of kilter with the cosmic order of the universe. He always complained that he made his second ring too late. That he could have travelled the world if he'd made it sooner. In the end, a demon stole it from him and hid it in the mortal world for feeble adventurers.

9207.d: This piece of leather appears to have been snatched from the strap of a bag.

9210.d: A piece of paper for the judge Satirev Onivin on which Gwenolaz Barnumuze wrote that she was not for sale.

9211.d: A sheet of paper for the attention of judge Satirev Onivin on which Enileda uses very flowery words to express her refusal.

9212.d: A letter of refusal to submit to the judge Satirev Onivin from Ma Cleopatra on which is written 'We do not have the same values...'

9213.d: A draft paper for the judge Satirev Onivin on which Maskara scrawled that she refused to become his puppet.

9214.d: A message written by Kwartzwatch for Satirev Onivin. The text suggests that she'd never take off her bandages for him.

9227.d: This list has been provided by Satirev Onivin, and details the Astrubian women he'd like you to talk to on his behalf: Ma Cleopatra, Enileda, Gwenolaz Barnumuze, Maskara, Kwartzwatch.

9228.d: Miss Yelliott's testimony is written down on this piece of paper.

9229.d: Miss Yelliott's somewhat dubious testimony is written down on this piece of paper.

9233.d: This living polymorphous object can either be a predator or a symbiote of inanimate capes. (This cape is a living thing. You must feed it other capes to keep it healthy and strong. Give it a meal, say, every 12 hours.)

9234.d:
This living polymorphous object can either be a predator or a symbiote of inanimate hats.  
(This hat is a living thing. You must feed it other hats to keep it healthy and strong. Give it a meal, say, every 12 hours.)

9235.d: This letter shows that you think there's something dodgy about Kit Dingaround's version of events.

9236.d: This letter shows that you think Kit Dingaround's version of events is to be believed.

9237.d: This letter shows that you find Miss Yelliott to be a credible witness, unless it's her so-called "music" that you enjoy.

9238.d: This letter shows that you find Miss Yelliott's version of events to be suspicious, unless it's simply because you do not like the way she speaks... or sings.

9239.d: This letter shows that you think Gnirreh didn't do it. What? Smelling of fish can be good, sometimes...

9240.d: This letter shows that you think Gnirreh actually slipped the secret document into Kit Dingaround's bag, or maybe it's revenge for the terrible odour that accompanies him.

9241.d: This letter shows that you believe Kit Dingaround is guilty of treason.

9242.d: This letter shows that you believe Kit Dingaround is innocent.

9243.d: This letter shows that you pleaded against Kit Dingaround. Danathor was pleased with your choice.

9244.d: This letter shows that you pleaded in Kit Dingaround's favour. Amayiro was pleased with your choice.

9245.d: This letter shows that you were not very convincing during the trial of Kit Dingaround and that the case against him has been dismissed. No need to wait for Danathor or Amayiro's recognition.

9247.d: This key grants you access to the terrible Fungus Dungeon.

9248.d: This key grants you access to the Blop Dungeon.

9249.d: If you find the other pieces of this key, you'll have to go and fight the Rainbow Blop. If you don't want to look for the other pieces anymore after hearing that, I understand.

9254.d: This key grants you access to the Rainbow Blop Dungeon.

9255.d: This living polymorphous object can either be a predator or a symbiote of inanimate amulets. (This amulet is a living thing. You must feed it other amulets to keep it healthy and strong. Give it a meal, say, every 12 hours.)

9256.d: This living polymorphous object can either be a predator or a symbiote of inanimate rings. (This ring is a living thing. You must feed it other rings to keep it healthy and strong. Give it a meal, say, every 12 hours.)

9263.d: A parasite never feels so at home as when he's lodged in the bark of a Mushnid. From time to time the creature will scratch itself, tearing off a part of its diseased skin which can turn into a mushroom itself if it falls in the right place. This mushroom will then find the nearest Mushnid to parasite... as vicious circles go, this one is pretty gruesome.

9265.d: Here are some Miteters, those strange things you sometimes find on the heads of Cracklers with dubious personal hygiene.

9266.d: This blubber came from a Royal Jelly. It's an essential ingredient of paralysis potions.

9267.d: This Trumperelle trunk still has the toxic breath of its former owner. Now it's usually used as a phony musical instrument to kill whole audiences at 'assassination concerts.'

9268.d: This Hammer of Light seems to have lost the spirit that gave it its power. As such, it doesn't look particularly impressive.

9269.d: The Mushmunch has a tongue of incredible length and softness for licking spores off its companions. If I'm not mistaken, it's the only enviable trait they have.

9270.d: A doll made by Maskara's skilled hands to replace the one that the Spirit of Light lost.

9271.d: This simple ring symbolises the promise Maskara made. She will play dolls with you (and especially be your doll) whenever she can. This makes it one of the most valuable assets in the world.

9272.d: You dared to steal this crate from your own Tower of Orders to give it to the Rogues, without even knowing what it contains. To do so is to betray the trust that your Order Master put in you.

9277.d: The Mush Mish has the annoying habit of wanting to scratch its itchy eyes with its pointy staff. Sometimes it loses an eye, and sometimes when it scratches its neck, it loses its head.

9278.d: The Mush Tup has two arms, two legs and two heads. All this means is that it's two times dumber than you'd expect.

9279.d: This spit is delicious, if a little slimy. It's often used to grease weapons. Or warriors if they enjoy fighting with no clothes on.

9280.d: This beast only has four spines on its head, but what spines... sharp as gads they are!

9281.d: Ougaa has stunning headgear, and you're holding a piece of her special hat in your hands.

9339.d: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. For once, the gods might not have been pulling your leg.

9366.d: This pink tutu will be ideal for showing your little behind off at the New Year's festivities. Made of ancestral cotton and stretchy Sponge Mob mousse, soft and comfortable with a swishing skirt, this piece could be the first in a long line of tutus for a future star dancer.

9379.d: You should give this small box to the one you love. If you're the kind of person who hates everyone, you may as well eat it yourself!

9380.d: This special Fairywork will spread some love in this World for the tough, but shower you with hugs in this World of love

9381.d: Gluttonous Greedoblops get so hungry that they'll even consider eating their own flowers. Fortunately, their snappy jaws always seem to stumble upon a wandering adventurer just in time.

9382.d: This flower has been plucked from the head of a Blopshroom. Don't worry about it, the Blopshroom never liked it anyway.

9383.d: The Trunkiblop has great big roots which draw up anything adventurers throw on the ground.

9384.d: If this flower wasn't royal, I bet you would have thrown it out by now.

9385.d: If this flower wasn't royal, I bet you would have thrown it out by now.

9386.d: If this flower wasn't royal, I bet you would have thrown it out by now.

9387.d: If this flower wasn't royal, I bet you would have thrown it out by now.

9388.d: When dried, rolled and smoked, this leaf can evoke hallucinations in the weakest adventurers, as well as an implacable urge for... relief. An overdose can lead to speedy death.

9389.d: This leaf feeds on the grey matter of the Royal Rainbow Blop. It's a good thing it's not too greedy!

9391.d: This flower was hidden in the cranial box of the Royal Rainbow Blop. It plugged up all the holes in the creature's memory.

9394.d: This headgear will give Mitcho-class style to anyone who wears it. It does have a strong smell of undergrowth that your friends could do without.

9395.d: This headgear was worn by Kuri herself for a few years. Until she decided to stop wearing crappy headgear, that is.

9396.d: Called 'Zawooin Ling' in the ancient language of the Lenalds... rumour has it that this item was forged in a volcano beneath Fire Pandala by Zeewon, a mysterious Wabbit.

9401.d: This skin has been through the wars and yet it has emerged unscathed. It should be just as useful now it's been removed from its former owner.

9402.d: The little wings attached to these slippers will give smelly feet some fresh air... But be careful, don't use them to play Gobbowl... Gobballs may not particularly like getting stung on the arse...

9403.d: The little wings attached to this hammer make it lighter and easier to handle... It can even fly on its own and hit you on the head while you're sleeping. Hilarious.

9404.d: The sting at the end of this cape will prevent your enemies from kicking your arse! However, you won't be able to sit down without getting hurt...

9405.d: By wearing this hat, you have to accept that you're running the risk of being hit by a Moskitoswatter...

9406.d: These Lousy Pig's ears are still warm and essential for you to seduce any Lousy Pig you'll come across. Don't laugh, you still don't know how lonely you can get in the Countryside of Amakna.

9407.d: Some people actually call this cape "Cloak Screw" and just hate anyone who calls it anything else. No matter what you call this cape, one thing's sure, it's useless for opening up bottles!

9408.d: This ring will turn you into a Lousy Pig, which should satisfy your closest friends.

9409.d: This little cork-screw shaped tail will bring out the jealousy of the people around you.

9410.d: Not as trendy as the Clint is, but a lot more elegant, this hat will show the others how sophisticated you are.

9411.d: This cape will protect your back from getting sunburnt. But be careful, it doesn't go all the way down to the behind of every adventurer.

9412.d: The sling of this belt is tightly tied to it, so tightly tied that you won't be able to take it off. It will only impress highwayboys you'll meet.

9413.d: The spurs on these boots will enable you to cut up your Dragoturkey when you decide it's time to eat it.

9414.d: Your head will easily fit this humongous emptied lemon and the little pip inside it will feel at home!

9415.d: This cape was made from the peels of lots of different citrus fruits. It's a pretty, refreshing cape, but unfortunately it doesn't glow in the dark.

9416.d: If your water becomes tasteless, just stick this ring on your finger, stick your finger in the glass and vigorously stir it in until it falls off. There you go! A delicious blood orange and lemon mixture... and one finger less. You can't have it all, you know...

9417.d: If you ever dreamt of drinking your enemies' blood while hitting them, this staff's made for you!

9418.d: The next barber who tries to give you a haircut will be lucky not to break their comb.

9451.d: This huge piece of crystal can be used as a rigid cape, though it won't make you stronger... But the next monster that will try to devour you, will choke on it.

9452.d: This ring will make your finger radiant.

9453.d: With this belt around your hips, no one will ever dare pinch you again for fear of having their fingers cut off.

9454.d: This amulet can be used as a bib for both the young and the old.

9455.d: You can wear this ring as a toe ring if you need to snuff out your foot odour.

9456.d: If you think your backside never had the attention it deserved, just put on this long cape which will dress it up and catch everyone's attention.

9457.d: This hat smells of Demonic Roses which should rid you off your lice, and any other form of parasites that squats your head.

9459.d:
Santa Jaws gets a twisted pleasure-pang when he reads the wish list of a child he's devoured.
You haven't written yours yet, so here's a sample.

9460.d: This is one Pokipik who'll never see the light of day. Aren't you ashamed of yourself?

9461.d: The Kimbo is said to wear this wig to pay tribute to a handsome, perfectly tanned young man that he met on his island. What a wonderful smile he had! Anyway, he hides the ridiculous wig under his coco.

9463.d: This jewel is so powerful that it'd kill a Moskito from 30 paces, if only its smell didn't prevent anything from getting that close!

9464.d: This scary amulet was hidden away in a remote mansion for ages. When it was alive, it used to dream of travelling around the world and all the places it would see. In the end, the only place it got to go around is your neck, the poor thing!

9468.d: This dangerous shovel will steal your vitality, your youth, the water in your body and your precious Troofles.

9469.d: Built up with fungi, this sword is perfect to infect your enemies' bowels.

9471.d: This magic hat can only be worn by adventurers who are not yet married, and so wearing it advertises your all-consuming desire to find a soulmate to all the other tragic loners in Amakna, who will flock around you at the nearest Zaap, clucking and squawking like broody hens. Inevitably someone will let off a few Fairyworks in a vain attempt to win your affection, but you'll end up with a splitting headache, be unable to speak, and have the feeling that you're walking through treacle.

9472.d:
Renowned for its aphrodisiac virtues, this sweet candy is the perfect gift for your beloved.
This candy gives between 11 and 20 HP and has a surprise!

9474.d: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 2000 souls using this soul stone.
9474.n: Risky Soul Stone for Sublime Souls

9475.d: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 2000 souls using this soul stone.
9475.n: Regular Soul Stone for Sublime Souls

9476.d: You'll have a good chance of capturing level 2000 souls using this soul stone.
9476.n: Lucky Soul Stone for Sublime Souls

9479.d: If nothing else, the pin nailed into this hat will shrink a big-head...

9480.d: With such a nice target sewn upon your cape, your enemies will have no excuse for missing you.

9481.d: The pin nailed into this shield can be used as an extra-close combat weapon and kill your enemies.

9482.d: If you don't want to scare your friends away with your ugly face, just hide it behind this nice, welcoming shield.

9483.d: When Iops get stars from their teachers for good work, they stick them to this shield. From time to time, they would stick them all over themselves to show off in front of their schoolmates.

9484.d: This shield isn't quite a full protection guarantee for the owner, but it is great at chasing ghosts.

9485.d: The three little balls at the bottom of this cape will enable you to give great headbutts if you learn how to spin!!

9486.d: Either with or without this hat, you'll look like a buffoon...But with it, at least, you'll have an excuse!

9487.d: This certificate was given to you by Morgan Faym'n. It contains some details which may interest you and it attests to your conversion.

9488.d: This register belongs to Morgan Faym'n and contains many documents, some of which explain how to become a Bontarian. Inside is a page that you must fill in yourself.

9489.d: This register belongs to Morgan Faym'n and contains many documents, some of which explain how to become a Brakmarian. Inside is a page that you must fill in yourself.

9490.d: This certificate states that you belong to an order. If you want to join another order, you have to wait seven days from the date you received your certificate. Even warriors get to change their mind from time to time. Don't make a habit of it, though!

9491.d: You now see life through rose-tinted glasses, and you're happy as a princess on Kwismas Island.

9525.d: This gift is a survival kit you might want to hold onto while going on dangerous love missions.

9526.d: You wrote a note on this piece of paper to remind yourself that you should never threaten an Astrubian when there are armed village guards nearby.

9527.d: Some old, powdered ingrown toenails which used to belong on the toes of an Enutrof. Many years have passed since it was ground down, but the powder still smells of feet. It makes you wonder if you might have been tricked...

9528.d: This powerful amulet used to belong to Lear, the leader of a long-defunct cult. Apparently he communicated with extra-dimensional beings and was able to clone souls. He was also able to resurrect himself... which must have been pretty handy when there were no priests about.

9529.d: Sometimes souls can't or even don't want to be reincarnated. This potion is useful for forcing them to regain their original forms.

9530.d: With a bit of luck, you'll be catching Gabby Tongues instead of Snappers with this rod.

9531.d:
This strange organ is sometimes used as part of the Gabby Tongue interrogation technique.
This underhanded method involves forcing the victim to swallow a Gabby Tongue, rendering them unable to speak without flailing around like a madman, as if they were moshing, or worse, slam-dancing. This tires them out very quickly, and then the secondary effects kick in - the victim mistakes the very first person they see for their best friend in the whole world. Getting information out of them when they're in this state is a piece of cake.

9532.d:
This is one of the two statuettes Maimane gave to Sumens and represents the goods and evils of mankind. It owes its appearance to a spell Sumens cast on it, who wanted to keep it safe from greedy hands.
Two questions remain: does this statuette represent good or evil? And most importantly, why does it look so ridiculous?

9533.d: This soul stone was enchanted by the master of the Order of the Putrid Eye himself and will coax souls into letting themselves be caught of their own free will.

9534.d: This soul stone contains the soul of Terra Bitya the Enutrof. You should take good care of it if you don't want your own soul to end up inside it.

9535.d:
If you manage to use it correctly, this potion can accelerate the growth of plants by modifying their genes. No one knows if there are any side affects when the plants are eaten, but shhhhh. What the customers don't know can't hurt them! 
You'll need two peasants and two alchemists to carry out the operation.

9536.d: This scroll activates the effects of the Transgenesis potion when it's poured on oat cereals.

9537.d: This book doesn't only contain twisted stories of walking and talking dead, it also describes the ritual for forcing a soul to return to its body.

9538.d: This potion allows you to recall a memory that was inadvertently lost.

9539.d: You took this badge from a Bontarian renegade who didn't deserve to have it.

9540.d: This cape will protect your neck from the wintry weather and your behind from low blows...

9541.d: This special hat will make you look like the Godfather. You should be proud!

9542.d: These shoes are very shiny even when they're worn out. They're perfect for impressing your opponents when they get them right in their faces.

9543.d: This heavy ring will give more power to your slaps and more passion to your caresses...

9544.d: This fearsome magic weapon was made by the famous handyman Hissering. It channels the magic energy of its user before shooting it out with great force. It also changes the appearance of its user and gives them new spells to use. With this weapon, you'll just become another person and your Tormentator your sole friend, until you decide you're done with it.
