11010.d: Using this powerful potion will increase the capacity of your pet permanently. Be careful though, only one dose will work. Trying more than once will cause disappointing results.

11011.d: Crazier than a regular Minifoux, but much less ginger, this pet can swim underwater without needing to block up its nose. It feeds on creatures that live in the Tree Keeholo.

11012.d: This pet may have stripes, but that won't stop it from sniffing your bottom or trying to relieve itself on your carpet. What did you expect? This pet loves to hunt the creatures that live in the Sidimote Moors.

11013.d: This ugly Black Quaquack was rejected by his own family because he was different: he loved listening to the songs of Jon Lemon, the famous minstrel. Maybe he was just misunderstood. After a difficult childhood, he decided to arbitrarily take revenge on all creatures of the Crow family. He devours them without pity.

11014.d: This pet stayed out too long in acid rain. It doesn't glow in the dark and it isn't magic, but you can make a very potent salad dressing from its saliva. It will only eat creatures from the Jelly family.

11015.d: This strange creature crossed the oceans on a block of ice to escape from a lost port. It looks like it's taken you for a block of ice. This soul-eating pet only likes the taste of beach creatures.

11040.d: Using this powerful potion will permanently increase the capacity of your pet. Be careful though, only one dose will work. Trying more than once will cause disappointing results.

11041.d: Heavy, clumsy, dull and ugly, just how was Goultard able to become such a formidable fighter using this mediocre sword? Wielding it yourself will not improve your skills, it will just make you look ridiculous.

11042.d: This belt was given to Goultard by his father for his 5th birthday. It is more solid than its appearance suggests, and will keep your trousers snugly around your hips. It can also be used as a washing line, or even a skipping rope.

11043.d: This hat is so tight-fitting that it compresses the skull and causes strong hallucinations. Fortunately, Goultard wore it when he was young, and what's more, he has quite a small skull, which betrays his roots.

11044.d: A few mouldering bones and some funereal jewellery is all that is left of Goultard's family.

11045.d: Goultard wore this mantle until he discovered the three sisters, when it was forgotten about in the back of an old cupboard.

11046.d: This cursed necklace's aura is so powerful you're having difficulty getting rid of the damned thing.

11047.d: Da Rorc has given himself up, escort him to Lethaline.

11048.d: A simple map and an intelligence potion. Even Dark Vlad should be able to escape from his maze with that.

11049.d: Slap this hat on your head, peel it for a few hours, and eventually, if you're lucky, you might find a tiny pip.

11050.d: The cape, which releases a pleasant citrus aroma as you walk, will transform you into a powerful Moskito trap.

11051.d: If you dip this amulet into your glass, your tasteless water will be transformed into a delicious, citrus-flavoured beverage.

11052.d: The soles of these boots are made from the tough skin of fruit harvested on an island whose very existence remains unknown to mere mortals.

11055.d: Padded with Bow Meow hair and covered with bark, this hat is extremely flammable. You should not sit on it if your pants are on fire.

11056.d: In hot weather, this cape's scales spread open to help your sweat evaporate. When it rains, this cape's scales spread open to let the rain in and rinse your posterior.

11057.d: This belt is composed of scales arranged spirally in accordance with the Vibronacci suite.

11058.d: Who were you hoping to seduce with a ring like this?

11071.d: Stained, spotted and wrinkled, these few pages are almost illegible. However, through the thick layer of grime you can still make out some words. These pages are an extract from a forgotten book detailing Goultard's origins.

11077.d: When it comes to sounding out his opponents, Lonne Jenone has more than one string to his fiddle - he uses it as a hammer. One thing is certain: sparks will fly!

11078.d: This leather cape, though light, will accompany you on all your incredible rides on the back of a Dragoturkey...

11079.d: Before being worn by Lonne Jenone, this hat belonged to Sergeant Payper, who was a rather quiet chap rarely prone to sticking his oar in.

11080.d: This versatile pair of boots will guarantee full freedom of movement, which is the reason that Lonne Jenone wears them when he dances with Boowolves.

11082.d: These boots were specially designed to destroy your opponents' shin pads, and then their shins, and then your own toes.

11083.d: You can use this ring to puncture the Gobbowl Ball when you want to quietly enjoy a break in play.

11084.d: Gadget was one of the most creative handymen the World of Twelve has ever seen. Unfortunately, he was also one of the most stupid. They say he mistook his wife's head for his anvil on more than one occasion, although she didn't complain, apparently.

11085.d: If you wear this belt upside down and press on it hard enough, you may be able to activate its integrated retromagic module. It has never worked, but you can activate it anyway. Then you can then sell it on to someone even more naive than you.

11086.d: Gadget made this cape in the hope that it might enable him to fly and thus more easily escape the beatings administered daily by his wife.

11087.d: Worn by several generations of handymen, this ring will protect your knuckle from hammer blows. Unfortunately, it is never sold in packs of five.

11088.d: Grillian was a great magician. He is most famous for having reinvented Scamper powder, having forgotten how to manufacture it.

11089.d: This cape is supposed to protect your posterior from carnivorous plant bites.

11090.d: This is a wanted notice for Lethaline Sigibul.

11091.d: Grillian the magician traded a magic ring for this pair of boots. It seems that he lost out on the deal, as they aren't even padded.

11092.d: Grillian wore this amulet around his neck when... When... Oh, what does it matter? He died and now this amulet is yours.

11102.d: Hardened to Frigost's harsh climate, this flower is much more resistant than its delicate aspect would suggest. That said, to preserve the alchemic properties of such a rare plant, it must be handled carefully when harvested.

11103.d: This enormous bag contains an impressive quantity of Snowdrops.

11104.d: Beyond the realms of the Tofu, the Gobball and even the Iop, there is a creature dwelling in a dimension of idiocy unimaginable even to your cretinous mind: the Quaquack!

11105.d: This Quaquack hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11106.d: Spines as sharp as Bworker's blades, scales as thick as the bark of a Soft Oak, and eyes as black as the feathers of a Crow. This fish may be formidable, but served up on a plate it is quite simply delicious.

11107.d: This tree appears to tremble when you touch it. After all the axe blows you've dealt it, it's not surprising it's scared of you.

11109.d: Not only is this surprising cereal resistant to Frigost's extreme climate, it lends a delicate taste of chocolate to any milk into which it is dipped.

11110.d: Hard enough to scratch glass and dark enough to sap your morale, this rock has lost all of the heat of the lava from which it came. It would be perfect as a tombstone, as long as it isn't yours.

11111.d: This enormous bag contains an impressive quantity of Icefish.

11112.d: This enormous bag contains an impressive quantity of Aspen.

11113.d: This enormous bag contains an impressive quantity of Frosteez.

11114.d: This enormous bag contains an impressive quantity of Obsidian.

11115.d: Spring is here, you can smell it. Well, it's either Spring or the rotten Uridnac that's attached to you.

11116.d:
This little fish is very fond of people and attaches itself to them easily. 
However, its biological rhythm is peculiar: it is only active in the month of Aperirel when Silouate warms the fresh water where the fish thrives.

11117.d: Mastogobs need to be shorn once a year, just like the armpits of Pikokos.

11118.d: There isn't the tiniest piece of edible meat left on this bone, so there's no point you gnawing on it.

11119.d: Frigostians normally eat these ears with vinaigrette, as they taste awful, and Frigostians love vinaigrette.

11120.d: They say that if you boil this leather 8 times in water, it becomes edible. That's a Frigostian's idea of a funny joke, by the way.

11121.d: This eye must have seen the rumps of a fair few female Mastogobs in its time. Now all the poor thing can see is the fluff in your pocket.

11122.d: The most reckless Frigostians play a game with Mastogob Warriors while they are sleeping by attempting to throw three metallic rings around each of their horns without waking them up. Unsurprisingly, no one has ever made it to the end of the game alive.

11123.d: You pulled this tooth from the jaw of a still-living Mastogob. What's wrong with you? Are you crazy, or something?

11124.d: These entrails froze as soon as you pulled them from their body cavity.

11125.d: As if it wasn't already bad enough that he has no arms, what's going to happen to the Pingwin whose foot you tore off?

11126.d: How can a skull be ethereal? Having thought about it a lot, you find yourself laughing at the answer to that question.

11127.d: This tear symbolises resilience in the face of oppression.

11128.d: Instead of wetting, this tear burns any combustible material with which it comes into contact, so there's no risk of your makeup running when your boyfriend leaves you for his Dragoturkey.

11129.d: Extract of Snowfoux musk is enormously popular with the female Snowfoux population, and makes a great gift for your suitors or rivals.

11130.d: This lump of lichen was frozen solid by the cold. Once defrosted, you can use it in a Frigostian variant of Black Pudding Pizza.

11131.d: You'd have to be a real dork not to understand how useful an object like this is.

11132.d: Because you stole his spoon, that poor bear has to use his fingers to eat. You're a monster.

11133.d: Following the example set by the Royal Tofu, certain Pingwins grow a vibrating feather that is chock-full of magic. As for its usefulness...

11134.d: There's something trapped in this cube of ice cut from Frigost's Frozen Lake. You've got two options if you want to find out what it is: wait until the ice melts, or, like any self-respecting brat, hit it until it shatters.

11135.d: This hairy little tail was well hidden under the Venerable Mastogob's thick wool. That didn't stop you from finding it and pulling it off, though, did it?

11136.d: It's dirty, but venerable. Kinda reminds you of someone.

11137.d: This is all that's left of the Stunted Rats from Grandfather's cellar. You certainly didn't pull any punches, did you?
11137.n: A lump of Faded Stunted Rat

11138.d: Nope, that's not a Mastogob Brain you're holding in your hand, it's a Pea Seed. The difference is obvious: the Pea Seed is cold to the touch.

11139.d: Emmer is an ancient version of the wheat that is currently cultivated in Amakna. Anyone would think time stands still on Frigost.

11140.d: Once used as flour for biscuits, the cultivation of this seed was banned following a stupid bet. The former mayor of Frigost bet an Ecaflip that he would only eat one cookie made from Granola Flour. He lost the bet, and his fortune.

11141.d: This tiny seed comes from a mature Pynekone.

11142.d: Placing a Lentil Seed on each of your eyelids won't make you see better, but you'll certainly look more stupid than usual if anyone sees you doing it.

11143.d: Sparo wasn't worth his salt, and that's why he ended up in a barrel. Don't say you weren't warned.

11144.d: Pull the stalk out, count to two and throw this seed as far as you can. If it lands next to an Atomystique he'll explode with rage. Young militiamen finish their Grenhayde Seed training pretty quickly.

11145.d: Slum-dwelling children attack civilised people with these seeds. You may be wondering how that works, but it's better not to know, really.

11146.d: This seed has undergone a massive increase in temperature followed by extreme cooling, which has made it brittle and fragile.

11147.d: This seed has a high carbon content and when there's a full moon, it makes a strange noise. You'd have to be really stupid or a Iop to believe such nonsense.

11148.d: An old legend tells that the flour made from this seed was used for making the bread of Demon Steak sandwiches, favourite dish of the demon lord Rushu. Even today, Frigostians are wary of it.

11149.d: If you like piling on the slap, and singing in the shower, this seed is for you. Eating it will have you wiggling your hips in front of a roaring crowd. Be careful, however, as its effect is very temporary.

11156.d: This flower was popularised by the town crier Jorg Farmboy, all the other town criers hate him for it.

11157.d: Powdered and boiled, ingesting this tulip is recommended if you want to lose weight quickly. The disadvantage is that the weight of your wallet diminishes just as quickly.

11158.d: Discovered by the famous botanist Yosef, this rose gives off the heady scent of sweaty Frighog dung, and reminds you of your most intimate moments.

11159.d: This flower casts a shadow in the shape of an Osamodas.

11160.d: The stems of this flavoursome rhubarb are hollow, and once appropriately arranged, produce a sound when blown into that's not unlike unaccompanied vocal music characterized by consonant four-part chords for every melody note in a predominantly homophonic texture. Or so the story goes, anyway.

11161.d: The person who discovered this exquisite flower quickly went around proclaiming it to be the most beautiful ever discovered, and I, for one, wholeheartedly agree.

11162.d: A Xelor Lord of Time discovered this beautiful flower, but was tearfully forced to part with it.

11163.d: They say that this rose is blessed by the gods, something that they don't say about you.

11164.d: The petals of this hellebore smell like dry-roasted peanuts.

11165.d: There was a time when chewing this flower was fashionable amongst Iop high society. They thought it made them look smart, which might have been true, if Iops were capable of thinking.

11166.d: The name of this flower is a tribute to Sander, the famous admiral of the Frigost fleet, who died hitting his head against the walls of the house of his rival, Al Hiartus.

11167.d: The pollen of this lily has the peculiar property of bringing some people out in a terrible rash, or invoking a euphoric sense of happiness in others.

11174.d: Use this key to enter the greenhouse where the Royal Mastogob hides.

11175.d: The key contains high levels of asbestos and as a result floats very well on water and on salad dressing. You can also use it to enter the Pingwin Dungeon.

11182.d: One thing's for sure, without his wig, the Royal Mastogob certainly loses some of his authority...

11183.d: The Royal Pingwin himself used this Icefish against you. Wherever it came from, however, it will just end up on the barbeque like any other Icefish.

11190.d:
If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. For once, the gods might not have been pulling your leg.
Please note, this gift can only be opened on a DOFUS 2.0 server.

11191.d: Their soles may be worn but these boots are very comfortable. They have trampled the soil of the most dangerous dungeons as well as the heads of the most vicious monsters.

11192.d:
If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. For once, the gods might not have been pulling your leg. 
Please note, this gift can only be opened on a DOFUS 2.0 server.
11192.n: Gift: Legend of the Dungeons Boots

11193.d: A Handyman could use this plank to make something delightful - a coffin, for example. Just bear that in mind.

11194.d: This flour dissolves in mimilk, giving it a delightful chocolate flavour. The inhabitants of a lost island, preferring frozen desserts, like to dissolve it in water.

11195.d: You need find some treatment before you get any worse.

11196.d: Unable to strike new currency because of a lack of metal, Frigostians carve Kamas from the ice and trade them for various local objects. This coin has no value outside of the island.

11197.d: The vaccination campaign against this disease has already cost the town of Frigost the modest sum of 2 billion Kamas and has had no significant result. The Frigostians may as well just throw their Kamas out of the window.

11198.d: This vaccine provides effective protection from the Lurgi, but its effects wear off quickly. It needs to be renewed every week.

11199.d: This seed, cold to the touch, releases a powerful chocolate aroma.

11200.d: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. For once, the gods might not have been pulling your leg.

11201.d: You took this sample from a Mastogob suffering from a heavy cold.

11202.d: Herr Peece needs this water for his research into a cure for the common cold.

11203.d: This weed is well sought by alchemists, Eniripsas and Eniripsa alchemists. A plant similar to this one can be used to make a powerful liqueur popular with sailors, Enutrofs and Enutrof sailors.

11204.d: You went to great lengths to get this blood sample. Let's hope it was worth it.

11205.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 1am but before 4am.

11206.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 4am but before 7am.

11207.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 7am but before 10am.

11208.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 10am but before 1pm.

11209.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 1pm but before 4pm.

11210.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 4pm but before 7pm.

11211.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 7pm but before 10pm.

11212.d: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 10pm but before 1am.

11213.d: More resistant than a pair of Captain Chafer's Kriptonite Underpants, and more aggressive than a band of Astrubian Hunters, these ticks are a veritable nightmare for their host.

11214.d: This blood sample was taken from a Mastogob infected with ticks.

11215.d: This blood sample was taken from a Mastogob Warrior infected with ticks.

11216.d: This blood sample was taken from a Venerable Mastogob infected with ticks.

11217.d: This blood sample was taken from a Mastogobbly infected with ticks.

11218.d: Wogew the Hewmit has asked you to deliver this envelope to Otomai. It contains several useful documents on the ticks that live on Mastogobs, but also on Wabbits.

11219.d: The Royal Mastogob uses his tail to shoo away Moskitoes during the summer months. It's neither use nor ornament the rest of the year, and sometimes he even forgets it's there.

11221.d: No one knows for sure exactly when the Mastogobs arrived on Frigost. What is for sure is that they've been there a long time, because certain Frigostian households still pass down Mastogob Wool underwear from generation to generation, and there are several examples dating back centuries.

11222.d: When it's not planted firmly in the jaw of the Pingwinkle, this beak can be found planted firmly in your backside.

11223.d: In olden times, Pingwinkles only used to visit Frigost's shores for a few days during the winter, but now the island has frozen over completely, they've decided to stay - which is as good an excuse as any to steal their feathers all year round.

11224.d: Frigostians have often wondered what purpose these ridiculous wings could serve. After all, a Pingwobble could never possibly hope to take off.

11225.d: It's very oily, isn't washed very often, and it shines. Nope, I'm not talking about your wig, but this Pingwobble Skin.

11226.d: This oil was extracted from a Mama Pingwin. It will take you a very long time to wipe the memory of how exactly you extracted it from your scarred mind.

11227.d: Everyone on Frigost loves to stuff their underwear with Mama Pingwin down. Some people say they do it to keep warm, but only a Iop would believe that.

11228.d: There are plenty of questions about Frigost that don't have answers, and, more worryingly, plenty of answers that don't have questions. You will never know where the Shaman Pingwin found this giant fishbone.

11229.d: The Shaman Pingwin's Beard smells of fish and goat musk.  This potent mix is used by the bravest inhabitants of Frigost as a Mastogob repellent.

11230.d: Don't be fooled by its modest size, it knows exactly where it's going.

11231.d: Usually hidden by a decaying fish, the ears of the Kung-Fu Pingwin hear one thing, the calls of available partners during mating season. So you're free to make fun of Kung-Fu Pingwins in perfectly safety as long as you don't look like a potential partner.

11232.d: The Royal Pingwin is well respected by the inhabitants of Frigost, who, blinded by his noble title, think he's probably more important than he actually is, and don't hesitate to kill him as a result.

11233.d: Don't pretend you don't know exactly which hole this enormous egg came out of.

11234.d: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11235.d: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11236.d: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11237.d: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11238.d: Skrats use their tails to balance when they're rolling their acorns along the floor. Skrats seem impervious to ridicule.

11239.d: Skrats spend the first few years of their lives looking for the best acorn possible. They spend the rest of their lives trying to remember why they've hidden it.

11240.d: A very serious, progressive scientific study has shown that the teeth of the Sabredon were the very first cause of perforated buttock amongst the Frigostian population.

11241.d: Sabredon Hairs were once used to stuff quilts - which certain Frigostians of dubious personal hygiene could then use as an excuse to mask their polecat stench.

11242.d: This tusk smells like someone's underpants. Not yours, though.

11243.d: A Glacial Boar's skin pads its angular bones quite nicely, meaning it stays festively plump all year round.

11244.d:
I followed a hoary Mama Pingwin and she led me to her den, where hundreds of other Mama Pingwins were hiding. It's an opportunity  not to be missed. I'm going to head inside and shoot anything that moves, there'll be enough meat for the next decade.
Gerard.

11245.d: Unlike those of the Moowolf, these family jewels have neither value nor purpose.

11246.d: Just before shuffling off this mortal coil and joining the sanctuary of Frighogs killed in action, the one you killed gave you a last look of such ferocity that your blood ran cold. As if it wasn't cold enough already on Frigost...

11247.d: A Frighog's ears are pierced all over. Is this because they like piercings, or is it because you can even hear Jon Lemon's songs on Frigost too?

11248.d: This ear reminds you of one of the favourite songs of young Frigostians: "Kanigloo gloo gloo, Greedoblop blop blop tadada tzum tzum". There aren't many lyrics, sure, but that way a Iop can just about memorise it.

11249.d: This fabric reminds you of the second verse of one of the favourite songs of young Frigostians: "Frighog hog hog...". Unfortunately, you don't remember the rest of the words.

11250.d: While they were still alive, the Mayor of Frigost's political opponents would tell anyone who would listen that she wore Wooly Bow Meow Hair lingerie.

11251.d: No one knows for certain what exactly this sternum is used for.

11252.d: Young Frigostian schoolchildren have a game called "BowMeouch" which involves cutting a paw off a Stunted Rat and using it to simulate footprints in the snow. They attract Snow Bow Meows in search of prey to ambush. Once the Snow Bow Meow is caught, they shave its fur off and turn it into a muffle. Aren't children wonderful?

11253.d: Before Frigost froze over, Stunted Rats were hunted for their fur, which was then sold on the Amaknean continent under the name "Exotic Kitsou Skin".

11254.d: Crabeyes are hunted by the fishermen of Frigost for two reasons: their permanent bad temper and their tendency to play jokes on the fishermen by snipping their nets with their pincers. The fishermen get their revenge, and play jokes on the crabs by snipping their pincers off.

11255.d: The eye contains a vitreous fluid that is used in traditional Frigostian recipes, when it replaces vinegar - but only if you let the eye ferment for long enough.

11256.d: Gullipops are rather stupid, badly behaved creatures, whose guano lies scattered in stinking piles around the port of Frigost. They like to steal fish from fishermen, but once well-trained, they are able to "liberate" the personal effects of distracted tourists and hide them in their beaks.

11257.d: Frigostian schoolchildren use these feathers to write with, which is why mother Gullipops always stress the need to accelerate when passing a school to their chicks.

11258.d: The date the pines were received is marked on this receipt. Show it to Gormor the Mangler to receive your pay.

11259.d: Chief Anbifketf needs these trunks for the pipework heating system.

11260.d: This thick and sticky blubber makes an excellent fuel that burns for a long, long time - which explains why Pengwins never feel the cold.

11261.d: This list shows the missing pieces the fishermen of the Frozen Lake need to repair their equipment.

11262.d: Damar gave this ring to Valy Domidat thirty years ago.

11263.d: This fairywork produces a pleasant pyrotechnic effect for a few seconds and burns your retinas for the rest of your life.

11264.d: This Pingwin skin is in very poor condition. You won't be able to use it to make new underwear for Captain Chafer Day.

11265.d: This Pingwobble has been trained to be able to regurgitate enormous quantities of Icefish and leave them intact. The only problem is, its digestive process starts after half an hour.

11266.d: While you were fighting, your Pingwobble was eaten. This is all that's left of him.

11267.d: This discount will be apply when you rent a room in the upcoming ice hotel.

11268.d:
This old plush has to belong to someone, but who?
Double-click to use.

11269.d: The gum is of no use to you because your breath is too bad. On the other hand, Mac Gayver, the Xelor, will find a surprising use for it.

11270.d:
This chest contains many heirlooms. In the absence of anyone else, you might be able to claim a reward from its owner.
Double-click to use.

11271.d:
This sealed book is in poor condition. Forcing it open to read its contents may make it unusable. You'd better hire a professional, but which one?
Double-click to use.

11277.d: This Pingwinkle doesn't like being adopted and will and flee at the first opportunity. In the meantime, you can show it to your friends for them to abuse.

11278.d: You have defeated a Skrat but unfortunately it has decided to follow you everywhere. Now you have the opportunity to find out if its bad luck is a legend or not.

11279.d: This saw is used to cut blocks of ice. It will also cut frozen limbs particularly well.

11280.d: Steel plates are very popular among Frigostians, who use them to manufacture machinery and steel pipes.

11281.d: This mask is used by workers to protect their faces in hazardous working conditions. It also protects very well from slaps and thrown dishes if you have forgotten your wife's birthday.

11282.d: These gloves protect objects from your grubby little mitts. Certain Srams use them to protect their identity by hiding their fingerprints.

11283.d:
A Sword Smith can create this saw from:
- 2 x Glacial Boar Leather.
- 1 x Mama Pingwin Oil.
- 2 x Gullipop Feather.
- 1 x Pingwinkle Beak.
- 1 x Kriptonite.
- 1 x Aspen Wood.
- 5 x Mastogob Wool.
- 10 x  Whetstone

11284.d:
A Miner can melt this plate from:
- 5 x Coal.
- 25 x Iron.
- 10 x Tin.
- 10 x Manganese.
- 5 x Cobalt.
- 1 x Aluminite.
- 1 x Sulphur Pouch.
- 1 x Mother of Pearl.

11285.d:
A Tailor can make this hat from:
- 5 x Mama Pingwin Down
- 5 x Venerable Mastogob Wool
- 2 x Kanigloo Ear.
- 2 x Glacial Boar Leather.
- 2 x Pingwinkle Beak.
- 1 x Coal.
- 5 x Iron.
- 5 x Tin.

11286.d:
A Jeweller can make this ring from:
- 4 x Pingwinkle Feather.
- 2 x Pingwobble Wing.
- 10 x Shaman Pingwin Beard Hair
- 10 x Sabredon Hair.
- 2 x Skrat Tail.
- 4 x Mastogobbly Leather.
- 2 x Crabeye Pincer.
- 10 x Woolly Bow Meow Hair.

11287.d: You must escort him to Mac Gayver.

This plan shows how to cobble together a prototype Drinking Trough from:
- 1 x Charm Drinking Trough.
- 2 x Kung Fu Pingwin Ear.
- 10 x Mama Pingwin Down.
- 2 x Kanigloo Fabric.
- 10 x Glacial Boar Leather.
- 2 x Crabeye Eye.
- 10 x Stunted Rat Fabric.
- 2 x Frighog Baleful Eye.

- 10 x Frighog Pierced Ear.
- 2 x Gullipop Beak.
- 10 x Crabeye Claw.
- 10 x Sabredon Hair.

- 10 x Pingwinkle Feather.

- 10 x Kanigloo Ear.
- 2 x Woolly Bow Meow Sternum.

This plan shows how to cobble together a prototype Slapper from:
- 1 x Charm Slapper.
- 2 x Pingwobble Wing.
- 10 x Kung Fu Pingwin Tail.
- 2 x Sabredon Tooth.
- 10 x Skrat Tail.
- 2 x Stunted Rat Paw.
- 10 x Woolly Bow Meow Hair.

11292.d: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11293.d: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11294.d: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11296.d: Here's a dose of vaccine against the Lurgi.

11297.d:
Germain, if you're reading this letter, it means I am dead. You're probably looking for my booty, so I want you to know that I will never tell you where it is hidden. 
Cheers!

11299.d: Mister Penguin is now under your control. Take him to the village Militia at your leisure.

11301.d: Pirate Bhey is now under your control. Take him to the village Militia at your leisure.

11302.d: The Masked Avenger is now under your control. Take him to the village Militia at your leisure.

11303.d: The YeCh'Ti is now under your control. Take it to the village Militia at your leisure.

11306.d: Engraved on its handle you can read: "This sword steals the life of the poor and redistributes it to the rich." Too bad you're poor.

11307.d: Az le Tech wanted to trade this treasure for his freedom with the Enutrof conqueror Sétroc. Once in his possession, Sétroc did not keep his word and executed Az le Tech. As he lay dying, he cast a curse that will befall anyone who lays their hands on this treasure.

11308.d: You have stolen some of Az le Tech's treasure. Look what happens to greedy people.

11309.d: Very handy for pinching the buttocks of its enemies or grabbing pickles stuck to the bottom of the jar, this claw is a Talklyka Pirate's pride and joy.

11310.d: It's difficult to say what purpose this rope could serve for a Talklyka Pirate, because everyone knows they haven't got a clue how to tie knots.

11311.d: Some pirates can't swim and so they need a buoy. They may eventually beach on the black sand beaches of the Cradle of Alma after floating around for several years. Once they've back on terra firma, they're generally thirsty for revenge. But since they can't take revenge on the sea, they take revenge on the weak, as well as tourists, or just simply weak tourists.

11312.d: It's difficult to call this a tail, it's more of a Karrybean Pirate extremity.

11313.d: Yuara Pirates always keep a little oil with them to ensure that their wheel rotates correctly, but end up drinking it in a misguided attempt to stop their heads rotating instead.

11314.d: This shell protected the Yuara Pirate from sea spray and guano while it was sailing. Now it's beached, it uses it to protect its delicate pupils from the black sandstorms of the Cradle of Alma.

11315.d: Ignorant people might think this is a Spinnaker pole or a bowsprit, while any Frigostian tell you that this is a vertical spar and therefore a mast.

11316.d: Even the best Frigostian research scientists have failed to explain the usefulness of teeth for a ghost, especially a ghost tied to a mast. Perhaps it uses them to gnaw at the ropes?

11317.d: This shell was stolen from a powerless mollusc by a Harpy Pirate. It hasn't made the Harpy Pirate any more powerful so far.

11318.d: This shell belongs to what appears to be a former Frigostian-turned-pirate who was transformed into a ghost when he swallowed too much water while swimming. That's what happens when you have too much salt in your diet!

11319.d: If you turn this fabric over, you'll find some invaluable advice: "If you see an enemy, rob him of his treasure, hide it on a desert island and put a cross on a map so you can remember its location. Remember not to hide the map with the treasure".

11320.d: Vigi Pirates are selected for their excellent visual capacity. They are able to discern a school of tuna during a storm at night with an octopus covering their eyes, guano on their eyelids and the songs of Jon Lemon playing in the background.

11321.d: Also known as "Buck Lightyear", "Buck Aroo", "Buck Adoaboutnothing" or "Buck Off", this pirate has sailed every sea known to man and beast. The tides have decided that he should end his days on the black sand beaches of the Cradle of Alma.

11322.d: Broken twice by cannon balls, three times from rolling in the sea spray, and four times having slipped on dried guano, this bone made a wealthy man of the ship's doctor, until he was finally thrown to the sharks for dark tales of gambling, women, alcohol, insubordination, provocations to a duel, treasure theft, scuttling and mutiny. A succession of little things which eventually led to his downfall. You do not mess with Buck Anear.

11323.d: This stone was levitating around an Atomystique until you tried to avoid it, or levitate yourself - you don't know exactly what happened, but now you've got a headache and you're covered in steaming mud.

11324.d: This piece of lava was ejected at high speed from an unexpected orifice of an Atomystique that you desperately tried to finish off with a blows from a rusty rake. You were lucky not to be in its way when it went crashing into the arse of a local tourist.

11325.d: How can a vaporous creature give rise to solid waste? This question was first asked 74 years ago during the famous Frigostian contest for the Promotion of Young Graduate Geologists. No participant was admitted that year and the issue still remains one of the Island of Frigost's most terrifying mysteries.

11326.d: This steaming bone changes shape according to the mood of the Solfatare - a beast renowned for its terribly foul moods.

11327.d: This stone heart fills with steam when the Steam Crackler meets a partner. This peculiarity allows you to quickly determine if you've killed a single Steam Crackler, you just need to see if its heart floats.

11328.d: Steam Cracklers are comparable to Cracklers made from steam that have decided to do battle with anything that does not resemble them in any way, or that they can just about make out through the steam. Surprisingly, they lays eggs filled with steam.

11329.d: The Fumaroller was waving this huge stone at the end of what appeared to be its tail. He had hoped to intimidate you, until you found his weak point. Unfortunately you failed to memorise it, as your head is full of cotton wool.

11330.d: This vaporous artefact smells like rotten eggs mixed with guanocamole. The mere mention of this mixture makes you hungry.

11331.d: The mofette takes its name directly from a geological feature that is quite common in the Tears of Ouronigride. This stone resembles one of its organs, a kidney perhaps.

11332.d: Behind this strange name hides a rock with a vascular structure. But you can just be happy likening it to a piece of the giant mofette you just savagely cut in two.

11333.d: Even the Magmarmition itself thinks this is junk. Just don't put it in your pockets, especially those that aren't fireproof.

11334.d: This vertebra contains bone marrow that has already been cooked and is ready to be consumed. What you are holding in your hands is the precursor to an entire line of microwave ready meals.

11335.d: After having taken blows from it several times to your face, you finally have the right to keep it in your bag as a lucky charm.

11336.d: We don't know how the Snowfouxes arrived on Frigost, but we know that their distant cousins come from Pandala. This information helps you to better understand the origins of the frozen Pandrista residue you slept in last night.

11337.d: This leather is thick enough to allow the Soryo Snowfoux to withstand low, low temperatures and go sledging on his arse without hurting himself, which makes you particularly jealous.

11338.d: Long used for stuffing the underwear of complex-ridden Frigostians, this wool is now known to give spots to anyone who strokes it. You have now found an excellent excuse to justify your pestilent pimples.

11339.d: It's difficult to find anything more stupid than the offspring of a Yokai Snowfoux, yet some parents seem to have succeeded... You're looking for a link with this Snowfoux Wool, but you can't see any, even squinting and shaking your fists.

11340.d: The braincase of the Yokai Snowfoux has just about enough room to hold an evaporated snowflake. But as stupidity is frightening, all Frigostians are terrorised by this creature, even though it's barely able to put one paw in front of the other.

11341.d: Ripped straight from the body of the Tengu Snowfoux, this wool is particularly warm, and will strengthen your virility if your chest wig is a little sparse.

11342.d: The completely waterproof leather was used by Frigostians to craft supple, smooth, soft containers to put things in. Some of them even claimed they didn't need to use the containers, as they were happily married.

11367.d: This syringe contains a single dose of vaccine against the Lurgi, tested and certified by Rose Line.

11368.d: This Mama Pingwin follows you because she has no choice, but she will flee at the first opportunity.

11369.d: This seed has been entrusted to you by Panoramist to repopulate the Lonesome Pine Trails.

11370.d: This drink is very sweet and has the distinction of being made from frozen grapes. This explains its rarity and its unique, refined taste.

11371.d: Also known as the "Mastogob grass drink", Frigrowka is said to facilitate human contact and address difficult issues. As for Frigostians, they drink it mostly because they like to drink.

11372.d: This cape is long enough for you to be able to afford to leave blank lines between each cribbed note you've made before you take that all-important, life-changing exam.

11373.d: The tailor who made this hat had to use 12 powerful characteristic scrolls to craft it. Or possibly 12 sheets of toilet paper.

11374.d: There's enough room for one of your friends to write your name on this paper amulet, which is just what breeders do so they know which Gobballs belong to them.

11375.d: This strong and rigid undergarment is not very comfortable, but then it was made with paper mache, after all. Having the saliva of a stranger on your buttocks does not seem to bother you in the slightest, I notice.

11376.d: This huge feather cape accentuates your figure.

11377.d: In some tribes, the wisdom of the Chief is measured by the number of feathers on his hat. Yours has only one, and what's more, it is very small, and quite grubby.

11378.d: Lighter than conventional sandals, they have only one real drawback, they don't suit ticklish people at all.

11379.d: This amulet will tickle your neck and make you cough up that frog in your throat.

11380.d: This wounded hunter needs Herr Peece' medical expertise. At the slightest hint of a fight, he'll take refuge where you found him.

11381.d: This request was prepared by Djauns for a harness for Snow Bow Wows. Before signing it, he reminded you to hurry because time is running out.

11382.d: The last person who tried to use this cape to fly down from a cloud crashed into a bank.

11383.d: This hat isn't waterproof, and as a result, you'll have to use a ridiculous umbrella wherever you go.

11384.d: Hook this ring around the neck of any children in your charge, and then connect the ring to a rope that you've hung from a tree. Now you can enjoy yourself and the children can't escape.

11385.d: Collecting this fur without damaging it was no mean feat when you take into account how badly you fought its former owner.

11386.d: These boots are perfect for dishing out punishment with your feet so that you don't have to get your hands dirty. The children will adore you!

11387.d: You must escort him to Larry Tutthe so he can become his new assistant.

11388.d: This crate contains everything that Larry Tutthe needs.

11389.d: You collected this water from the Tears of Ouronigride for Ogivol Victor.

11391.d: This creature is developing right before your eyes! You'd better hurry up or it'll get so big you won't be able to carry it any more.

11392.d: You proudly fought the Snowfoux. Their remains are proof of your victory.

11393.d: The striped cape belonged to a prisoner famous for his dilemma.

11394.d: This striped hat is big enough to hide a ball and chain. But not necessarily the one you have hanging around your foot.

11395.d: This small chain could pass for an amulet if wasn't the tip of a padlock.

11396.d: The man who gave this belt such a stupid name is actively sought by the police, the years he'll spend in prison when the catch him still won't make up for such a lack of creativity.

11397.d: This cloak with a ridiculous name is intriguing nonetheless, and belonged to a righteous man who claimed he wanted to clean up the streets of Brakmar. Nobody knows if he was a vigilante or a dustman.

11398.d: This hat will give you the allure of a Borbat. You're single at the moment, right? Yeah, you're going to stay single for quite a while.

11399.d: This book's spine reads: "A book for upholders of the law who doesn't afraid of anything". And you thought you could use it...

11400.d: The shoemaker who designed these boots fitted them with Borbat wings so that their wearer could fly. Well, it was difficult to hear anything above the obnoxious din, but that's what you thought you the merchant was saying when you bought them from him at the Astrub Zaap.

11401.d: This wooden cape grows larger when you lie. There's a good chance you'll trip over it regularly as a result.

11402.d: You can also use this hat as traffic cone should you have an accident while riding your Dragoturkey.

11403.d: Transforming into a ghost pirate didn't really suit you, you're definitely not a sailor. You'll feel better in 24 hours, I'm sure.

11404.d: You've been turned into a ghost so that you can enter the Rebellious Spirit's wreck.

11406.d: Only educated people know the usefulness of this serum, which is why you haven't got a clue what it does.

11407.d: If you serve your drinks "on the rocks" using this special ice cube, they're sure to have an unrivalled flavour and freshness.

11408.d: Do you swear to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth?

11409.d: This purse contains enough Kamas to help you buy a decent outfit. Given the difficulty of the job, it represents a fortune. You can't use it for anything else, sadly.

11410.d: Worn to Captain Chafer's Panty Party, this outfit will cause envy amongst men, and especially amongst women eager to taste the forbidden fruit.

11411.d: Worn to Captain Chafer's Panty Party, this dress will turn your suitors' heads and cause many a stiff neck. Your local physiotherapist will thank you.

11412.d:
These documents are a copy of the inheritance, property deeds and other paperwork belonging to the Santho family. They show, among other things, the purchase and the legacy of hundreds of acres of farmland south of Bonta. The purchases are spread between the years 551 and 555, just after the glaciation of Frigost. They were made possible by the immense wealth of Edmond Santho, who made his fortune by selling huge quantities of cereals of Frigostian origin.
Currently, only one field does not belong to Raymond Santho: that of Robin Marmoni.
11412.n: A copy of the Santho family dossier

11413.d: The key to Heike Holo's cell.

11414.d: Heike Holo wants to escape, you must escort her to the boat bound for Wabbit Island.

11415.d: These documents concern the theft of cereals coming from Frigost. The Montay family's boats are mentioned.

11416.d: This pair of boots was carved out of a tree trunk. Unless it's the opposite.

11417.d: This ring was made from sawdust and something very sticky, and it's better that you leave it at that.

11418.d: Jon Lemon loved this cape to death, which explains why he wears it to each of his funerals.

11419.d: Jon Lemon always put on these boots when he had a deposit to make... in the hut at the bottom of his garden.

11420.d: This old hat is bordering on the ridiculous, and it's how Jon Lemon earned the nickname "The Moustachioed Grandmother". That name tends to put him in a bad mood...

11421.d: Jon Lemon should never have used this blowpipe just after eating. Since that day he's had to use it as a simple staff and as he so often repeats, "It was better before".

11461.d: This Atomystique, who is looking at you in a very strange way, is determined to follow you everywhere.

11462.d: A rose by any other name would smell as sweet.

11463.d: This rose was the muse of the king of villains, who smiled at life.

11464.d: Mack Gotjooze is afraid to travel alone and will run away if things go awry.
